homer.title: Study reader: Greek is missing a line in Books X, XVI and XXIII, so ~818 lines carry wrong line numbers and the word data of the neighbouring line
homer.detail: build_study_data.py indexes treebank words by the line's position in greek.json (enumerate(b['lines'], 1)), and the template prints that position as the line number. The Perseus Greek omits the lines that Murray brackets. The canonical numbering keeps them (e.g. 16.101 ἔλθοι ἀλητεύων…), and so do the treebank cites and the Murray English range labels. As a result, from X.459, XVI.101 and XXIII.49 to the end of each book, every Greek line (1) shows a number one lower than its canonical number, which is the number the English range labels and the popover's 'Od. b.l' citation use, and (2) is paired with the treebank words of the previous line. The fuzzy prefix matcher then wraps only a few tokens, and often the wrong ones. The tap-any-word feature (the page's main purpose) is essentially dead in XVI and XXIII, and misleading where it does fire. Smaller local shifts caused by treebank line merges hit about 24 more lines (I.96-98, I.260-270, III.304-308, IV.76-78, XIV.63-64).
homer.evidence: Line counts: X 573 vs canonical 574, XVI 480 vs 481, XXIII 371 vs 372. The per-line treebank/token match falls below 50% for 114 lines of X (from 460), 379 of XVI (from 102) and 320 of XXIII (from 50); every other book has 0–14. Rendered DOM: tappable tokens are 15% in XVI (753/4865) and 13% in XXIII (347/2683), against 87–91% in every other book (X: 73%). Popovers observed: XVI line labelled 105, tap 'μεγάροισι' → form 'με', lemma ἐγώ 'I'. Line 107, tap 'τε' → 'τεθνάμεν', θνήσκω 'to die'. XXIII.47, tap 'κείατʼ' → 'κε', ἄν 'modal particle'. X.470, XVI.190 and XXIII.183 (the bed test) have no tappable words at all. study.json: text line X.459 'ἀλλʼ ἄγετʼ ἐσθίετε…' is paired with the treebank words from line 460.
homer.repro: Open /homer-odyssey/study.html#bk-16, scroll to the line labelled 105 and tap 'μεγάροισι'. The popover shows 'με · ἐγώ · I (first person pronoun)'. Most words from line 102 onward do not respond to taps.
homer.fix: Keep canonical line numbers: extract the `n` attribute of each <l> into greek.json/greek.md, or at least record the gaps. Key words_by_line and the displayed line number by that n, not by position, and render bracketed or absent lines as gaps. Add a build assertion that each book's line count matches the canonical count and that the per-line treebank match rate stays above a threshold.
verifier_corrections: The XXIII.47 example ('κείατʼ' → 'κε', ἄν) is not caused by the line shift. Line 47 comes before the gap at 49, and its treebank words are the right ones. The wrong match comes from a separate matcher bug in study-template.html:336-341: the text marks elision with U+02BC 'ʼ' but the treebank uses combining U+0313, so elided tokens never match exactly, and the prefix test binds them to a later short word such as 'κε'. That affects elided words in every book: about 229 elided tokens are wrapped to the wrong treebank word. The template's word-matching lines are 335-343, and the render loop is 330-331. 'Every other book has 0–14' low-match lines is slightly off: Book IX has about 17 (a treebank gap at 520-531) and I has about 16. The last line of every book also has no word data. These are separate, smaller issues.

Two wording fixes. First, the popover citation does NOT use the canonical number. It prints 'Od. ' + bn + '.' + ln with the same positional ln (study-template.html:370), so the citation is wrong along with the gutter number. Only the Murray English range labels are canonical. Second, in Book X the Greek text and treebank agree through position 458, and the treebank itself has no cite 10.459. The pairing breaks from X.459, but where X's missing canonical line sits (possibly 10.456 διογενὲς Λαερτιάδη) is not established. The claim that 'from X.459 each number is one lower than canonical' is unverified for X, though the word-data shift is certain. Also, the template's matcher is on line 339, not in the range 336-341.

The builder line refs (142-143) are correct. The template's prefix match (data/study-template.html ~line 339) is what turns the misalignment into wrong morphology on non-function words, e.g. μεγάροισι shown as με/ἐγώ. Related but separate defects in the same data: (a) Book XVI has a Murray milestone typo, chunk [275,579] then [580,284]. In study.html Book XVI, Greek lines 285-480 therefore render twice (196 duplicated line numbers in the DOM), and the English for 275-279 appears only after line 480. (b) Small local treebank cite drifts at I.95-98, I.259-269, III.304-308 and IV.76-78 cause short misalignment runs of a different origin.

Minor precision: the first misaligned text line is array line 459/101/49 (it shows no words); from 460/102/50 on it shows the previous line's words. The treebank also has no entry for the omitted number, which supports the finding's cause (an edition omission whose numbering was lost in greek.json).

homer.title: Study reader Book XVI prints Greek lines 275–480 twice; Book VI has an empty '320–319' chunk
homer.detail: The Murray English is chunked at Perseus 'line' milestones, and the build trusts them blindly. In Book XVI a milestone reads 580 instead of 280, so the chunk before it becomes [275, 579]. The template clamps that to line 480 and renders all 206 remaining Greek lines beside only five lines' worth of English. The next chunk [580, 284] renders no Greek (its English, 280–284, floats under the label '580–284'), and chunks 285… then render lines 285–480 a second time. Book VI has a duplicate 320 milestone, which produces the chunk [320, 319]: an English paragraph with no Greek under the label '320–319'.
homer.evidence: DOM for Book XVI: 676 .gk-line elements for a 480-line book. 196 line numbers appear twice (the first are 285–289). #ch-16-275 holds 206 lines, labelled '275–480'. #ch-16-580 holds 0 lines. Backwards range labels found: XVI '580–284', VI '320–319'. Screenshot: scratchpad/work/odyssey-extras/study-bk16-580.png.
homer.repro: Open /homer-odyssey/study.html#bk-16 and scroll to line 275. Greek runs to 480 next to one short English paragraph. Keep scrolling: an English-only block labelled '580–284' appears, then lines 285–480 start over.
homer.fix: In build_study_data.py, validate milestones: they must be strictly increasing and no larger than the book's line count. Repair known typos (580→280) or merge out-of-order milestones into the previous chunk, drop empty chunks, and fail the build on any chunk where end < start. In the template, never render a chunk whose range is inverted or already covered.
verifier_corrections: Beyond the finding: Book VI's duplicate milestone also produces duplicate element ids (two section#ch-6-320).

One addition: the Book VI duplicate milestone also emits two <section id="ch-6-320"> elements (duplicate DOM id). Line refs are right: the milestone is read at 125, end is computed at 159, the loop and clamp are at 326-330, and the range label is at line 350.

homer.title: Toolbars overflow phone widths: edition, theme and settings controls unreachable in theater, pdf-reader, fullbleed, the Odyssey reader and Odyssey mobile at 320px
homer.detail: The bars were sized for 3 editions and have no phone layout. html/body are overflow:hidden (and theater's .controls is a fixed 56px with flex-wrap), so anything past the edge cannot be scrolled to. Result: in the Odyssey reader on any phone you cannot change theme or text size. In theater and pdf-reader most editions and every theme are unreachable. Odyssey mobile.html, the phone-specific format, loses its Next-book button at 320px. The previous audit fixed exactly this class of bug in khayyam-rubaiyat/reader.html (P0) and in the spread-reader footers; Homer was excluded then.
homer.evidence: elementFromPoint at each control's centre (work/homer-nav/r2/bars.js, theater_phone.js, mobile2.js). **homer-odyssey/reader.html:** at 390, theme-btn [389..433] and settings-btn [437..481] are off-screen; at 320 the Modern tab is too (shots/bars_homer-odyssey_reader.html_m.png). The Iliad reader fits. **theater.html (controls visible):** Iliad 390, Cowper and all 5 theme dots at y=855 with viewport height 844; at 320 Pope too. Odyssey 390, Cowper/Murray/Greek/Modern and the 5 dots at y=855-886; at 320 everything from Pope on (shots/theater_homer-odyssey_m_controls.png). **pdf-reader.html:** Iliad 390, Cowper and 5 dots; 320, all 3 editions and 5 dots. Odyssey 390, Cowper/Murray/Greek/Modern and 5 dots; 320, all 6 editions and 5 dots. **fullbleed.html:** Iliad 390, 3 theme dots; 320, all 5. Odyssey 390, Modern and 5 dots; 320, Greek too. **homer-odyssey/mobile.html:** at 320, next-btn-m [346..387] is off-screen and Modern is clipped. At 390 and 320 the '1 / 24' counter is squeezed to 15px wide and wraps over 3 lines, spilling out of the bar (shots/mobile_homer-odyssey_m.png, mobile_homer-odyssey_s.png).
homer.repro: Open homer-odyssey/reader.html on a 390px phone: the ☀ theme and Aa settings buttons are not visible and cannot be scrolled to. Open homer-iliad/theater.html on a phone, tap to show controls: Cowper and the theme dots are below the screen edge.
homer.fix: Below ~600px, collapse the edition tabs into a <select> or a bottom sheet (mobile.html already has a sheet pattern), or make the edition group horizontally scrollable with the other controls pinned. Give theater .controls height:auto (or move editions/themes into a sheet). Move mobile.html's edition switch out of the bottom bar. Re-run an elementFromPoint reachability check at 320/390.
verifier_corrections: Scope is accurate. In Odyssey mobile.html at 320 the lost Next-book button is partly mitigated: a horizontal swipe still changes book, so this sub-item is medium. The Odyssey reader's theme dots are <span>s with no keyboard access (reader-template.html:392-396), so hiding the theme button removes the only theme path, not just one of several.

A minor wording fix: reader.html does not set html/body overflow:hidden. Its bar is position:fixed, which has the same effect (clipped, no horizontal scroll: document scrollWidth equals innerWidth). Theater, pdf and fullbleed do use overflow:hidden. Also cite homer-odyssey/data/mobile-template.html:65-78 for #bottom-bar with justify-content:space-between (the file and lines are already listed).

Minor precision fixes:
- Iliad pdf-reader at 320: Butler is partly visible (x302-346), not fully off-screen.
- illustrated's clipping occurs only at 320.
- The study.html bar is reachable by swiping (overflow-x:auto), so that sub-item is low severity.

The pdf-reader detail is slightly off:
- At 390 the Iliad Pope button is also clipped by 1px.
- At 320 the Butler button is only partly off-screen (x=302), not wholly off.

The study.html item is reachable by scrolling the bar, so it is low on its own. The workaround of rotating to landscape exists but is not obvious.

homer.title: fullbleed.html and pdf-reader.html pagination breaks on phones, tablets in portrait and narrow windows: blank pages, cut-off lines, stuck on page 1
homer.detail: Each page turn shifts #pageset by a fixed pixel amount in JS: SPREAD_WIDTH=920 in fullbleed, COL_STEP=620 in pdf. But the CSS lets the page box shrink: `max-width: 94vw` / `92vw`, `columns: 1` at <=860px, and `width: 94vw` at <=700px. As soon as the box is narrower than 920px (fullbleed, i.e. viewport < ~979px) or 620px (pdf, viewport < ~674px), each turn lands at the wrong offset. Also, #pageset has width:auto, so a negative margin-left makes the multi-column box wider. In the single-column phone layout the one column grows by 920px per turn. Result: on phones the fullbleed reader shows the same book heading and argument, cut at the left, on every spread after the first; nobody can get past page 1. pdf-reader shows blank pages, then scattered fragments with lines cut off. This breaks the invariant that homer-iliad/CLAUDE.md itself states ('COL_STEP must equal the viewport's own width'). It also answers both todo.md items 'Re-verify the CSS-column pagination in a real browser': it is broken.
homer.evidence: Playwright page-continuity probe (scratch r2/paged.js, paged2.js), comparing each line's client rects with the viewport after every ArrowRight. 390x844, Iliad fullbleed (Pope I): spreads 2-7 all show only children p0-p1 (heading/argument), with rects like `[-5480..302]` in a 342px viewport; #pageset grows to 5862px wide. Odyssey fullbleed: same. Iliad pdf 390x844: page 2 clipped, pages 3-4 empty, 5 skips in 6 turns. Odyssey pdf: pages 3-5 empty. 820x1180 (iPad portrait) fullbleed: spreads 2+ show p0-p1 only, clipped. 960x1000 (half of a 1920 screen): left column starts mid-word and the counter reads 'Spread 7/46' (24 at 1440). 660x900 pdf: 16-20 clipped lines per page. Control runs: 1024x768 fullbleed and 768x1024 pdf are clean, as is 1440x900 (0 skips, 0 clipped across all of Pope I). Screenshots: work/homer-nav/r2/shots/flip_homer-iliad_fullbleed.html_m_butler_1.png (text cut on left), flip_homer-odyssey_pdf-reader.html_m_pope_2.png (blank page 3/27), flip_homer-odyssey_pdf-reader.html_m_pope_5.png (blank except a stray '!'), fullbleed.html_960x1000.png.
homer.repro: Open homer-odyssey/pdf-reader.html#bk-pope-1 on a 390px-wide phone and tap › twice: page 3/27 is blank. Or open homer-iliad/fullbleed.html#bk-butler-1 at 390px (or in a 960px-wide window) and press → once: lines are cut off at the left edge.
homer.fix: Measure the real page geometry at runtime instead of using constants: step = viewport.clientWidth, and set the column width from it (e.g. 2 columns: (clientWidth - 2*PAD - GAP)/2; 1 column: clientWidth - 2*PAD, with column-gap = 2*PAD so step == clientWidth). Give #pageset an explicit width equal to the viewport (or move an inner fixed-width track with transform: translateX) so shifting it never resizes the multi-column box. Recompute on resize while keeping the current text position. Then update the CLAUDE.md 'Known caveat'.
verifier_corrections: Small line fix: the invariant quoted from homer-iliad/CLAUDE.md is at line 137 ('Important invariant'). Line 203 is only the 'Known caveat' heading, which refers back to it. At 390px the fullbleed reader does not literally repeat the heading each time: every spread after the first shows only clipped fragments of the first children (heading/argument), and no body text is ever readable. The pdf-reader at 390 shows clipped fragments of lines that move forward, with some pages fully blank. Everything else is as stated.

The cited lines are accurate. One minor point: the quoted invariant is at homer-iliad/CLAUDE.md:137-138; line 203 is the 'Known caveat' section. Also worth adding to the fix: the resize handler (fullbleed :259, pdf :244) calls loadBook(currentBook), which resets to spread/page 0. Rotating a phone or tablet therefore also throws away the reader's page, so any runtime re-measure has to keep a text anchor.

The Iliad percentages reproduce almost exactly. The Odyssey figures depend on the edition: the default edition gives 79.3% (fullbleed) and 68.6% (pdf) at 390, and Odyssey pdf-reader at 680 is 0% in the default edition. Scope is confirmed as Homer only: no other book's pdf-reader uses a constant step (alice and gibran derive it from vp.clientWidth).

The scope is wider than 'phones and narrow windows'. fullbleed breaks in any viewport under about 979px wide, including ordinary laptop split-screen windows. pdf-reader breaks under about 674px, drifting about 5.6px per page at 680px, so the cut-offs only start after page 8 or so there. The Odyssey fullbleed citation leaves out line 50 (the same viewport CSS). An extra consequence, inferred and not tested: on Android the page-number <input> in pdf-reader opens the soft keyboard. That fires resize, which resets to page 1, so a typed page number can be undone when the keyboard closes.

Scope: pdf-reader is only affected below about 674px, so tablets such as 820x1180 are fine there; fullbleed is affected below about 979px. My percentages are for non-whitespace characters and differ a little from the finder's, with the same magnitude. Add to the root cause: the negative margin-left widens the auto-width #pageset, so in narrow 1-column mode the column itself grows on every turn. Any fix must also fix #pageset's width (or its column-width/count) to the viewport, and not only compute the step at runtime. Separately, the resize handler calls loadBook(currentBook), which resets to spread 1.

Root cause: #pageset gets a negative margin-left while its width is auto, so it widens by spreadIdx×920 (or pageIdx×620) and the columns reflow on every turn. This is on top of the constant-vs-CSS width mismatch. At 390px the last fullbleed spread of Odyssey Book I is blank, not 'text from the middle of Book I'. The proposed fix is incomplete: measuring the step at runtime still leaves the reflow. It must also pin #pageset's width to the viewport's content width (for example an explicit px width set from clientWidth, or flex:none plus width) or move the content without changing its width (transform, or scrollLeft on the viewport). Only then do step = column-width + gap and page count = ceil((scrollWidth + gap)/step) hold. Lines are correct: fullbleed-template.html 50/88/134-136 (Iliad) and 50/88/137-139 (Odyssey); pdf-template.html 54/78/120 (Iliad) and 54/78/123 (Odyssey).

homer.title: Keyboard handlers take over keys meant for focused controls and ignore modifiers; closed drawers stay in the Tab order; mobile.html has no keyboard support
homer.detail: The document-level keydown handlers only skip INPUT/TEXTAREA (pdf: INPUT only) and never check modifier keys. reader.html: Space on a focused edition tab scrolls the page instead of choosing the edition. ArrowLeft/Right on the role=tablist changes the BOOK instead of moving between tabs, contrary to the ARIA tabs pattern. Alt+ArrowLeft (browser Back) is swallowed and changes the book. fullbleed/pdf/theater: Space on any focused button turns the page or book instead of pressing it. pdf-reader: with the book <select> focused, ArrowLeft/Right/Space turn pages, so the select cannot be changed with arrow keys. The closed reader sidebar (24 buttons at x=-260) and mobile.html's closed bottom sheets remain focusable off-screen. mobile.html has no key handling at all: Esc does not close its role=dialog aria-modal sheets. reader.html's theme dots are <span>s, so keyboard users can only cycle themes.
homer.evidence: work/homer-nav/r2/reader2.js, both books: after focusing #ed-butler, Space moved scrollY 467→1232 and the edition stayed pope; ArrowRight on it changed #bk-pope-3→#bk-pope-4 with focus still on ed-butler; Alt+ArrowLeft went back to Book III, and a dispatched Alt+ArrowLeft reports defaultPrevented=true; Shift+Tab from ☰ focused sidebar-chapter@-260 four times. paged_misc.js: Space on focused Butler went fullbleed 'Spread 2/33' (edition still pope), pdf 2/55; select focused then ArrowRight gave page 5/40, Space page 6/40. tabmobile.js: Tab order continues after next-btn-m into sheet-book-item(OFFSCREEN y=955…). mobile.js: 'Esc closes sheet? false'.
homer.repro: In homer-iliad/reader.html, Tab to the 'Butler' tab and press Space: the page scrolls and the edition does not change. Press → there: you jump to the next book.
homer.fix: Return early when e.altKey/ctrlKey/metaKey is set, or when e.target is a button, select, input or [role=tab]. Implement roving arrow keys inside the tablist. Mark closed drawers and sheets `inert` (or visibility:hidden). Add Esc/arrow handling to mobile.html. Convert reader theme dots to <button aria-label> (the khayyam index implementation is canonical).
verifier_corrections: Line fix: the theme-dot spans are at homer-iliad/data/reader-template.html:389-393 and homer-odyssey/data/reader-template.html:392-396. :360-363 is the sidebar <nav>, which is the off-screen-focus part. Overstatements: Enter still activates the tabs and buttons (verified), so the Space hijack has a keyboard workaround. On pdf-reader, ArrowUp/Down are not intercepted, so the book <select> can still be changed with Up/Down; only Left/Right/Space are hijacked. Added scope: the '['/']' cases also swallow Cmd+[ / Cmd+] (Mac Back/Forward) in reader.html. The fullbleed/pdf/mobile/theater theme dots are real <button>s but carry only `title`, no aria-label (e.g. theater-template.html:153-157, and fullbleed buildThemeDots sets only dot.title). That is a related baseline gap to fix at the same time.

pdf-reader's book select can still be changed with ArrowUp/ArrowDown. The handler hijacks only ArrowLeft/Right and Space (Space would normally open the picker). The handler guard is `e.target.tagName === 'INPUT'` only, at homer-iliad/data/pdf-template.html:238-242.

Two sub-claims are overstated:
- pdf-reader: ArrowDown on the focused select still changes the book natively; only Left/Right and Space are hijacked.
- illustrated: End on the select also natively selects Bk XXIV, so the defect is landing on the last page of Book XXIV (629/629) instead of its first page, not an unrelated jump.
The core Space and Arrow hijacking claims stand as written.

The claim that screen-reader users are affected is overstated. NVDA/JAWS browse mode and VoiceOver (VO-Space) activate controls with a synthesised click, not a raw Space keydown, so the main impact is on sighted keyboard-only users. On the pdf-reader select, ArrowUp/ArrowDown still work; only ArrowRight/ArrowLeft and Space are taken over. The medium severity stands, because Enter is the only workaround and the theater Space-on-Prev moves in the wrong direction.

study.html part: the bigger defect is that the word spans (.w, study-template.html:340) have no tabindex and cannot take focus (w.focus() fails). A keyboard user cannot open the popover at all, so 'doesn't move focus into it' applies only to pointer and screen-reader-click users. Also, for the theater part, add AGENT_README.md:120 as the convention it violates.

The study.html sub-point is the weakest. Its words are non-focusable <span class=w> (study-template:340), so the popover can only be opened by pointer. Not moving focus into a non-modal popover opened by click is common practice, and making every word focusable would recreate the 29k-tab-stop problem the previous audit removed from meditations. The accurate problem is narrower: #pop sits at the end of <body> with role=dialog, so a screen-reader user who activates a word gets no cue that it opened. The mobile.html point about having no arrow-key navigation is minor for a phone-first format. The aria-modal/VoiceOver trap is, as the finding says, inferred and not tested.

homer.title: mobile.html disables pinch-zoom and has no text-size setting, so readers cannot enlarge text
homer.detail: The viewport meta is `maximum-scale=1,user-scalable=no`, and mobile.html offers only a book list and a theme sheet: no font-size control (reader.html has one). On the site's phone-first format, low-vision readers have no way to enlarge the 17px text (WCAG 1.4.4). iOS ignores user-scalable=no, but Android Chrome honours it in some configurations.
homer.evidence: The meta tag is at line 5 of both templates. mobile.js / mobile2.js controls inventory: list-btn, theme-btn-mobile, prev/next, edition buttons, and no size option. .bk-content font-size is fixed at 17px (mobile-template CSS).
homer.repro: Open homer-odyssey/mobile.html on a phone and try to pinch-zoom or find a text-size option.
homer.fix: Drop maximum-scale/user-scalable=no, and add a text-size row to the theme sheet (saved in {book}-mobile-prefs).
verifier_corrections: Wider scope: the same zoom block with no text-size setting also affects alice-in-wonderland/mobile.html:5 (generated by alice-in-wonderland/gen_mobile.py:32) and gibran-prophet/mobile.html:5. Both block pinch in Chromium and neither has a size control, so the fix should cover all four pages plus the two Homer templates and gen_mobile.py. The newer vedas, khayyam-rubaiyat and aurelius-meditations mobile pages leave out the restriction and zoom normally, so the site is inconsistent here. Status is 'new' for all four pages: the 2026-08-20 audit covered alice and gibran and never mentioned this. One fact is too weak: Android Chrome honours user-scalable=no by default, not only 'in some configurations'. The user has to opt in to Force enable zoom or Page zoom to get around it.

The scope is wider than Homer, and the whole mobile format shares the same root cause. The same meta and the same missing size control are in alice-in-wonderland/mobile.html:5 (generated by alice-in-wonderland/gen_mobile.py:32) and gibran-prophet/mobile.html:5 (only TOC, theme and prev/next buttons). The old audit didn't flag those either, so status 'new' applies to all four pages. Two small factual fixes: (1) there are no files named mobile.js or mobile2.js; the controls and script are inline in data/mobile-template.html (buttons at lines 116-134, sheets at lines 138-144). (2) Android Chrome honours user-scalable=no by default, not just 'in some configurations'; only the opt-in 'Force enable zoom' accessibility setting overrides it. The fix list should also add a text-size option to the Alice and Gibran mobile pages (saved in alice-mobile-prefs and gibran-mobile-prefs), or add a link to reader.html.

The locations are right. The same meta also appears in alice-in-wonderland/mobile.html:5 and gibran-prophet/mobile.html:5, as the finding already says. The newer mobile.html pages in the other books omit it, which supports removing it here.

The WCAG 1.4.4 claim fits the page as served. The platform notes, though, should say Android Chrome's accessibility settings (force zoom, text scaling) are inferred workarounds, not tested.

The line refs are correct. Minor wording issue: the comparison with illustrated.html only holds for zoom. illustrated.html has no font-size control either (its only buttons are page arrows, theme dots, theme cycle and prev/next book); it just leaves pinch-zoom enabled. The same meta in alice-in-wonderland/mobile.html and gibran-prophet/mobile.html is the same root cause, if another auditor covers those.

homer.title: Theme dots and icon-only controls miss the accessibility baseline: what the smoke pass's 5 and 24 unlabeled buttons are
homer.detail: - **The '5 unlabeled buttons' in every Homer format** are the theme dots. - fullbleed, pdf-reader and mobile build them in JS with dot.title = t, so the only accessible name is the raw id: 'light-purple', 'dark-blue'. - theater gives them a title only ('Dark Violet'). - None have aria-label, which AGENT_README requires; a title is not a substitute on touch. - **The '24' in reader.html** are the progress-bar segments: : nested interactive elements, two Tab stops, both named '←'. The page arrows are named '‹' and '›' (title only). - **illustrated.html at ≤640px** hides the ' Odyssey' span, so the back link's name becomes '←'. - **No state:** - Theme dots in fullbleed, pdf-reader, mobile, theater, study and both index pages have no aria-pressed. - The edition buttons in mobile, theater, fullbleed and pdf-reader have no aria-pressed or aria-current. - A screen reader cannot tell which edition or theme is active (only reader's tabs and illustrated's dots expose state). - **Index pages:** the light-azure and dark-blue dots are both #2e6ab4, so two of the five swatches look identical.
homer.evidence:
CDP Accessibility.getFullAXTree names:
- pdf-reader: link '←', button '←', button '‹', button '›', buttons 'light-purple'…'dark-blue'.
- mobile: buttons 'light-purple'…'dark-blue'.
- theater: 'Light Purple'… from title.
- reader: 24 buttons 'Book I'…'Book XXIV' (progress) plus 24 '1 Book I'… (sidebar); no theme-dot nodes; the only theme control is 'Change theme'.
- illustrated at 390: link '←'.

themetap.js (390 touch): first tap on the reader theme button → theme 'sepia' and expanded=true at the same time.

keys.js: when #theme-btn has focus, .theme-dots opacity is 0 and the dot is a SPAN with tabIndex -1.

The index screenshot shows two identical blue dots.
homer.repro:
1. Open homer-iliad/reader.html and Tab to the theme button: the five swatches never appear and can't be focused.
2. In homer-iliad/pdf-reader.html, inspect the toolbar with a screen reader: 'dark-violet, button', and '←' twice.
homer.fix:

homer.title: Ancient Greek text is announced as English: no lang="grc" in any Odyssey reader, the study page or the word popover

(2) The Greek lines, the transliteration and the popover form all inherit lang=en, which breaks the AGENT_README baseline on marking language changes. Screen readers will read polytonic Greek with an English voice. (3) Touch targets: theme dots 13x13 with no hit-area expander, Translit/English toggles 22px tall, book select 27px, popover close button 18x20. The baseline is 40px or more. (4) Theme dots have no aria-pressed, so the current theme is not announced (illustrated.html does this correctly). (5) Line numbers use text2 at opacity .55, about 2.1:1 in every theme (1.7:1 in dark-blue). Transliteration and range labels are 3.36:1 in dark-blue (a site-wide token). The Tab sequence visits only the back link, select, toggles, 5 dots and Prev/Next. closest('[lang]') for .gk-text, .tr-text and #p-form returns 'en'. Measured sizes: theme-dot 13x13, tog 87x22, book-select 101x27, back 28x35, p-close 18x20. The aria snapshot shows the theme buttons with no pressed state. Move focus into #pop on open and return it on Escape. Add lang="grc" to .gk and #p-form, and lang="grc-Latn" to .tr-text and #p-tr. The line-number worst case is dark-blue at 1.71:1, which the finding states correctly.

One fix caveat: document-level keydown handlers at study-template.html:396-400 already bind ArrowLeft and ArrowRight to previous/next book. They skip only input, select and textarea targets. One caveat on the suggested fix: the document-level keydown handler at study-template.html:396-400 changes book on ArrowLeft/ArrowRight whenever the target is not an input, select or textarea. Left/Right word navigation would jump to the previous or next book unless that handler also ignores events from the word or line widget, or the widget stops propagation. homer.title: Illustrated keyboard: global key handler hijacks Space and arrows on focused controls (Space on 'Previous page' goes forward; Space cannot pick a theme)
homer.detail: The document-level keydown handler calls preventDefault() and go(1) for ' ', ArrowRight and PageDown, and go(-1) for ArrowLeft and PageUp, whatever element has focus. It does not skip buttons or selects and does not check modifier keys. Pressing Space on a focused button, the standard way to activate it, therefore suppresses the button's click and turns the page forward. A keyboard user on 'Previous page' moves the wrong way, and a keyboard user on a theme dot turns the page and never changes the theme.
homer.evidence: Starting at #bk-2-p30 (31/629), focus #pg-prev and press Space: 32/629, one page forward. Enter on the same button: 31/629 (correct). Focus 'Sepia theme' and press Space: the page advances to 32/629 and the theme stays light-purple. ArrowRight on the focused book select turns the page.
homer.repro: On illustrated.html, press Tab until 'Previous page' has focus, then press Space. The page counter increases.
homer.fix: Return early when e.target is a button, select, input or link (or anything inside #top-bar) for Space, Enter and arrow keys, and ignore events with altKey, ctrlKey or metaKey set.
verifier_corrections: Minor: the finder wrote 'Enter on the same button: 31/629'. From a fresh 31/629, Enter on Previous correctly goes to 30/629. Home and End in the same handler also fire on a focused select, and Space on the narrow-width #theme-cycle button is hijacked the same way, so the fix should cover those too.

Same scope, with more affected keys: Home and End are also taken from a focused <select>, where they would normally pick the first or last option, and they reset the book position. Because no modifier check exists, Alt+ArrowLeft/Right (browser Back/Forward) are also intercepted by preventDefault and turn the page instead.

homer.title: Murray (Loeb 1919) edition: text split mid-sentence at every 5-line chunk and full of orphan footnote numbers
homer.detail: The Murray seed was made by treating each Perseus eng3 line milestone (a Loeb 5-line citation chunk) as a paragraph, the same chunks the study reader uses. The reader shows the edition as prose: justified, with a 1.5em indent and a paragraph gap. Sentences are therefore broken into separate indented paragraphs throughout. Footnote reference numbers from the source were left glued to the preceding word, with no footnotes shown, in all five readers and in the study reader's English column.
homer.evidence: 1,588 of 2,434 Murray 'paragraphs' (65%) end mid-sentence and 1,431 start in lowercase. For example, Book I paragraph 1 ends 'upon the sea,' and paragraph 2 begins 'seeking to win his own life…'. 191 footnote numbers are glued to words: 'Argeiphontes,1', 'flashing-eyed1', 'wrath2', 'unresting1', 'mid-Argos.”1', and so on; Book I alone has 17 (DOM query of .chapter-text p). The same 191 appear in seeds/study.json's English chunks. Screenshot: reader-murray-bk1.png. Also 11.102 has the typo 'Archaeans'.
homer.repro: Open homer-odyssey/reader.html#bk-murray-1 and read the first screen: indented paragraphs break mid-sentence at 'upon the sea,' and 'that bright goddess,', and 'Argeiphontes,1' appears a few paragraphs down.
homer.fix:
Rebuild murray.md from the eng3 XML using real paragraph (

) boundaries, joining text across milestones, and drop or convert note markers (/n). Keep the 5-line chunking only for study.json. If paragraph structure can't be recovered, at least join chunks until the text ends with sentence-final punctuation, and strip /(?<=[A-Za-z,.;:’”])\d+/ markers.
verifier_corrections: The '11.102' typo reference means Book XI, 102nd paragraph (0-based index 101); it is not line 102. There is no Murray generator script in the repo (murray.md arrived in commit bd7bafb), so the fix means writing a new extractor rather than editing an existing one.

The 'Archaeans' typo is in Book XI, Loeb lines 505–509 (the Neoptolemus/Scyros passage, murray.md:2293), not 11.102. '1,588 end mid-sentence' counts paragraphs ending in ';' or ':'. Strictly mid-clause endings (no .!?;:—) are 1,329 (55%). The title's 'at every 5-line chunk' overstates it: the split happens at every chunk, and 55–65% of chunks break mid-sentence.

The Perseus murray-eng3.xml is not in the repo and the internet is blocked here, so I could not check how the markers are encoded. itertext() on a <note> holding footnote text would pull in the whole note, not a bare digit. So the digits probably come from an empty marker element or from plain p.text/tail text, and the fix should look at the real XML rather than assume <note>. It may need a regex strip such as (?<=[A-Za-z,;:.!?”’—])\d+(?=\s|$). The claim that the footnote text is included nowhere could not be verified either way. Besides study.html, the affected pages are the Murray tab of reader, mobile, fullbleed, theater and pdf-reader.

homer.title: Iliad Cowper seed shows an editor's prose commentary as verse and has scanning errors (OCR), despite the changelog saying commentary was excluded
homer.detail: Thirty-two lines of editorial commentary, from the Gutenberg edition's notes, were parsed as Cowper's verse at the end of three books. All five Iliad readers show them as the book's closing lines, one 70-character 'verse line' at a time. They are Book VI lines 646–650 ('It may be observed, that Hector begins to resume his hope of success…'), Book X lines 684–699 ('The vividness of the scenes presented to us in this Book constitute its chief beauty…') and Book XI lines 1035–1045 ('It will be well here to observe the position of the Greeks… upon this depends the great catastrophe of the poem.'). The same seed also has scanning (OCR) and marginal-number artifacts: 2.295 'Thersites. Instant starting to his side, 295' (a leftover line number), 10.482 'quar4ers', 10.513 'minu4e', 15.537 'B9 Hector pierced', 15.563 'Te5cer'. Lines 16.746–747 are two rows of asterisks ('* * * * *'), probably a transcription separator; worth checking against PG #16452. The changelog says 'editorial-commentary exclusion (Cowper's uncredited "—Felton." notes)', so only notes signed '—Felton.' were caught.
homer.evidence: I scanned for runs of lines of 62+ characters in the verse seeds; the only runs are these three passages. In the browser, reader.html#bk-cowper-11 ends with the commentary lines (screenshot iliad-reader-cowper-11-end.png). The OCR words were found with the digit regex /\d/ over the lines.
homer.repro: Open homer-iliad/reader.html#bk-cowper-10 and scroll to the end of Book X: sixteen lines of modern prose criticism follow 'Delicious, from the brimming beaker drawn.'
homer.fix: Delete the three commentary blocks from cowper.json. Fix quarters, minute, 'By Hector', Teucer, and remove the '295'. Check the asterisk rows against the source. Add a check to the parser: flag any verse line over about 60 characters and any digit.

homer.title: Study: ~270 word popovers show a wrong lemma and gloss because the lemma normaliser strips a leading ῥ
homer.detail: norm_lemma() runs re.sub(r"^[̀-ͯ᾽-῿ʼ᾿]+", "", lemma) to drop stray leading marks. The range ᾽-῿ (U+1FBD–U+1FFF) also covers precomposed letters such as ῥ (U+1FE5) and Ῥ (U+1FEC). Every lemma that starts with rough-breathing rho loses its first letter. The diacritic-stripped gloss fallback then often matches a different word, so the popover shows a malformed lemma with a confidently wrong meaning, or no gloss at all.
homer.evidence: There are 57 malformed lemmas covering about 269 word occurrences (not counting the 216 correct ῥ' → ἄρα). Examples: ῥακέων (Od. 22.1) → lemma 'άκος', gloss 'a cure, relief, remedy for' (should be ῥάκος 'rag'). ῥέζω → 'έζω' 'settle, set firmly'. ῥεῖα 'easily' → 'εῖα' 'on! up! away!'. ῥίς 'nose' → 'ίς' 'sinew, tendon'. ῥαίω 'shatter' → 'αίω' 'perceive'. ῥοδοδάκτυλος 'rosy-fingered' (22×) → 'οδοδάκτυλος' with no gloss. All 57 affected lemmas begin with a vowel that has no breathing mark.
homer.repro: Open /homer-odyssey/study.html#bk-22 and tap 'ῥακέων' in line 1. The popover reads 'lemma: άκος (akos) · a cure, relief, remedy for'.
homer.fix: Strip only combining marks and spacing modifiers, for example with a class limited to U+0300–U+036F, U+1FBD, U+1FBF–U+1FC1, U+1FCD–U+1FCF, U+1FDD–U+1FDF, U+1FED–U+1FEF, U+1FFD–U+1FFE, ʼ and ᾿, or by testing unicodedata.category(c) == 'Mn'/'Sk'. Regenerate study.json and assert that no lemma starts with an unbreathed vowel.
verifier_corrections: Scope: 57 malformed lemmas covering about 295 occurrences, not about 269. The finder counted only forms whose own first letter is ῥ, and so missed augmented or reduplicated forms such as ἔρρεξα, ἔρρεεν, ἐρρύσατο and ἔρριψε, whose lemmas are also mangled. The claim that 'all 57 begin with a vowel that has no breathing' is inaccurate. The range also contains ῆ (U+1FC6), so ῥῆγος→'γος' (15×) and ῥῆσις→'σις' lose two letters and start with a consonant. There are also 3 occurrences of ῥ̓ with an empty lemma, probably the same stripping removing the whole lemma. The fix is still the right one. The assertion should be 'no lemma changed by the leading-strip regex other than genuinely stray marks', not only 'no lemma starts with an unbreathed vowel'.

Scope detail: the strip does not always stop after the ῥ. If the next letter is also a precomposed character in U+1FBD–U+1FFF (for example ῖ or ῆ), that is stripped as well, so ῥῖγος becomes 'γος' and ῥῆσις becomes 'σις'. The claim that 'all affected lemmas begin with an unbreathed vowel' therefore misses these consonant-initial cases. The fix's regression assertion should instead be 'no lemma whose forms begin with ῥ lacks an initial ρ', or it should compare against the raw treebank lemma. Also, the 31 ῥ̓ tokens lemmatised as ἆρα (the interrogative particle) come from the treebank and are not caused by this bug.

Impact is limited to about 0.3% of tokens, but it includes very frequent Homeric words (ῥέζω, ῥοδοδάκτυλος, ῥεῖα). The suggested fix regex contains the range '῭-`'. Make sure the upper bound is U+1FEF GREEK VARIA and not an ASCII backtick (U+0060); otherwise Python rejects the reversed range. The builder cannot run as-is because its source paths point at a macOS scratchpad, so patching study.json directly is the practical route.

Add the other wrong glosses listed in the reasoning (ῥέζω, ῥάπτω, ῥίς, ῥάκος, ῥώψ, ῥαίω, ῥαίνω, ῥίον). Capitalized names are hit too (Ῥαδάμανθυς→'αδάμανθυς'). Write the suggested replacement regex with \u escapes: as typed in the finding, the '῭-`' part may use an ASCII backtick, which would make a reversed range and raise re.error.

homer.title: Illustrated on short desktop windows (viewport height ≲620px): stacked layout leaves 3–4 lines of text per page, ~2,500 page turns
homer.detail: trim() caps the spread width at H*1.55, and beside mode needs W > 860, so a desktop window of normal width whose viewport is under about 620px tall falls back to the stacked layout. The plate then takes up to 60% of the height, leaving a caption budget of about 3–4 lines. That describes a 1366x768 laptop with browser chrome and a bookmarks bar, a 1280x720 display, or a 1024x600 netbook. The book becomes ~4x longer than at 1440x900, and each page is mostly picture with lots of empty paper at the side.
homer.evidence: Lines of caption per page on a plated page of Book II: 1280x600 → 3 lines, 24 words, 2566 pages. 1366x620 → 3 lines, 2511 pages. 1024x600 → 3 lines, 2566 pages. 900x700 → 4 lines, 1910 pages. By contrast 1366x657 → beside, 13 lines, 1280 pages, and 1440x900 → 22 lines, 629 pages. Screenshot: scratchpad/work/odyssey-extras/ill-1024x600-bk2.png.
homer.repro: Open illustrated.html#bk-2 in a 1280x600 viewport and turn 3 pages: each page shows a small square plate and three lines of prose.
homer.fix: Choose beside whenever W0 (stage width) is above ~860, even if the trim ratio would clip it; let the trim width follow W0 on short screens instead of H*1.55. Alternatively lower the stacked plate cap (e.g. 45% of H) when capAvail would fall below ~8 lines.
verifier_corrections: The trigger is a viewport height of about 561–623px on any window of about 981px width or more, plus narrower non-phone windows such as 900x700 (4 lines). Worth adding: at 560px or less the narrow media query switches to full-width beside, so shrinking the window makes reading much better, which shows the threshold is the bug. '1280x720 display' should read '1280x720 CSS screen', for example a 1080p laptop at 150% OS scaling, whose viewport is about 600px tall.

The affected band is viewport heights of about 561-623px on windows wider than about 980px. At 560px and below the NARROW media query switches to the full-width beside layout, which is far better: 851 pages at 1280x560 against 2566 at 1280x600. Name that discontinuity as the clearest symptom. The line-569 escape clause `W > H*1.6` is dead code for non-narrow viewports because of line 547. The 900x700 example has a different cause: stage width 780 < 860, which is 'narrow screen → stacked' by design per homer-odyssey/CLAUDE.md. Drop it or note it as a design limitation rather than this bug.

homer.title: Theater: tap, click, Space, j or a short swipe on the text jumps to the next whole book and discards your place; mobile.html swipe does the same
homer.detail: In theater a 'slide' is a whole book (500-1100 verse lines, ~34,000px of scroll for Pope Book I on desktop). Yet any click anywhere on #stage (the text), Space, j, or a 50px horizontal swipe calls go(1), which re-renders the next book at scrollTop 0. On touch devices the controls are auto-hidden, and the natural gesture to reveal them (tapping the text) fires touchstart to show the controls and then click, which advances a book. So every attempt to reach the controls skips ~40 screens of text, and going back lands at the top of the previous book. The AGENT_README keyboard contract says j/space scroll. Here they change book, and ArrowDown/PageDown do nothing until the user first Tabs into the scroller. mobile.html uses a similarly loose swipe (60px, ratio 1.5): a slightly diagonal flick while scrolling changes book, and swiping back returns to the top of the previous book.
homer.evidence: work/homer-nav/r2/theater_phone.js at 390x844 and 320x640, both books: scrolled .book-view to 4000, then touchscreen.tap on the text gave `{"hash":"#bk-pope-2","st":0,"vis":true}`. Desktop theater.js: wheel to 2000, mouse click on the text went to Book III. On load, ArrowDown/PageDown/End left scrollTop at 0. Space went to #bk-pope-2, j to Book II, k to Book I. swipe2.js (CDP touch), Book III at scrollTop 3000, flick dx=-80/dy=-45: theater and Odyssey mobile both went to #bk-pope-4 at scrollTop 0; swiping back gave #bk-pope-3 at scrollTop 0.
homer.repro: On a phone, open homer-iliad/theater.html#bk-pope-1, scroll well into the book, then tap the text to bring up the controls. Book II opens at its first line.
homer.fix: Remove click/tap-to-advance on the text, or limit it to explicit edge zones or to when scrolled to the end, and make a tap only toggle the controls. Make Space/j/k/ArrowDown/PageDown scroll .book-view (tabindex=-1, focus it after render) and keep ArrowLeft/Right for books. Raise the swipe threshold (e.g. >100px, dy < 30px) and/or require the book to be scrolled to its end. Persist the in-book scroll position (see the position finding).
verifier_corrections: Only theater's part is a defect as stated: the click/tap-to-advance, Space/j changing book, and no keyboard scrolling until Tab. For homer-iliad/data/mobile-template.html:273-279 and homer-odyssey/data/mobile-template.html:277-283, the swipe is the intended swipe-between-books gesture with a normal threshold, so drop the 'slightly diagonal flick' claim. The dx=-80/dy=-45 test gesture is mostly horizontal. The remaining mobile problem is the lost in-book scroll position when you swipe back, which belongs to the position finding. Keep ArrowLeft/Right for books, but the fix should not require changing mobile's threshold.

The behaviour is documented as intended in homer-iliad/CLAUDE.md:173-175, so this is a UX/design defect, not a regression or undocumented bug. The 'AGENT_README keyboard contract' applies to reader.html only (AGENT_README.md:90). A scroll-drag also reveals the controls, so 'every attempt to reach the controls' is overstated. The mobile.html swipe part is low severity at most. Add to the evidence: a mouse drag-selection of text also advances the book (click fires on the common ancestor). Lines are right: Iliad theater :264-267, :269-273, :280-283; Odyssey +3.

The line ranges are right: iliad template 251-267, odyssey template 254-270. In the built files the code is at homer-iliad/theater.html:262-264 and homer-odyssey/theater.html:265-267.

Two small corrections:
- Touch is not strictly the only way to reveal the controls. A short vertical scroll also fires touchstart and reveals them without advancing. Tapping, though, is the natural gesture and it jumps to the next book.
- The same stage-click pattern, not gated to fine pointers, also exists in gibran-prophet/theater.html:479-486, which is outside Homer scope. The khayyam, alice, meditations and vedas theaters do not use it.

The 'intended for desktop (CLAUDE.md)' claim is inaccurate. homer-iliad/CLAUDE.md:173-175 documents click-stage-to-advance and swipe with no pointer restriction, so the docs should be updated along with any fix. The line ranges are right; the key lines are Iliad 262 (touchstart→showControls) and 264-267 (stage click→go(1)), and Odyssey 265 and 267-270. homer.title: fullbleed/pdf page count goes stale: reading forward into a shorter book adds 9-15 blank or repeated pages, and every page turn visibly reflows the columns
homer.detail: loadBook() swaps in the new book and measures pageset.scrollWidth before applySpreadOffset()/applyPageOffset() reset margin-left. Because #pageset is width:auto, the old negative margin still makes it as wide as the previous position. So after paging forward off the end of a book (the normal way to read straight through), or switching edition mid-book, the new book's page count is at least the old page index. The reader then flips through trailing pages that are blank or, because of column balancing, repeat the book's last lines, before reaching the next book. The counter ('Spread 1/33') is also wrong. The same width-follows-margin effect makes the columns re-flow during every 0.3s page-turn transition: text rewraps and crosses the spine, then snaps back. Separately, the page count is never recomputed after web fonts load. The Odyssey CLAUDE.md documents that exact race for illustrated.html (fixed there with document.fonts.ready), but fullbleed/pdf still have it.
homer.evidence: work/homer-nav/r2/stale.js at 1440x900. Iliad fullbleed, Pope Book III loaded fresh = 'Spread 1/18'; reached by ArrowRight off the end of Book II = 'Spread 1/33'. 15 extra spreads before Book IV, 9 fully blank (first blank at 24/33); stale2.js shows spreads 19-23 re-showing lines 559-577. Odyssey pdf, Pope Book V fresh = 33 pages; after reading on from Book IV = 56, with 15 blank pages. midflip.js, column width sampled per frame during one turn: 380, 398, 432, 482, 539, 595, 403 ... 533, 380px. shots/fullbleed_midturn.png shows the right column running across the spine. Font race (simulated, real EB Garamond not loadable here): swapping in a wider substitute 2.5s after load left Iliad fullbleed at 24 spreads when 27 were needed, and the last line never became visible.
homer.repro: Open homer-iliad/fullbleed.html#bk-pope-2 at 1440x900, hold → until Book III opens. The footer says 'Spread 1/33'; keep going and spreads 19-33 are blank or repeat the ending.
homer.fix: Reset marginLeft to 0 with the transition disabled before measuring, then compute the count. Give #pageset a fixed explicit width (or animate transform on an inner track) so shifting never resizes the multi-column box. That removes both the stale count and the mid-turn reflow. Repaginate on document.fonts.ready (and on fonts 'loadingdone'), keeping the current text anchor.
verifier_corrections: The stale count comes from any loadBook() call while margin-left is nonzero, not only from reading off the end of a book. That includes Next/Prev Book, edition switch, book-select and the resize handler (fullbleed-template.html:259/262, pdf-template.html:244/247). The Odyssey pdf case adds 23 extra pages, 15 of them blank, which is worse than the '9-15 blank' in the title suggests. The mid-turn reflow only affects readers without prefers-reduced-motion. The font-load race is code-inferred, not observed.

The findings are accurate. Add that the stale count carries into every following book when reading straight through (Book IV also opened at 1/33), and that edition switches and book-select mid-book trigger it too. The font-race part is unverified here, and with the real EB Garamond it more likely adds blank trailing spreads than hides text. This shares its root cause and fix with finding 0 and should be cross-referenced there.

homer.title: Your place inside a book is never saved: reload, resize, rotation or an edition switch returns to the start of a 25-57 page book
homer.detail: Every format stores only the book (#bk-<ed>-N). A Homeric book is long: Iliad Pope Book V is 46,981px in reader.html at 1440 (~52 screens); Pope Book I is 24 spreads or 40 pdf pages; Odyssey Cowper books are ~56 pdf pages. reader.html: on reload the browser restores the scroll position, then the rendered `<section id="bk-pope-5">` matches the URL hash, so native fragment navigation (made smooth by `html{scroll-behavior:smooth}`) carries the reader back to the top of the book. theater/mobile never save the .book-view/#bk-slide scrollTop. fullbleed/pdf keep the page neither in the hash nor in prefs, and their resize handler calls loadBook(), which resets to page 1 on any resize or device rotation. The AGENT_README convention for paged readers (#p-N) is not followed at all. The previous audit's open item concerned #p-N being viewport-dependent; here there is no sub-book position.
homer.evidence: work/homer-nav/r2/reload.js and idcheck.js, homer-iliad/reader.html#bk-pope-5 scrolled to 15000: after reload, scroll events run 6524→6415→6075→5492→4688→3732→2744→1852→1153→691→468→442, and 442 is the section top. theater.js: wheel to scrollTop 3000, reload gives 0. mobile.js: scrollTop 5000 gives 0 after reload. paged_misc.js, both books: fullbleed 'Spread 10/24', reload gives 'Spread 1/24'; 9 turns then a window resize 1440→1400 gives 'Spread 1/24'; pdf page 10/40 gives 1/40 on reload and on resize.
homer.repro: Open homer-odyssey/pdf-reader.html#bk-pope-1, go to page 10, reload (or resize the window): you are back on page 1. In reader.html, scroll halfway through a book and reload: the page glides back to the book's first line.
homer.fix: Add a viewport-independent sub-position to the hash, e.g. #bk-pope-5-l283 (line or paragraph index), which also avoids the #p-N problem. Write it with replaceState, throttled, on scroll or page turn, and restore it in script after render. Rename the section id so it never equals the hash. On resize, repaginate and seek to the anchored line instead of page 1.
verifier_corrections: Scope nuance: for reader.html, AGENT_README.md:92/136 defines the scrolling reader's hash as chapter-level (#ch-N). Every book's reader.html therefore returns to the chapter top on reload by house convention. Homer makes this worse because one 'chapter' is 25-57 screens, and the id==hash collision adds the visible smooth glide. The edition-switch reset is largely inherent, since editions have different line/paragraph counts, and is the weakest part of the claim. The clearest defects are in fullbleed and pdf: the resize reset (a plain bug) and the missing page position in the hash (AGENT_README.md:99/137 asks for #p-N). Side note: fullbleed, pdf and mobile write `book` into their localStorage prefs (e.g. fullbleed-template.html:177, pdf-template.html:159, mobile-template.html:195), and theater writes 'iliad-theater-book'. AGENT_README.md:159-160 forbids this. The finding's statement that the *page* is kept in neither place is still accurate.

For reader.html, reload loses the position intermittently (a race between scroll restoration and fragment scrolling to the section id that equals the hash), not always. The title's 'never saved' is accurate for theater, mobile, fullbleed and pdf. Add: fullbleed and pdf store `book` in the {book}-{format}-prefs localStorage object, which AGENT_README says must never hold position.

The line numbers are accurate. Minor point: the Odyssey illustrated.html #bk-N-pM is a global, viewport-dependent page index, so it is not a fully repagination-safe model either. The suggested line-anchored hash is the better fix, and it also covers the old audit's 'left open' concern.

Line refs are correct. The Odyssey resize listeners (fullbleed-template:262, pdf-template:247) should be listed too. Likely aggravation, not device-tested: phone rotation fires resize, and so may the on-screen keyboard opening for the pdf page-number input, which would reset to page 1.

homer.title: mobile.html and theater.html drop taps made during the fade animation, so the display and internal state disagree (books silently skipped, wrong edition shown)
homer.detail: render() returns early while its 220ms (mobile) / 260ms (theater) fade is running. But mobile's goTo() and both formats' setEdition() update `current`/`activeEdition` before calling it, and the pending render's timeout draws the book it captured earlier. A quick double tap on Next therefore shows Book II while the state is Book III; the next tap shows Book IV, so Book III is skipped. A Prev tap right after the double tap does nothing visible. Tapping two edition buttons quickly shows the first edition's text while the active button, the top-bar label and the URL hash say the second. That wrong hash is what a reload or shared link will use.
homer.evidence: work/homer-nav/r2/mobile2.js, touchscreen taps on Next 90ms apart (390 and 320, both books): `{"cur":2,"hash":"#bk-pope-2","lbl":"Book II"}`, third tap gives `"#bk-pope-4","Book IV"`. mobile.js: double Next then Prev leaves the hash at #bk-pope-2, cur 1. Edition taps 60ms apart: text is Butler prose ('When the companies were t…'), active button cowper, hash #bk-cowper-3 (Iliad m: label 'Butler' but active 'cowper'). theater.js, clicks 80ms apart: indicator 'Book III · Samuel Butler', Butler prose, active button cowper, hash #bk-cowper-3.
homer.repro: On a phone, open homer-iliad/mobile.html#bk-pope-1 and double-tap → quickly: Book II shows. Tap → once more: Book IV appears.
homer.fix: Inside the setTimeout, read the latest state (EDITIONS[activeEdition], current) instead of values captured when the call started, and re-run the render if the state changed during the fade. Alternatively queue the latest request instead of dropping it. Do not mutate `current` in goTo() when the render will be dropped.
verifier_corrections: Scope: theater's go() checks `if (animating) return` before it mutates `current` (theater-template.html:226-231, Odyssey :229-234). Theater therefore cannot skip books; it is affected only through setEdition(), where the displayed edition and the active button/hash/localStorage edition disagree. The book-skip part applies to mobile only (Next/Prev buttons, swipe and the book sheet all go through goTo). Minor: in Odyssey mobile the top-bar label comes from the live SHORT_NAME[activeEdition] (mobile-template.html:193). There it shows the *second* edition's name over the first edition's text; in the Iliad it shows the first ('Butler'). The same dropped-render window also exists for the first 220/260ms after load because init calls render().

homer.title: Illustrated: the reading position moves on every reload and every return visit (page index restored against the pre-web-font pagination)
homer.detail: On load, paginate() runs at inline-script time, before EB Garamond has loaded (the file's own comment says so), so the pages are measured with fallback-font metrics. restore() then applies the saved page ordinal (#bk-N-pM, or prefs.page when there is no hash) to that fallback pagination. When the font arrives, repaginateKeepingPosition() re-anchors on the first sentence of that wrong page. Each reload therefore moves the reader by the ratio between the two paginations (the HANDOFF reports 866 fallback pages vs 748 real ones, so about 14%), and the new wrong page is written back to the hash and to localStorage, so the error compounds. The landing page links illustrated.html without a hash, so every returning reader takes the prefs.page path and hits the same drift.
homer.evidence: Google Fonts was simulated in the sandbox with route interception (FreeSerif served as 'EB Garamond', 250 ms delay). Reading at #bk-20-p549 ('Fulfill now even for wretched me…'), reload 1 landed on #bk-21-p565, reload 2 on #bk-22-p582 and reload 3 on #bk-22-p599. Returning through index.html with no hash landed on #bk-23-p616. The il-label trace shows each load mapping p549 onto the 629-page fallback pagination (550/629), then jumping to 566/646 after the font loads. The direction and size depend on the metric ratio, and every reload loses the place.
homer.repro: With web fonts loading normally (live site, cold or slow cache), open illustrated.html#bk-20, turn a few pages, reload. The page shown is not the one you were on, and it keeps moving on each further reload.
homer.fix: Anchor the position to content rather than to a page ordinal. Write a sentence or paragraph id to the hash (e.g. #bk-20-s1234, where s is the gi used in repaginateKeepingPosition) and resolve it after every pagination. Alternatively, defer the first restore until fonts.load() resolves, or capture the target sentence before the first paginate and resolve it against the final pagination. Keep reading #bk-N-pM as a legacy form.
verifier_corrections: Narrow the scope: the drift happens only when EB Garamond is not yet available at inline-script time, i.e. a cold or evicted font cache or a slow network, including opening a saved or shared #bk-N-pM link on a fresh device. With a warm HTTP cache in Chromium, no drift was observed on reload, new tab, or browser restart. Add one more failure mode: when the web font paginates to more pages than the fallback, a saved ordinal beyond the fallback page count resets the reader to the book's splash page (hash path) or to the cover (prefs path). With real EB Garamond against Georgia (fewer pages with the web font), the drift would run backwards by about 14% of the page index. Severity is medium, not high.

'On every reload' is overstated. In Chromium, same-tab reloads with the font in the memory cache did NOT drift: the first pagination already used the web font (549/646 at DCL) and the position was stable across 3 reloads. The drift occurs whenever the web font is not already in memory at inline-script time: cold loads, new browser sessions/tabs with a disk-cache-only font (verified), and slow networks. The finder's route interception disables Playwright's HTTP cache, which made every reload cold. On the live site the real fallback is Georgia, which is wider than EB Garamond (HANDOFF: 866 vs 748 pages), so readers would drift BACKWARD about 14% per visit rather than forward as in the sandbox.

homer.title: Illustrated: page index kept in prefs, and a shared #bk-N-pM link opens in a different book on another screen size (the book-number fallback never runs)
homer.detail: render() does prefs.page = cur, which puts a page ordinal into odyssey-illustrated-prefs. AGENT_README says a prefs object must never carry a page index. Page counts vary with viewport (479 to 2636 pages measured), so both prefs.page and the pM in the hash point at unrelated text on another window size. restore()'s comment says it falls back to the book number, but it returns n whenever n < pages.length and only uses the book number when the index is out of range. The page can therefore land in a different book from the one named in its own hash, and then rewrites the hash to match. #cover is not parsed (it falls through to prefs.page), and neither the study nor the illustrated page listens for hashchange. This relates to the audit's 'deliberately left open' note that #p-N is viewport-dependent, but here the book is in the hash and the cheap fallback the code claims to have is not implemented.
homer.evidence: A desktop reader at #bk-20-p532 (Book XX) sends the link to a phone (390x844). The phone shows 'Bk VIII ✦', 533/1207, with Nausithous text, and the hash is rewritten to #bk-8-p532. A phone link #bk-9-p575 opened on desktop shows Book XXII (Agelaus). localStorage after reading: {"theme":"light-purple","page":628}. Setting location.hash='#bk-7' in the page leaves the content on the cover.
homer.repro: At 1440x900, open illustrated.html#bk-20 and turn 5 pages, then copy the URL. Open it in a 390x844 phone context: the book picker reads Bk VIII.
homer.fix: Remove page from prefs and keep only presentation state. In restore(), accept pM only if pages[n].bi matches the book in the hash; otherwise use the book's splash page, or better a sentence id (see the reload-drift finding). Handle #cover explicitly and add a hashchange listener on both pages.
verifier_corrections: The '479 pages' low end was not reproduced; I measured 629 at 1440x900 with fallback fonts, 1207 at 390x844 and 2636 at 320x640. It probably depends on font or viewport. The in-page location.hash='#bk-7' test leaves the content on whatever page was showing (Book XX in my run), not specifically on the cover. The root cause is the same: there is no hashchange handler.

Minor: the missing hashchange listener is not an AGENT_README requirement (it only requires parsing on load), so treat that part as polish. The prefs.page convention violation also feeds the no-hash drift in finding 2 and shares its fix, a content-anchored position.

homer.title: Illustrated serves full 2048×2048 JPEGs everywhere: ~11 MB to reach the first page of Book I on a phone, 5 × 2 MB files shown as 70px tiles
homer.detail: Every plate is a single 2048×2048 JPEG of 1.5–2.5 MB. The cover, the sticky scene art (346px wide on a phone) and the title-page fan of up to five tiles (70–106px) all load the same full-size file, with no srcset, no thumbnails and no WebP/AVIF. The prefetcher also pulls the next plate on the cover. On a phone data plan, opening the edition and tapping once to the Book I title page costs about 11 MB before a word of prose is shown. The ~100 live plates total about 200 MB.
homer.evidence: Measured at 390x844 (DPR 3): the cover loads title-plate (1.61 MB) and prefetches calypso-glimpse (1.84 MB), 3.4 MB. The Book I splash adds council-of-gods, telemachus-sees-her, athena-at-the-gate and spear-rack (~7.6 MB): about 11 MB unique. Tiles report naturalWidth 2048 and displayed width 70–75px (phone) or 99–106px (desktop).
homer.repro: Open illustrated.html#cover on a phone profile with the network panel open, then tap › once. About 11 MB of JPEG transfers.
homer.fix: Generate derivatives at build time (e.g. 256px tiles, 1024px and 1600px panels, WebP or AVIF plus JPEG). Emit srcset/sizes from build_illustrated.py, use the 256px file for .tp-tiles and cover-size images for the panel, and prefetch only the next scene's appropriately sized file.
verifier_corrections: Framing: the 11 MB is front-loading plus oversized files, not waste. The tile files are the upcoming Book I plates and are reused from cache, and the prose is not blocked by them. The real excess is resolution, since 2048px is served for 70px tiles and a 390–726 CSS-px panel. Minor side note: the splash prefetch branch picks the book's first img block, which is title-plate with splashOnly, even though splash pages never show splashOnly plates.
Per-plate sizes range from 0.96 to 3.15 MB, not 1.5-2.5 MB. There are 101 live plates totalling 207 MB. Everything else is accurate.

Correct the figures: about 3.5MB at #cover, and about 11MB (not 16MB) by the Book I title page. The title should read 'about 11MB'. The preload at :851-855 fetches up to 3 pages ahead, not just the next plate. The tiles reuse plates that the book shows later, so the main savings come from a phone-sized srcset variant for #art-img and a thumbnail for .tp-tiles, not from avoiding bytes that would never be used.

Replace the figures with 3.45MB on cover and 11.0MB cumulative at the Book I title page (6 images), not 6.9MB and 16.3MB. Book directories range from 6.5 to 25.7MB, not 12-24MB. The preload is the next 3 pages (lines 851-856), not just the next plate. Add the root cause in homer-odyssey/data/prepare_plates.py:143-150: every plate is resized, even upscaled, to 2048 and saved at quality=93 with subsampling=0 (4:4:4), which inflates file size. Lower quality and 4:2:0 subsampling, alongside smaller variants, would cut bytes a lot.

homer.title: Illustrated pagination blocks the main thread ~2.7 s twice on every phone load and ~3.9 s on rotation
homer.detail: paginate() measures every sentence of all 24 books (~123k words) with a DOM probe, synchronously. It runs once at inline-script time and again after fonts load, and runs again on any width change. The reader cannot turn a page, tap the picker or change theme until each pass finishes.
homer.evidence: PerformanceObserver long tasks at 390x844 with 4x CPU throttle: [2764, 2577] ms on load (#bk-4) and [2605, 2066, …, 3851] ms including a rotation to 844x390. At 1440x900 with 1x CPU: [631, 723] ms. For comparison, study.html at 4x shows [57, 733, 476] ms.
homer.repro: Open illustrated.html#bk-4 in a phone profile with 4x CPU throttling and tap › right away. Nothing happens for several seconds.
homer.fix: Paginate the current book first and render, then paginate the rest in idle chunks (requestIdleCallback or setTimeout slices), or paginate lazily per book. Cache pages per (viewport, font-loaded) key. Skip the fallback-font pass entirely by awaiting fonts.load() (a short timeout is fine) before the first paginate, which also fixes the reload-drift finding.
verifier_corrections: Line refs are correct (paginate 611-707; initial call 978, font repass 991-996; resize 1022-1030). Also note the ResizeObserver repass at 1003-1012. One nuance: the first pass runs before the first render() (978-980), so it delays first paint (the reader sees nothing yet). The freeze on a page that is already visible comes from the second (font) pass and the rotation pass. The comment at 1015-1016 shows the author knows the cost, but nothing tracks it as open.

My numbers match the finding: [2354, 2555] at 4x on load vs the claimed [2764, 2577], 3774 vs 3851 on rotation, and [704, 548] vs [631, 723] on desktop. Two details to add. First, the first pass runs before the initial render, so a reader sees a late first paint, not a dead › button; the unresponsive-tap symptom comes from the second, font-triggered pass. In the field that pass fires whenever the EB Garamond files arrive, which is usually just after first paint, when readers start tapping. Second, the cost is acknowledged in code comments (lines 985-990 and 1014-1016) but tracked nowhere as an open item.

homer.title: Other transcription errors in the seeds (typos, stray footnote numbers, a merged couplet)
homer.detail: The following errors appear in all readers. Some may come from the PG transcriptions, but the pipeline has no proofing step. (1) Pope Iliad 22.662–663, the book's final couplet, was merged and re-split as 'So spake the mournful dame: her matrons hear, Sigh back her sighs, and' / 'answer tear with tear.' (2) Butler Odyssey has footnote numbers left in the text: 1.25 'mine above all others 10—for', 8.41 'asleep in your ship.” 72', 15.41 'meat and wine.” 137'. (3) Name and word typos: Butler Iliad argument III 'Alexandria, also called Paris' (Alexandrus) and argument IV 'Fandarus' (Pandarus); Pope Iliad 12.426 'Peteus’ son'; Cowper Iliad 7.142 'Pelaus', 14.565 'Atenor'; Pope Odyssey 8.64 'Poutonous', 13.393 'Bebold', 20.1 'devine', argument I 'Mantes', argument XX 'Caesippus'. (4) Pope Odyssey 10.76 and 19.640 use a backtick (`) as an opening quote.
homer.evidence: Found with the digit regex, a scan for verse lines of 60+ characters (Pope 22.662 is the only merged one), and an edit-distance-1 scan of proper names against frequent names. Each hit was checked in context.
homer.repro: homer-iliad/reader.html#bk-pope-22: the last two lines are the broken couplet. homer-iliad/reader.html#bk-butler-4: the argument says 'Fandarus'.
homer.fix: Correct these in the seeds (and in the .md files for the Odyssey). Add parser checks: stray /\s\d+$/ or /\w\d/, verse lines over 60 characters, and backticks.
verifier_corrections: parse_md_seed numbers the backtick lines Pope Odyssey 10.77 and 19.641, not 10.76 and 19.640. The pope.md file lines, 5692 and 11711, are correct. The finding also misses a second 'devine' at homer-odyssey/seeds/pope.md:1607 (Pope Odyssey 3.540, 'Artist devine'). None of these strings are in study.html or illustrated.html, so only the five parallel readers per book are affected, not 'all readers'.

homer.title: Modern translation typography inconsistent between books
homer.detail: Book VIII uses straight double quotes (67) where the other 23 books all use curly “ ”. Book XVIII uses curly apostrophes (18) where every other book uses straight ones. CLAUDE.md describes a 'curly-quote speech conventions' style contract for the subagent-drafted books.
homer.evidence: Per-book quote counts from parse_md_seed(modern.md): book 8 has 67 straight double quotes and 0 curly; the other books have 0 straight and 23–104 curly. Book 18 has 0 straight apostrophes and 18 curly; the other books have 9–44 straight.
homer.repro: homer-odyssey/reader.html#bk-modern-8: the dialogue uses "…" rather than “…”.
homer.fix: Normalise Book VIII to curly double quotes and settle one apostrophe style across all 24 books (then rebuild build.py and build_illustrated.py).
verifier_corrections: Most other books also have a few ’ as the closing mark of nested ‘…’ quotes (for example Book IV has 13 ’ and 15 ‘), so '23 others use straight apostrophes' means 'straight for apostrophes'. Book XVIII is the only book with no straight apostrophes at all.

homer.title: Study transliteration drops capitals on υ-diphthongs and prints the Greek question mark as ';'
homer.detail: When υ follows a vowel, translitWord() rewrites the last emitted vowel with the lowercase diphthong, which loses the capital of a word-initial capital vowel. Names like Οὖτις, Εὔμαιος, Εὐρύκλεια, Εὐρύμαχος and Αὐτόλυκος come out lowercase, in both the line transliteration and the popover. translitLine() also leaves the Greek question mark ';' as ';' and converts the ano teleia '·' to ';', so in the Latin transliteration a question and a colon/semicolon look identical.
homer.evidence: Od. 9.366 'Οὖτις ἐμοί γʼ ὄνομα· Οὖτιν…' → 'outis emoi gʼ onoma; outin de me kiklēskousi'. Popover for Οὖτις shows 'outis'. Od. 23.183 '…θῆκε λέχος; χαλεπὸν…' → '…thēke lechos; chalepon…'.
homer.repro: Open /homer-odyssey/study.html#bk-9 and look at line 366's transliteration.
homer.fix: In the diphthong branch, keep the case of the replaced vowel (capitalize the diphthong if the previous letter was uppercase). Map Greek ';' (U+037E or ';') to '?' and '·' (U+0387/U+00B7) to ';' or ':' consistently in the Latin output.
verifier_corrections: The Greek question mark in this data is the ASCII ';' (U+003B), not U+037E, so the fix has to map U+003B too, as the fix text already mentions. Also affected: the lemma transliteration in the popover, e.g. 'lemma: Οὖτις (outis)'.
