homer.title: Small navigation gaps: 'Back to reader' links drop your book and edition, fullbleed book buttons look enabled but do nothing, invalid hashes stay in the URL
homer.detail: (1) The fullbleed '← Reader', theater '↩ Reader' and pdf '←' links are a static href="reader.html". All formats share the #bk-<ed>-N form, yet moving from, say, Greek Book XII opens the reader at its own saved edition, Book I. (2) fullbleed disables Prev Book only on Book I spread 1 and Next Book only on the last spread of Book XXIV. On Book I spread 4, Prev Book is enabled but its handler checks currentBook > 0 and does nothing; likewise Next Book on XXIV. (3) Invalid hashes (#bk-99, #bk-pope-0) are ignored but stay in the address bar in reader.html, so the URL does not describe the book shown.
homer.evidence: backlink.js: fullbleed, theater and pdf at #bk-greek-12, back link → reader.html shows 'translated by Alexander Pope / Book I'. paged_misc.js: 'Book I spread 4: Prev Book disabled? false -> after click Book I · Spread 4/24'; 'Book XXIV spread 1: Next Book disabled? false -> after click … Spread 1/31'. reader.js: #bk-99 left the hash as '#bk-99' with Book III displayed.
homer.repro: Open homer-odyssey/theater.html#bk-greek-12 and click '↩ Reader': you land on Pope, Book I.
homer.fix: Set the back links' href from the current hash on each navigation (reader.html#bk-<ed>-N). Disable Prev/Next Book on book-number boundaries, or make them jump to the first or last page of the book. Rewrite the hash to the displayed book when it is invalid.
verifier_corrections: The repro is only valid for the Odyssey. #bk-greek-12 is not a valid Iliad hash (that page falls back to Pope 1 on its own), so use #bk-cowper-12 for the Iliad. Sub-point (3): 'Book III displayed' only happens after a hashchange from Book III. On a fresh load the reader shows Book I. Line citations are correct.

homer.title: Study reader passage links are thrown away: #ch-9-100 opens Book I and the hash is overwritten; in-page hash changes are ignored
homer.detail: Every chunk carries an id (ch-<book>-<line>) and the CSS styles .chunk:target, so passage links look intended, and citing a passage (Od. 9.366) is the natural thing to share from a study reader. But init only accepts ^#bk-(\d+)$. Any other hash falls back to Book I, and renderBook() immediately replaces it with #bk-1. Scroll position within a book (up to 55,000px tall in Book IV) never reaches the hash. There is no hashchange listener either: after location.hash='#bk-5' the page still shows the previous book, so URL and content disagree.
homer.evidence: Fresh load of study.html#ch-9-100 gives hash '#bk-1', scrollY 0, Book I. #Od.9.100 gives the same. A same-document navigation to #bk-12 while on Book IX leaves 'IX' displayed.
homer.repro: Open /homer-odyssey/study.html#ch-9-100 in a new tab. It shows Book I, top of page, and the URL becomes #bk-1.
homer.fix: Parse #ch-B-L (and a line form such as #l-B-L): render book B, scroll to the chunk containing L after render, and flash it. Update the hash to the top visible chunk with an IntersectionObserver (replaceState, throttled). Add a hashchange handler.
verifier_corrections: A plain reload does restore the in-book scroll position: after reload, scrollY was back at 20000 through the browser's scroll restoration. So only bookmarks and shared links lose the place, not refresh. The .chunk:target CSS is at study-template.html:100.

homer.title: Odyssey pages take ~8s to show any text on a throttled phone: every format inlines all 6 editions (1.5 MB gzip), and the header shows wrong placeholder text meanwhile
homer.detail: build_content() inlines all 6 editions x 24 books into every format. Odyssey files are 4.4 MB raw / 1.50 MB gzip; Iliad 2.6 MB / 0.96 MB. A view needs one book of one edition (17-49 KB of text). The render script sits after the data, so until the whole payload has downloaded and parsed, no text appears and every button is inert. During that time reader.html shows static placeholder text copied from the Iliad: 'translated by Alexander Pope · 1720 · heroic-couplet verse'. Odyssey Pope is 1725, and the placeholder appears even for #bk-greek-3. Because the data is inlined, switching format (reader → mobile → theater) downloads the same 1.5 MB again; nothing is shared through the cache.
homer.evidence: work/homer-nav/r2/perf.js with a gzip server emulating GitHub Pages (the sandbox server does not compress), CDP Slow 4G (1.6 Mbps, 150ms RTT), 4x CPU, 390x844. Odyssey reader: transfer 1,502,783 B, FCP 380ms (chrome only), first book text 8071ms. Odyssey mobile: first text 8007ms, one 249ms long task. Iliad mobile: 5217ms. Odyssey mobile on 9 Mbps: 2320ms. loadshot.js at ~4s into loading homer-odyssey/reader.html#bk-greek-3: translator-line 'translated by Alexander Pope', caption '1720 · heroic-couplet verse · 24 books'. Edition switch after load is quick (~100-170ms).
homer.repro: In Chrome DevTools set 'Slow 4G' and CPU 4x slowdown, open lib.sadh.app/homer-odyssey/mobile.html: the reading area stays empty for ~8s and the buttons do nothing.
homer.fix: Emit per-edition (or per-edition-per-book) JSON/JS files under the book directory and fetch the requested one first, prefetching the rest when idle. At minimum, move the data into one shared external editions.js so all formats reuse the cached copy. Replace the static header placeholders with neutral text (or hide them until the first render).
verifier_corrections: Context the finding omits: the self-contained single-file design with inline data is a documented house convention (AGENT_README.md:9-10, README.md:117 'no external fetches', homer-iliad/CLAUDE.md:7 and Architecture step 1). The proposed external-data fix therefore needs a docs change too. It does have precedent: vedas/rigveda.html:228 already fetch()es per-mandala JSON. The wrong placeholder year is only in homer-odyssey/data/reader-template.html:442. :441 is a generic default that is correct whenever the default edition (pope) is active. The ~8s figure depends on Slow-4G plus 4x CPU emulation; the finding's own 9 Mbps run shows ~2.3s. Related docs drift: homer-odyssey/CLAUDE.md says '5 editions, not 3', but the build embeds 6 (murray was added). homer-odyssey/study.html (5.6 MB raw, 1.36 MB gzip) has the same pattern.

The placeholder is at homer-odyssey/data/reader-template.html:441-442; the correct Pope Odyssey year is 1725 (the template's own line 370 says so). Treat page weight as a known trade-off of the single-file convention. Any fix beyond neutral placeholder text needs the maintainer to relax AGENT_README's single-file rule, so the finding should say so rather than present external JSON as a plain fix.

alice.title: pdf-reader hides most of the book on phones and a large share on common laptop screens
alice.detail: splitChapterIntoPages() never measures anything. It assumes 65 characters per line and 32 lines per page, scaled only by zoom, whatever the size of the card. resizePageCard() sizes the card from the viewport, and #pageInner has overflow:hidden, so whatever does not fit is silently cut off. The next page starts at the next block, so the hidden text never appears anywhere. It also ignores the font setting (Mono is much wider), and the page-number label is drawn over the overflowing text.
alice.evidence: Hidden-word sweep over all 121 pages (hidden.js, t_pdfvp.js): 390x844 = 118/121 pages clipped, 59.2% of the book's words invisible; 320x640 = 75.7%; 1366x768 = 107 pages clipped, 8.4%; 1280x720 = 19.2%; 1440x900 and 1920x1080 = 0%. With the Mono font at 1440x900: 97 pages clipped, 6.2%. Page 5 at 390 has scrollHeight 1134 in a 463px card; screenshot shots/pdf-m-p5.png shows the page cut mid-sentence ('but then I wonder what'), with the '5' label over the text. The sandbox serif is Liberation Serif, close in metrics to EB Garamond, and the error is far larger than any font difference.
alice.repro: Open alice-in-wonderland/pdf-reader.html at 390x844 (or on a 1366x768 laptop), go to page 5, and compare its last visible line with the first line of page 6: whole paragraphs in between are missing.
alice.fix: Paginate by measurement, as mobile.html already does: after resizePageCard(), fill a hidden box with the same width, height, padding, font and zoom as #pageInner, one block at a time. Re-paginate on resize, zoom and font change, and keep the reading position by chapter plus block index. Split over-tall paragraphs, or let a page scroll, rather than clip.
verifier_corrections: Add a contributing cause: the phone overrides `#pageInner { padding: 32px 24px }` (line 457, 768px query) and `#pageInner { padding: 24px 16px; font-size: 15px }` (line 466, 600px query) never apply. `.zoom-100 #pageInner { font-size:16px; padding:48px }` (line 364), specificity 1,1,0, out-ranks bare `#pageInner` (1,0,0). This is the same specificity-bug class the old audit fixed in the toolbar, and it narrows the phone text column to about 262px, which makes the clipping worse. The desktop percentages depend somewhat on the font, since EB Garamond does not load here. The phone numbers do not.

The line references are accurate. At 1366x768 I counted 88 clipped pages, not 107 (107 is probably a scrollHeight>clientHeight count), but the 8.4% hidden-word figure matches. The laptop figure is sensitive to the font; a realistic laptop viewport (1366x657) is much worse (34.5%).

alice.title: index.html (the 'Classic Book') drops 5–8% of the text on desktop and 19–30% on phones
alice.detail: paginate() sets the measuring div's width to refPage.offsetWidth, which is the .page-inner box including its 22–30px side padding, and its height to offsetHeight-10, which ignores the 24px top and 34px bottom padding. The real .page-content is therefore 52px narrower and 36–48px shorter than the box the text was measured in. Every full page overflows, and .page-content{overflow:hidden} cuts off the tail; the next page starts at the next paragraph, so those lines and whole paragraphs are lost. Pagination also runs before webfonts load (no fonts.ready), never re-runs on resize or rotation, and there is no phone layout, so a 390px screen gets two 139px justified columns.
alice.evidence: t_idx.js at 1440x900: measure box 600x826 vs real text box 548x778; at 390: 191x770 vs 139x734. Hidden-word sweep: 1440x900 = 6.5% of words hidden (54 whole paragraphs never shown, 56 partly); 1366x657 = 8.0%; 1920x960 = 5.2%; 390x844 = 19.0%; 320x640 = 30.0%. After a resize from 1440x900 to 900x700 a page overflows by 415px. In shots/index-d-s6.png, page 8 ends mid-line on 'Nile On every golden scale!' and page 9 skips the whole 'How cheerfully he seems to grin…' paragraph. In shots/index-m-s5.png, page 6 ends 'which way' and page 7 jumps ahead.
alice.repro: Open alice-in-wonderland/index.html at 1440x900, open the book, pick 'II. The Pool of Tears' and flip to pages 8–9: the bottom line of page 8 is half cut and the next paragraph is missing from page 9.
alice.fix: Measure against the real text box: use the page-content's clientWidth and clientHeight, or append the measuring div inside a hidden clone of .page-inner. Await document.fonts.ready before paginate(). Re-paginate on resize while keeping the chapter and paragraph. Use a single-page spread at 600px and below.
verifier_corrections: My percentages run slightly higher than the finding's: 7.7% vs 6.5% at 1440x900, 9.8% vs 8.0% at 1366x657, 31.2% vs 30.0% at 320x640. This is probably counting method. The title's '5-8% desktop' should read about 5-10%. The fonts.ready claim is inferred from the code and cannot be observed here, because webfonts are blocked in this sandbox.

Line references are correct. The desktop loss depends on font-load timing. With the same font for measuring and rendering it is 5-10% (I got 7.7% at 1440x900 against the finder's 6.5%). If pagination measures in a wider fallback such as Georgia before EB Garamond swaps in, it drops to roughly 0.6-3% on desktop but stays 7-19% on phones. Adding a fonts.ready wait makes the geometry bug more consistent, not less, so the measurement-box fix is the essential part.

alice.title: fullbleed has no keyboard route to jump to a chapter or page
alice.detail: The chapter scrubber is built from <span> elements with click handlers, the TOC entries are <li> elements with click handlers, and the editable page number is a clickable <span>. None has a tabindex or role. A keyboard or screen-reader user can only turn pages one at a time, which is roughly 55 spreads to reach chapter XII. The previous audit converted the theme dots to buttons but left these click-only.
alice.evidence: tabStops() on fullbleed.html#p-10 at 1440x900: Prev, Next, Theme and the 5 theme dots, then back to BODY. The count of focusable scrubber, TOC and page-num elements is 0.
alice.repro: Open fullbleed.html#p-10 and press Tab repeatedly: no chapter numeral, TOC entry or page number ever receives focus.
alice.fix: Render the scrubber items and TOC entries as <button> elements with aria-label 'Chapter N: title' (reader.html's ch-node pattern), and make the page number a <button aria-label='Go to page'>.
verifier_corrections: Worse than stated for the TOC: its <li> entries are not click-only in practice either. The #click-left/#click-right zones (fullbleed.html:484-489, z-index 8) sit on top of them, so a mouse click or tap on a TOC entry flips to the next page instead of jumping (verified at 1440 and 390 in f6toc.js). Rebuilding the entries as <button>s will not fix that unless they are also raised above the click zones, or the zones are disabled on the TOC spread.

The TOC entries are worse than 'click-only': mouse and touch cannot use them either. The #click-left/#click-right zones (z-index 8, lines 484-489) sit on top of them, so a click flips the page instead of jumping to the chapter. Converting the entries to <button> is not enough; the TOC must also sit above the click zones (or the zones must be disabled on spread 2). gibran-prophet/fullbleed.html:1419-1426 has the same span scrubber, which is the same root cause outside Alice.

alice.title: reader.html: Escape throws a ReferenceError and never closes the chapter sidebar
alice.detail: The Escape case calls `themeDropdown.classList.remove('open')`, but themeDropdown has not existed since the dropdown was replaced by dots (commit 9ec1aa0, April). The ReferenceError aborts the handler before closeSidebar() runs. AGENT_README specifies 'Esc to close panels' for reader.html. web-reader.html's equivalent handler works.
alice.evidence: t_reader.js at 1440x900: with the sidebar open, pressing Escape leaves it open (open before and after = true) and throws pageerror 'themeDropdown is not defined', on every Escape press. git blame dates the line to cfbe712 (2026-04-01).
alice.repro: Open reader.html, click the ☰ button, press Escape: the sidebar stays open and the console shows 'themeDropdown is not defined'.
alice.fix: Delete lines 2062–2063, or replace them with `themeWrap.classList.remove('expanded')`.
verifier_corrections: Clarification: Escape does still close the settings panel, because lines 2060-2061 run before the throw. Only the sidebar close (and the theme-button reset) are lost.

alice.title: Invisible controls take keyboard focus: closed sidebars, reader's hidden chapter scrubber, and back-to-top
alice.detail: reader.html: the off-canvas sidebar is hidden only with translateX(-100%) and comes before the top bar in the DOM, so a page's first 12 Tab stops are invisible links at x=-260. The ch-node scrubber adds 12 more buttons at opacity 0, created as buttons nested inside the #back-to-top <button> (nested interactive content). It is revealed only on #back-to-top:hover, with no :focus-within reveal and no touch path, which breaks the AGENT_README baseline. #back-to-top itself is focusable at opacity 0 while at the top of the page. web-reader.html has 12 invisible sidebar links after the settings button. pdf-reader's closed #sidebar is a focusable scroller at x=-180. None of the drawers moves focus into itself when opened.
alice.evidence: tabStops() on reader.html at load: Tab stops 1–12 are a.sidebar-chapter 'HIDDEN [-260,…]'; #sidebar-toggle is only the 13th. After focusing #back-to-top, the next 4 Tabs land on ch-node buttons with op=0. The accessibility snapshot lists the 12 chapter buttons as children of button 'Back to top'. #back-to-top accepts focus at opacity 0. web-reader: Tab stops 7–12+ are sidebar links at x=-300. pdf-reader: div#sidebar receives focus while hidden.
alice.repro: Open reader.html and press Tab once: focus goes to an invisible link offscreen, and it takes 13 Tabs to reach the first visible control.
alice.fix: When a drawer is closed, set `inert` (or `visibility:hidden` after the transition). When it opens, move focus into it and return focus on close. Move .ch-scrubber out of the button into a sibling container, reveal it on :focus-within and via a tap path, and make #back-to-top `visibility:hidden` (not only opacity 0) until .visible.
verifier_corrections: Also add web-reader.html: its #back-to-top is focusable at opacity 0 at the top of the page (Tab stop 19). pdf-reader.html contributes only one invisible Tab stop, the scroller itself, so it is minor compared with reader.html.

Scope addition: web-reader.html's #back-to-top (line 603, CSS 484-512) is also focusable at opacity 0 (Tab stop 19). The pdf-reader instance adds only a single stop, so it is minor. Line citations are accurate.

alice.title: Global key handlers stop Space from activating focused buttons in 6 formats; in theater, Space on Back goes forward
alice.detail: These handlers call preventDefault on Space and the arrow keys wherever focus is, excluding only INPUT/TEXTAREA or nothing at all. A focused button therefore never gets its Space activation: the page scrolls or flips instead. They also ignore modifier keys, so shortcuts such as Alt+Left are swallowed as scroll or flip. pdf-reader, single and index get this right.
alice.evidence: t_space.js / t_rest.js: reader, focused sepia dot + Space: theme unchanged, page scrolls 765px. web-reader, focused Settings + Space: panel stays closed, page scrolls. scroll.html, focused theme button + Space: theme unchanged, page scrolls. fullbleed, focused theme button + Space: theme unchanged, page flips (spread 8 to 9). mobile.html, focused theme button + Space: theme unchanged, page flips. theater, focused '← Back' + Space: moves forward (101 to 102). Enter works everywhere.
alice.repro: Open theater.html#s-100, Tab to '← Back' and press Space: the position goes to 101/102 instead of 99.
alice.fix: At the top of each handler: `if (e.altKey || e.ctrlKey || e.metaKey) return; if (e.target.closest('button,a,input,select,textarea,[role=slider],[contenteditable]')) return;`. Change mobile.html via gen_mobile.py.
verifier_corrections: fullbleed.html has the same 'Back goes forward' problem: Space on #btn-prev ('Previous page') flips forward, from page 17 to 19. Add mobile.html:452 as the generated copy of gen_mobile.py:479. The claim that Alt+Left is swallowed follows from the code (no modifier check) but was not reproduced, because headless Chromium cannot exercise browser accelerators.

The theater numbers differ slightly. From #s-100, Space on Back goes to #s-101 (100/814 → 101/814), where Back should give #s-99. The evidence's '101 to 102' and the repro's '101/102' are off by one, but the behaviour is as described. The mobile.html instance is at mobile.html:452 (generated from gen_mobile.py:479).

alice.title: No Alice format honours prefers-reduced-motion
alice.detail: The AGENT_README accessibility baseline requires honouring prefers-reduced-motion. None of the 9 Alice files has the media query, while Meditations, Prophet and others do. Motion that always plays: 3D page-flip overlays (700ms in fullbleed, 600ms in index and mobile), the infinite 'Click to open' pulse on index, card slides in single, passage fades in theater, and smooth scrolling via `html{scroll-behavior:smooth}` plus behavior:'smooth' in reader, web-reader and scroll (a reload restore to chapter 12 animates across about 100k px).
alice.evidence: grep 'prefers-reduced-motion' in alice-in-wonderland/*.html finds 0 matches (other books have it). t_misc.js with reducedMotion:'reduce' (matchMedia reports true): fullbleed still creates a .flip-overlay with transition 'transform 700ms cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1)'.
alice.repro: Enable 'Reduce motion' in the OS, open fullbleed.html#p-10 and press the Right arrow: the full 3D flip still animates.
alice.fix: Add `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce){html{scroll-behavior:auto}*{animation:none!important;transition:none!important}}` to each file (gen_mobile.py for mobile). In JS, check matchMedia and skip the flip overlays (render directly) and use behavior:'auto'.
verifier_corrections: The gen_mobile.py:215 citation is wrong: line 215 is `</style>`. The mobile motion is at gen_mobile.py:128-141 (flip-overlay CSS), 243-244 (FLIP_MS=600) and 401 (inline transition), shipped in mobile.html. The restore scroll on ch-12 covers about 76k px, not about 100k. 'Prophet and others do' overstates coverage: Prophet has it in only 2/7 files, Vedas 3/7, Khayyam 4/6. Alice is the only book with none.

The gen_mobile.py:215 citation is wrong: that line is '</head>'. The mobile flip is at gen_mobile.py:243-244 (FLIP_MS=600, FLIP_EASE) and 401 (overlay transition). The reload restore scrolls about 76k px to chapter 12, not 100k. JS smooth scrolls to fix: reader.html:1888/1916/1951/2026/2042-2055, web-reader.html:652/782/822-835, scroll.html:161/284-294 and pdf-reader.html:696.

alice.title: mobile.html blocks pinch-zoom and has no text-size control
alice.detail: The viewport meta sets `maximum-scale=1,user-scalable=no`, and the page (the dedicated phone format) offers no font-size setting. Low-vision readers on browsers that honour the flag (Android Chrome by default) cannot enlarge the 17px body text, which fails WCAG 1.4.4. No other Alice reader blocks zoom.
alice.evidence: t_rest.js reads meta[name=viewport] as 'width=device-width,initial-scale=1,maximum-scale=1,user-scalable=no,viewport-fit=cover' at both 390 and 320. mobile.html has no size control (bottom bar: page number, scrubber, theme only).
alice.repro: Open alice-in-wonderland/mobile.html on an Android phone and pinch to zoom: the page does not scale.
alice.fix: In the gen_mobile.py TEMPLATE, change the meta to `width=device-width,initial-scale=1,viewport-fit=cover`, then regenerate. Ideally add a text-size cycle that re-paginates and is stored in alice-mobile-prefs.
verifier_corrections: This is not Alice-only. The same user-scalable=no meta is in gibran-prophet/mobile.html, homer-iliad/mobile.html and homer-odyssey/mobile.html, and in the Homer data/mobile-template.html files. The fix should reach those templates too. 'No other Alice reader blocks zoom' is correct.

The same root cause exists outside Alice. gibran-prophet/mobile.html:5 has the identical user-scalable=no meta and also no text-size control (only TOC, theme and prev/next buttons); homer-iliad and homer-odyssey mobile.html have it too (Homer is excluded). Group or cross-reference it with any Prophet finding. The fix location is correct: the gen_mobile.py TEMPLATE, then regenerate.

alice.title: Navigation controls and labels have very low contrast (1.6–3.1:1)
alice.detail: Several formats fade their navigation to a whisper with opacity or dim tokens. The results fall well below 4.5:1 for small text and 3:1 for UI components, for the very controls readers need to find their way.
alice.evidence: t_contrast.js, default themes at 1440x900: fullbleed Prev/Next 1.85:1, scrubber numerals 1.61:1 (10px, opacity .4), page numbers 1.70:1, running header 1.92:1. mobile.html scrubber 2.13:1 (9px), page counter 2.73:1, theme button 2.13:1. single.html Prev/Next and '1 / 12' 2.55:1 (11px). theater (dark-violet) Back/Next, counter and chapter label 3.08:1 at 10–11px. scroll nav numbers 3.34:1. Body text is fine (e.g. theater passage 14.6:1).
alice.repro: Open fullbleed.html#p-5 and try to read the roman-numeral chapter scrubber in the footer.
alice.fix: Keep decorative fades on ornaments only. Give interactive text at least 4.5:1 (drop the opacity multipliers, or darken --text-muted/--dim), and make icon-only controls at least 3:1.
verifier_corrections: The lowest values the tool reports (theater '← Back' 1.17, single '← Prev' 1.28) are the :disabled state at the first chapter, which WCAG exempts. They should not be counted. The fullbleed pattern (.footer-nav button opacity .5, .chapter-scrubber span opacity .4) is shared by aurelius-meditations, gibran-prophet and vedas fullbleed.html (footer at lines ~280/355/333). The root cause is therefore library-wide, not Alice-specific.

Missing locations: the fullbleed running header is at fullbleed.html:203-215 (opacity .55), and scroll.html is cited in the evidence but not in the files list. scroll.html:10 (--dim:#888) and :49 give 3.34:1 on 10px nav numbers and on the size/theme buttons. Mobile's #top-left running title (2.31:1) could also be listed. The page-number and running-header opacities are documented design choices in alice-in-wonderland/CLAUDE.md's Typography section ('Page numbers... accent color at 35% opacity', 'Running headers... 55% opacity'), so the fix should update CLAUDE.md as well. The fullbleed scrubber items are <span>s (line 388), which may also bear on keyboard reachability; that is a separate issue.

alice.title: No semantic chapter headings, main landmark or page-change announcements (reader.html and paginated formats)
alice.detail: In reader.html, the maintained primary reader, the 12 chapter titles are <div class="ch-title">. The only headings are the book <h1> and the sidebar's 'Chapters' <h2>, and there is no <main>, so screen-reader users cannot move between chapters by heading. web-reader.html uses <h2> correctly. fullbleed, index, mobile, theater, scroll and single have no headings at all, and none of the paginated formats has an aria-live region, so page turns and theater segment changes are silent.
alice.evidence: t_head.js heading counts: reader 2, web-reader 14, scroll 0, single 0, fullbleed 0, index 0, mobile 0, theater 0, pdf-reader 1. aria-live elements: 0 in all 9. No <main> in any file.
alice.repro: Open reader.html with a screen reader and use next-heading (H): it goes from the book title to the hidden 'Chapters' heading and stops.
alice.fix: Render chapter titles as <h2> (with the 'Chapter N' label inside or linked via aria-labelledby) and wrap the content in <main>. In paginated formats, give the chapter-header titles heading roles and add a visually hidden aria-live='polite' region announcing 'Page N of M' or the segment number.
verifier_corrections: The cited lines are correct. Minor: web-reader.html also lacks <main>. reader.html partly mitigates the missing headings with a <nav> of real chapter links, and that should be stated.

All cited lines are accurate. Scope is wider than Alice: gibran-prophet/reader.html, aurelius-meditations/reader.html and vedas/reader.html share the same div chapter titles, no <main> and no live region, so the fix belongs in the shared reader pattern/templates and in AGENT_README's accessibility baseline, which currently omits headings, landmarks and live regions. Also note that reader.html's sidebar <nav> of <a> chapter links is an existing, partial screen-reader workaround.

alice.title: Long paragraphs are clipped on short viewports in fullbleed, mobile and theater (theater cuts top and bottom)
alice.detail: The measuring paginators in fullbleed and mobile never split a paragraph. A block taller than a page is forced onto a page on its own and cut off by overflow:hidden. Theater centres each passage in a flex stage with overflow:hidden, so an overlong passage loses both its opening and closing lines and cannot be scrolled. Alice has paragraphs of up to 980 characters, so this bites on small phones and short laptop windows. mobile.html is the phone format, so its small-phone clipping matters most.
alice.evidence: hidden2.js/hidden3.js: fullbleed hides 1.0% of words at 320x640, 0.42% at 360x640, 0.15% at 375x667 and 0.31% at 1024x600. mobile.html hides 1.13% at 320, 0.38% at 360 and 0.07% at 375. theater clips 30 slides at 320x640 (2.7% of words), 14 at 360, 8 at 375x667, and 4–6 at 1024x600, 1280x640 and 1366x657; the worst is slide 11, with 193px hidden at 375x667. Screenshot shots/theater-375-s11.png: the passage starts mid-sentence at the top edge and overlaps the chapter label and theme button.
alice.repro: Open theater.html#s-11 at 375x667 (iPhone SE 2/3): the passage begins mid-sentence ('night, I should think!'), and its opening ('Down, down, down…') cannot be reached.
alice.fix: Split over-tall blocks at line boundaries (for example, measure with Range.getClientRects and carry the rest to the next page), or let a forced page scroll (overflow-y:auto). For theater, use `align-items: safe center; overflow-y: auto` on .stage and reduce the font size for passages taller than the stage. For mobile.html, edit the TEMPLATE in gen_mobile.py and regenerate.
verifier_corrections: The magnitudes in the evidence come from the DejaVu Serif fallback and overstate what readers with EB Garamond see. The claims of 193px hidden on theater s-11 at 375x667 and of 4-6 slides clipped at 1280x640 and 1366x657 are fallback-font artifacts. With a Garamond-like font, s-11 loses about 65px at the top and 65px at the bottom, and 1280x640 and 1366x657 clip only s-11, with no whole word hidden. The visible text at 375x667 starts at 'Dinah'll miss me', not at 'night, I should think!'. The fallback-font numbers do apply when Google Fonts fails to load (the text then falls back to Georgia). Add mobile.html:452-area generated code as the deployed copy of gen_mobile.py:313 (the pagination loop is around mobile.html:283-291).

The quoted percentages were measured with the Liberation Serif (Times) fallback, which sets wider than EB Garamond. With the real font, fullbleed and mobile probably do not clip at 375x667. They still clip at 320-360px widths, at 1024x600 (fullbleed), and on phones whose visible height is cut by browser chrome (for example 375x553). Theater clips across small phones and short laptop windows under either font. Minor: fullbleed's 'force it' branch (lines 729-736) and mobile's `if (i === si) i++` are unreachable. alice.title: fullbleed desktop page flips never update the URL hash, so reload or bookmark loses your place
alice.detail: The hash is written only inside renderSpread(). On desktop, flipForward() and flipBackward() update the DOM themselves and call updateIndicator(), never renderSpread(), so the hash freezes at the last jump. This is the same bug fixed in Prophet's fullbleed in commit e5db2c2 ('hash tracks desktop flips' via writeHashForSpread), never ported to Alice. The previous audit listed Alice's fullbleed as hash-compliant, and alice CLAUDE.md and todo both say '#p-N hash'.

From renderSpread(10), which wrote #p-15, a click-zone flip to spread 11 (page 17) leaves the hash at #p-15. On phones renderSpread runs on every flip, so mobile is fine (#p-50 to #p-51 after a swipe).
alice.repro: Open fullbleed.html at 1440x900, click the cover, press the Right arrow 10 times and reload: you are back on the title page.
alice.fix: Port Prophet's writeHashForSpread(): move the hash block out of renderSpread() into a helper and call it after the flip lands, in the inner setTimeout of both flipForward and flipBackward.
verifier_corrections: Minor gap: goToChapter, the TOC, the page editor and the resize handler all go through renderSpread and do update the hash, so the hash is only stale after arrow, button, click-zone or swipe flips on desktop. Status 'new' is right: the old audit listed Alice fullbleed as hash-compliant, but never claimed to have fixed the flip path.

alice.title: fullbleed page-number editor jumps one spread short; typing 1 opens the Contents page
alice.detail: On desktop, commit() maps page to spread with `ci===0 ? 2 : 3 + Math.floor((ci-1)/2)`. The hash-restore code (line 1423) correctly uses `3 + Math.floor((ci+1)/2)`, the inverse of contentIndexForSpreadLeft/Right. The editor's formula is always one spread early, so the requested page is never shown. This is the same off-by-one fixed in Meditations' fullbleed. CLAUDE.md documents the editable page number as a feature.
alice.evidence: t_fullbleed.js at 1440x900, starting from pages 20–21 and typing a target: 1 goes to the Contents spread (#s-2); 2 and 3 go to page 1; 50 and 51 go to pages 48–49. On mobile, typing 50 correctly shows page 50.

alice.fix: Use the same mapping as the hash restore: `currentSpread = ci === 0 ? 3 : 3 + Math.floor((ci + 1) / 2)`, and share one pageToSpread() helper between both call sites.
verifier_corrections: The same off-by-one also exists in gibran-prophet/fullbleed.html:1491-1494 (identical formula, confirmed in the browser: typing 30 shows pages 28-29), so it is not unique to Alice and the fix should cover both. alice.title: Arrow/Space keys inside fullbleed's page-number box flip the page and permanently freeze navigation
alice.detail: The document keydown handler flips on ArrowRight/ArrowLeft/Space without checking the event target. While the page-number <input> is open, pressing Left to move the caret (or typing a space) starts a flip. When the flip lands, updateIndicator() runs `document.getElementById('page-num').textContent = …`, but #page-num has been replaced by the input, so it throws. `busy = false` comes after that call, so busy stays true and every flip, button, click zone and chapter jump is ignored until reload. Because the desktop hash is stale, the reload also loses the reader's place.
alice.evidence: t_pnum.js at 1440x900 on #p-20: click the page number, press ArrowLeft, and the page flips (spread 13 to 12) with pageerror 'Cannot set properties of null (setting 'textContent')' and busy=true. After Escape, two ArrowRight presses and a click on Next, the spread is still 12 and busy is still true. On mobile the same error is thrown but nothing locks, because the mobile path does not use busy.
alice.repro: Open fullbleed.html#p-20 at 1440x900, click the '21' page number, press the Left arrow, then press Escape and try to turn pages: nothing responds.
alice.fix: In the global keydown handler, return early when e.target is an INPUT/TEXTAREA/SELECT or contentEditable. In updateIndicator(), guard a null #page-num. Reset busy in a try/finally inside both flip timeouts.
verifier_corrections: For the ArrowLeft repro, the busy reset that is skipped is flipBackward's, at fullbleed.html:1277-1281, not only 1174-1178. Cite both. Two related defects I saw while checking (separate root causes, not part of this finding): (1) the stale desktop hash affects every flip, not just this freeze, because flipForward and flipBackward never call renderSpread. (2) The page-number commit formula at fullbleed.html:1480-1482, `3 + Math.floor((ci - 1) / 2)`, is not the inverse of contentIndexForSpreadRight/Left, so it lands one spread early. Typing 21 and pressing Enter shows pages 18/19, and Escape moves the reader back one spread.

Add the flipBackward completion timeout (fullbleed.html:1276-1281) to the cited lines; the ArrowLeft repro goes through that path, not 1174-1178. The freeze applies to flips, buttons, click zones and the scrubber. The page-number input still navigates, because renderSpread ignores busy, so it is a workaround. The claim about losing the place on reload belongs to a separate bug: desktop animated flips never call history.replaceState. Related, separate root cause: commit() maps a page to `3 + floor((ci-1)/2)` (lines 1484-1485), which is one spread earlier than init's `3 + floor((ci+1)/2)` (1427-1428). So Escape ('cancel') on page 21 moves the reader to page 19, and typing 50 lands on page 49.

The same map feeds buildTOC(), so on phones the TOC shows desktop-formula page numbers for chapters that start on the unpadded mobile page list. The George Long English is keyed to the Leopold (Greek) numbering, but in long runs it belongs to a different meditation. reader.html shows the wrong English, and so do mobile.html, theater.html and pdf-reader.html, which render from the same JSON. The Greek toggle, sentence cross-highlighting, the detail panel (modern English + notes) and #m-B.N deep links all build on this pairing. The runs I checked by hand are 4.4–4.51, 5.32–5.36, 6.45–6.59, 7.37–7.75, 8.22–8.61, 9.29–9.42, 10.3–10.38, 11.7–11.39 and 12.4–12.36: about 260 passages, roughly 54% of the book. Books 1–3 are fine. In Books 4, 6 and 7 the annotations were written against the shifted English, so the English and the modern English agree with each other but not with the Greek. In Books 8–12 the annotations follow the Greek, so the English disagrees with both. Side effects: (a) 6.59 and 12.16 render as empty passages. Their English is shown one slot earlier. The note on 6.59 then wrongly tells readers the Greek 'has no corresponding Long translation … may represent a variant or duplicate'. (b) 55 of 159 proper-noun tooltips are never injected, because the name is not in the English shown for that number (e.g. 8.25 Lucilla, Verus, Faustina, Hadrian). (c) 11.39 carries 17 Long passages (long_nums 39–55) in one block. Root cause: parse_long_xhtml gives each

a number by counting paragraphs. Verse quotations that Standard Ebooks sets as separate paragraphs therefore become numbered passages of their own. Examples: 12.4 'All round, and in its joyous rest reposing;', 11.7 'Me and my children if the gods neglect', 7.37 'It is not right to vex ourselves at things', 5.32 'Never has wronged a man in deed or word.'. The last segment is numbered purely sequentially (lines 340-343), so every passage after that point shifts. The docs present this as '484/486 aligned', and the index advertises the Greek toggle.
meditations.evidence:
Examples from aurelius-meditations.json. 12.15: EN 'How ridiculous and what a stranger he is…' (Long 12.13), Greek 'ἢ τὸ μὲν τοῦ λύχνου φῶς…' (the lamp), modern English 'Does the light of a lamp shine…'. 6.57: Greek 'Ἰκτεριῶσι τὸ μέλι πικρὸν…' (jaundice/honey), EN 'No man will hinder thee from living according to…' (= Greek 6.58). 8.22: Greek 'Πρόσεχε τῷ ὑποκειμένῳ…' ('Attend to the matter before thee'), which appears as EN under 8.23. 4.4: Greek 'Εἰ τὸ νοερὸν ἡμῖν κοινόν' ('If our intellectual part is common'), which appears as EN under 4.5. Checks run: word overlap between English and modern English flagged 135 passages (Books 8–12). A Greek-keyword→English matcher flagged 198. Hand checks of ~35 passages confirmed the run boundaries. In the browser, mobile.html#m-12.15 with Greek and notes on shows three different meditations (screenshot work/meditations/shots/mobile-mis-12.15.png). reader.html 12.14 shows EN 'With respect to that which happens conformably to nature…' beside Greek 'Ἤτοι ἀνάγκη εἱμαρμένης…' (shots/reader-desktop-12.15.png). pdf-reader at 320px shows the same (shots/pdf-reader.html.s.png). reader.html 6.59 .med-main innerHTML is '

' (shots/reader-desktop-6.59.png).
meditations.repro: Open lib.sadh.app/aurelius-meditations/mobile.html#m-12.15 and turn on Αα and i. Or open reader.html, turn on Γγ, scroll to Book 12 §14–15 and open the detail panel. The English, the Greek and the 'Modern English' are three different meditations.
meditations.fix:
Re-key Long by the source's own per-passage containers/ids, not by counting

. Verse lines and multi-paragraph passages must be folded into their passage. Assert the paragraph count equals the passage count per book, and fail loudly on mismatch. Regenerate aurelius-meditations.json. Re-key (shift) the Book 4/5/6/7 annotation ranges that were written against the shifted English, and rerun the sentence-align generators. Correct the 6.59 note. Add a validation step, e.g. the length-ratio/keyword check used here, and update CLAUDE.md/todo '484/486 aligned'. Until then, consider hiding the Greek toggle for Books 4–12.
verifier_corrections: Scope: the annotations follow the shifted English in Books 4, 5, 6 AND 7, not only 4, 6 and 7. Book 5 does too: 5.32 modern English 'Never has wronged a person...' and 5.33 'Call to mind how many things...' both match the shifted English, not the Greek. Books 8-12 follow the Greek. The 6.59 note is at leopold-books-04-06.json line 1144 (the entry is around 1142). Of the 55 proper-noun tooltips that never get injected, a few are not caused by the shift: 2.13 Monimus, and 5.8/6.43 'Aesculapius' against Long's 'Æsculapius' spelling. The large majority (8.25, 8.31, 8.37, 9.29, 10.x, 11.x, 12.27) are caused by the misalignment.

Root cause, stated precisely: SE's p-ids are paragraph positions, not passage numbers, so every

gets its own number. That covers verse

lines and also plain continuation paragraphs with no marking; Book 4, for example, has no verse at all, and there Long 4.3 is split into 'Men seek retreats…' and 'This then remains…'. There is also an extra defect: the regex at collect_texts.py:285-287 matches only

or

, so Book 12's

is dropped. The second half of Long 12.3 ('and if thou shalt strive to live only what is really thy life…') therefore appears in no reader; grep finds 0 hits in the JSON, reader.html and mobile.html. Annotations that follow the shifted English are not limited to Books 4, 6 and 7. They also appear in Book 5 (5.32 and 5.33 match the EN, not the Greek) and in parts of Book 10 (10.5). Of the 55 proper-noun misses, about 5 are not caused by alignment: spelling differences (Æsculapius at 5.8 and 6.43, Mæcenas at 8.31, Baiæ at 12.27) and an annotation error (Monimus at 2.13, which belongs to Leopold 2.15).

meditations.title: None of the six reader links on the Meditations landing page can be clicked or tapped
meditations.detail: The 'Available readers' page of the landing book (spread 3, #p-3) lists reader, reader-casaubon, fullbleed, mobile, theater and pdf-reader. The absolutely positioned .flip-zone divs (z-index:40, each covering half the book, 30%/70% on phones) sit above the page content. Every click or tap on a reader link hits the flip zone instead. The page turns (forward on the right half, backward on the left) and the reader never opens. Only keyboard users, who can Tab to a link and press Enter, get through. A reader who arrives from the root catalog's 'Classic Book' link cannot reach any reader from here; the only way out is Back.
meditations.evidence: elementFromPoint at the centre of all 6 a.reader-link returns #zone-right at 1440, 390 and 320 widths. A raw mouse.click on 'Scrolling Reader' at 1440 went to index.html#p-4 (flipped forward). A touchscreen.tap at 390 went to #p-2 (flipped back). Keyboard focus + Enter navigates to reader.html. Injecting `.info-content a{position:relative;z-index:45}` makes a tap open theater.html. Screenshots: work/meditations/shots/index-p3.{d,m,s}.png.
meditations.repro: Open aurelius-meditations/index.html, click through to the 'Available readers' page (#p-3), click 'Scrolling Reader'. The page flips instead of navigating.
meditations.fix: Put the page content above the flip zones: e.g. `.info-content a{position:relative;z-index:45}` (verified), or have the zones ignore clicks that land on a link (`if (e.target.closest('a')) return;` with the zones under the content).
verifier_corrections: Minor: a tap at the link centre on a 390px phone flips forward to #p-4, not back to #p-2. The links sit inside the right 70% zone on phones, so which way it flips depends on where the tap lands. The listed line ranges are correct (CSS 237-243, zones 496-497, links 604-629, handlers at 879-880).

The line numbers are right. The finding says a tap at 390 goes back to #p-2; in my run the tap landed in zone-right and went forward to #p-4. Which way it flips depends on where the tap lands (the zones are 30% and 70% wide). Either way, the link never opens.

meditations.title: Invisible controls stay in the keyboard tab order (closed sidebar, hover-only scrubber, closed mobile sheets)
meditations.detail: In reader.html and reader-casaubon.html the closed #chapter-sidebar is hidden with transform only. Its 12 <a href='#ch-N'> links are the first 12 tab stops on the page, at x=−260 with focus rings off-screen, and the sidebar scroller itself also takes focus. The 12 .ch-node scrubber buttons nested in #back-to-top are revealed only on `#back-to-top:hover`, with no :focus-within, so keyboard focus sits on opacity:0 buttons. Nested inside a <button>, they are also flattened for assistive tech. In mobile.html the closed book and theme sheets use transform only, so 17 buttons stay focusable inside aria-hidden='true' dialogs (the aria-hidden-focus problem). CLAUDE.md already records the fix for the PDF sidebar (visibility:hidden), but it was not applied to these drawers.
meditations.evidence: Tab walk from page top in reader.html (desktop and phone): the first 12 focus targets are sidebar-chapter at x=-260, visible=false; the 13th is the sidebar toggle. Tab walk past the last detail button: back-to-top, then 12 ch-node with .ch-scrubber opacity 0, then the sidebar nav, then sidebar links again. mobile.html: 17 focusable buttons with an [aria-hidden=true] ancestor at 1440, 390 and 320. theater/pdf: 0.
meditations.repro: Load reader.html and press Tab. Focus disappears for 12 presses before reaching the ☰ button. In mobile.html, press Tab past the bottom bar: focus enters the hidden sheets.
meditations.fix: Add `visibility:hidden` (with the transition-delay trick already used in pdf-template) or `inert` to #chapter-sidebar and .sheet while closed, and remove it on open. Add `#back-to-top:focus-within .ch-scrubber{opacity:1;pointer-events:auto}` and move the scrubber out of the <button>, e.g. make them siblings in a wrapper.
verifier_corrections: Minor inaccuracies. At 390x844 (isMobile) the first Tab from load went to the first Details button, not to the sidebar links; the links were still in the order and were reached after wrap-around. 'The sidebar scroller itself also takes focus' was not observed. The reader.html lines cited (7820-7830, 7934-7948) are the JS that builds the links and nodes. The hiding CSS is at reader.html:134-142 and 506-519, the same as reader-casaubon. The generated mobile.html (lines 59, 102-106) is affected as well as data/mobile-template.html. The theme dots at opacity 0 in the top bar are fine, because .theme-wrap:focus-within reveals them.

Lines are correct. Drop or soften 'flattened for assistive tech': Chromium exposes the 12 nested buttons as separate buttons, and the real issue is invalid nesting plus focus on invisible controls. Add one instance: #back-to-top itself (opacity:0; pointer-events:none until .visible, reader-casaubon.html:493-503) is an invisible tab stop near the top of the page. Also cite the AGENT_README accessibility-baseline rule on :hover/:focus-within as the convention the scrubber breaks. Fix goes in reader-casaubon.html and data/mobile-template.html, then rebuild reader.html/mobile.html.

meditations.title: Space on a focused button scrolls/turns the page instead of pressing the button
meditations.detail: Each format's document keydown handler calls preventDefault() on ' ' and then scrolls or advances, without checking whether a button, link or control has focus. Space is the standard way to activate a button, so keyboard users who press it on Γγ, a Details icon, a theme dot or the book-list button move away from what they were reading instead. Enter still works. On desktop mobile/theater, Space also cannot scroll a long passage.
meditations.evidence: reader: focus #greek-btn, Space → data-greek stays undefined and the page scrolls 765 px. Space on a .med-detail-btn → details not opened; Enter → opened. mobile: Space on #greek-btn → aria-pressed false and hash moves #m-4.3→#m-4.4; Space on #toc-btn → sheet not opened, #m-4.5. theater: Space on the sepia dot → theme stays dark-violet, passage advances. fullbleed: Space on the dark-blue dot → theme unchanged, page flips.
meditations.repro: Tab to any button in these pages and press Space.
meditations.fix: At the top of each handler, return early when `e.target.closest('button,a,input,select,textarea,[contenteditable]')` or when e.altKey/ctrlKey/metaKey is set (this also stops the handlers from swallowing Alt+Left/Right, the browser's back/forward shortcuts). Rebuild the templated files.
verifier_corrections: pdf-reader.html is not affected: its handler does not bind Space and also skips SELECT. The mobile.html and theater.html built files have the same line numbers (190 and 132) as their templates. The Alt+Left/Right point is plausible from the code but I did not reproduce it.

Line refs are correct (mobile.html:190 and theater.html:132 match the templates). Add #sidebar-toggle and fullbleed's chapter-scrubber buttons to the affected-controls list; on the scrubber, Space goes one page forward instead of to the chosen Book. Fix in reader-casaubon.html (template for reader.html), then rebuild.

meditations.title: fullbleed.html ignores prefers-reduced-motion: 3D page-flip always animates
meditations.detail: AGENT_README's accessibility baseline requires honoring prefers-reduced-motion. fullbleed.html has no reduced-motion rule at all (grep count 0; every other Meditations page has one). Every page turn on desktop runs a 700 ms rotateY 3D flip set inline from JS, so even a CSS media query would not stop it.
meditations.evidence: `grep -c prefers-reduced-motion fullbleed.html` returns 0. Flip code sets `overlay.style.transition = 'transform ' + FLIP_DURATION + 'ms …'` unconditionally, with a 700 ms setTimeout.
meditations.repro: Enable 'Reduce motion' in the OS, open fullbleed.html on desktop and press →.
meditations.fix: `const reduce = matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches;` and in flipForward/flipBackward skip the overlay and call renderSpread directly (as the mobile path already does) when it is true.
verifier_corrections: The statement that a CSS media query cannot stop the flip is incorrect. An `!important` transition-duration rule, as in gibran-prophet/fullbleed.html:563-570, overrides the inline transition; either that or the JS matchMedia skip is a valid fix. Same root cause outside Meditations: alice-in-wonderland/fullbleed.html and vedas/fullbleed.html also contain 0 prefers-reduced-motion rules. Alice has the same FLIP_DURATION/rotateY flip code.

The detail's claim that 'even a CSS media query would not stop it' is inaccurate. An author !important rule overrides the inline, non-important transition. gibran-prophet/fullbleed.html:563-569 already uses `transition-duration:0.01ms !important`, and that alone would remove the motion, though the 700 ms busy/setTimeout delay would remain. The proposed JS fix (skip the overlay and call renderSpread) is still the cleaner option. The flip runs only above 768 px wide (isMobile at line 962). The same gap exists outside this book's scope in alice-in-wonderland/fullbleed.html (the pattern source) and vedas/fullbleed.html.

meditations.title: reader.html Greek text (486 blocks) and landing-page Greek have no lang attribute
meditations.detail: assemble-reader emits `<div class="med-greek">` without lang, so all 486 Greek blocks in the flagship reader are exposed as English. Screen readers read Koine Greek with English letter-to-sound rules, and font/hyphenation selection uses the wrong language. The three JS formats already set lang="grc", and AGENT_README calls lang marking 'critical in the multilingual readers'. The landing page's Greek title and quotations have none either.
meditations.evidence: grep: 486 occurrences of class="med-greek", 0 with lang. mobile/theater/pdf-reader each have lang="grc" on the Greek container. index.html has only lang="en" on <html>.
meditations.repro: Inspect any .med-greek in reader.html, or read the Greek toggle with a screen reader.
meditations.fix: Emit `<div class="med-greek" lang="grc">` in assemble-reader.py:239 and rebuild. Wrap the Greek strings in index.html in `<span lang="grc">`.
verifier_corrections: Add to the detail: the Greek column is hidden by default and appears only when the reader turns on the Greek toggle (reader.html:591 CSS, prefs.greek default off at around line 8002), so the impact falls on screen-reader users who opt in, not on every reader. Scope and line numbers are otherwise accurate. reader-casaubon.html and fullbleed.html contain no .med-greek blocks, so they are not affected. When fixing, lang="grc" on the div is inherited by the transliteration title attributes on the .gw spans (Latin transliteration). Consider lang="grc-Latn" on those if it matters.

Line numbers are accurate: assemble-reader.py:239, and index.html:539, 553 and 580. The scope is a bit wider than stated. (1) reader.html also has 13 inline Greek words outside .med-greek, in the notes and annotations (e.g. 'kaloethes (καλόηθες)', 'τροφεύς', 'κατὰ φύσιν ζῆν'), all with no lang. (2) fullbleed.html (25 Greek runs, e.g. 'εὐπατρίδαι', 'κόσμος', 'συμβαίνειν', 'τοῦτο ἔφερεν ἀυτῷ') and reader-casaubon.html (36 runs, e.g. lines 772, 777, 1446, 1512, 1677 and 1845) have inline Greek inside Casaubon's English with no lang either; the finding does not name these files. The fix should also wrap these inline Greek words in <span lang="grc">, in the annotation data and the Casaubon build or text sources. Severity stays medium only because the main Greek blocks are optional and hidden by default.

meditations.title: Casaubon reader and fullbleed present the 1900 editor's Fronto appendix as part of Book XII; 3 Casaubon passages left unannotated
meditations.detail:
After Book XII's last meditation, reader-casaubon.html continues with 100 plain paragraphs (34 KB, about 6k words) of Gutenberg #2680 back matter. This is 'APPENDIX', 'CORRESPONDENCE OF M. AURELIUS ANTONINUS AND M. CORNELIUS FRONTO', the Fronto letters and bare footnote lines like '[46] In the war against the Catti.'. It is rendered as Book XII body text with no heading. fullbleed.html (Casaubon) paginates the same material under the running head 'Book XII' (pages ~201–237 on desktop). The sidebar says Book XII takes 73 minutes. Separately, Casaubon VI.23, VI.34 and X.24 are plain

s ('XXIII Consider how many different things…') with no detail button, no number styling and no annotation. The docs/landing page say all 412 are annotated.

In the browser, '#ch-12 .chapter-text > p' count is 100 in reader-casaubon.html, and the first is 'APPENDIX'. Fullbleed CHAPTERS[11].html contains 'Fronto' and 'Catti'. ch-6 has med-num list … XXII, XXIV … XXXIII, XXXV … (XXIII and XXXIV are plain

Cut the appendix out of the Casaubon Book XII source, or give it its own clearly labelled 'Appendix (ed. 1900)' section with real footnotes. Wrap the three stray passages as .med-passage with annotations (assemble-annotations.py handles plain

The line numbers are right. Scope additions from the same root cause (numeral headings missed when the Casaubon text was split into passages): two more passages are fused into their neighbours with the numeral inline, in both reader-casaubon.html and fullbleed.html. They are VI.XXXVIII inside VI.XXXVII (… 'part of the comedy. XXXVIII. Doth either the sun…') and XI.XXXII inside XI.XXXI. The canonical JSON shows the same fusion: XXIII folded into XXII, XXXIV into XXXIII, and the appendix appended to XII.XXVII. The '73 minutes' figure is also inflated for a second reason: reader-casaubon.html:5625 counts .chapter-text textContent, which includes the annotation text for every book, not just the appendix. Separate issue, not covered by finding 0 (which is about reader.html/Long): a crude word-overlap check flagged about 120 Casaubon passages, mostly in Books VIII–XII. Six spot-checks all show another passage's Modern English/Notes: VI.II, VIII.X, IX.X, IX.XV, XI.XXIII, and XII.XXVII, which shows the annotation for 'In writing or reading…'. meditations.title: pdf-reader: the page card does not grow with its content, so text spills onto the grey viewer background on most pages
meditations.detail: The .page 'sheet' is a flex item in the column flexbox #viewport, which has a fixed height. Its default flex-shrink:1 lets it shrink to its min-height (64vh), while the passage, Greek, modern English and notes overflow below the white card onto --viewer-bg. The card then looks cut off mid-text. Secondary text on the viewer background is below AA contrast in the default theme.
meditations.evidence: Rendering all 486 pages and comparing page.scrollHeight with clientHeight: 173/486 pages overflow at 1440×900 and 367/486 at 390×844 (e.g. 1.6: box 770 px, content 1205 px). Screenshot work/meditations/shots/pdf-overflow.d.png shows passage 4.3 continuing below the white card. Contrast of --text-secondary #65707a on light-purple --viewer-bg #c8c4bc is 2.91:1. With `.page{flex-shrink:0}` injected, overflowing pages drop to 0 on both viewports.
meditations.repro: Open pdf-reader.html#m-4.3 (or almost any passage on a phone) and scroll down. The white page ends and the text continues on grey.
meditations.fix: `.page{flex-shrink:0}` (or `flex:none`) in data/pdf-template.html, then rebuild with build_pdf.py.
verifier_corrections: Mechanism: the card does not shrink to its min-height (64vh). It shrinks to the #viewport content-box height (e.g. 770px at 1440x900), with 64vh only as the lower bound. The counts are 174/486 at desktop (not 173) and 367/486 at 390px, and all 486 pages overflow at 320px.

At 1440 I counted 174/486, not 173. The same flex pattern (column-flex #viewport plus .page{min-height:60vh}, no flex-shrink) exists in khayyam-rubaiyat/pdf-reader.html:59-64, and its first page already overflows at 320x640. That is outside this book, but it is probably the same root cause. The low-contrast point applies only to secondary text (Greek, detail, footer) once it spills onto the viewer background. The main text stays readable at 6.44:1.

meditations.title: pdf-reader on phones: Greek toggle removed, book select squeezed to a chevron, theme dots off-screen at 320px
meditations.detail: The ≤768px media query hides #greekBtn along with the zoom controls. Greek cannot be turned on or off in pdf-reader on a phone; a desktop 'greek:true' pref carried to the phone cannot be turned off there. The remaining toolbar leaves the 'Choose book' <select> 52 px wide at 390 (it renders as 'Bo') and 18 px at 320. At 320 the Dark violet and Dark blue theme dots render past the right edge and cannot be tapped.
meditations.evidence: At 390×844: greekVisible=false, zoomVisible=false, bookSelect width 52 px (screenshot shots/pdf-reader.html.m.png shows 'Bo'). At 320×640: select 18 px; off-screen controls theme-dot@314-328 and theme-dot@336-350 (innerWidth 320); screenshot shots/pdf-reader.html.s.png.
meditations.repro: Open pdf-reader.html at 320–390 px wide and try to show the Greek or pick a book/dark theme.
meditations.fix: Keep the Greek toggle on phones and move the theme dots and Greek toggle into a small overflow/settings menu. Give the select a usable min-width, or replace it with the passage sidebar the toolbar already has.
verifier_corrections: The Greek toggle is also lost on tablets in portrait: the breakpoint is <=768px, so an iPad at 768 px wide is affected. A desktop Greek pref cannot follow the reader to another device (localStorage is per device). The real stuck-on cases are a tablet rotated from landscape to portrait, or a narrowed window. The select is squeezed but still usable through the native picker. The unreachable-dot problem is limited to widths below about 355 px (320-class phones).

Three corrections. (1) The phrase 'a desktop greek:true pref carried to the phone' is wrong: localStorage is per device and does not sync. The stranded-pref case is same-device, e.g. turning Greek on with a tablet in landscape and rotating to portrait, or narrowing a desktop window to ≤768 px. (2) The breakpoint is ≤768 px, so iPad portrait (768) also loses the Greek toggle even though there is plenty of room (select 313 px). The problem is not phone-only. (3) The squeezed select is cosmetic: it still opens the native picker with full labels, and the passage sidebar also navigates. Only the dark-theme dots at ≤~350 px and the missing Greek toggle block anything. The off-screen dots appear only below about 350 px; at 390 and 414 all five fit. Workaround: mobile.html has its own Greek toggle. Relevant lines: data/pdf-template.html:93 (the hide rule) and 103-118 (toolbar markup).

meditations.title: fullbleed: any resize or rotation silently changes the page being read, and the book scrubber/TOC then jump to the wrong book
meditations.detail: The resize handler repaginates (the page count changes with viewport height) but keeps `currentSpread` as a raw index. It never recomputes `chapterStartSpreads`, which only init() fills. After a desktop window resize or a phone/tablet rotation, the reader lands on unrelated text. It is worse when crossing the 768px breakpoint, because mobile spreads (ci+3) are reinterpreted as two-page spreads (2s−7). goToChapter() and the TOC page numbers then use stale spread numbers. This is the same class as the vedas fullbleed item in the previous audit, but for Meditations.
meditations.evidence: Desktop at #p-120 ('What they have done, they will still do…'), then resized 1440×900 → 1200×700: 237 → 345 pages, same #p-121 but the text is now 'XXIII Consider how many different things…'. After that resize, clicking scrubber 'XII' lands in Book 8 (getCurrentChapter()=8) and 'VII' lands in Book 5. Phone at #p-100 (Book 5), rotated 390×844 → 844×390: now #p-199 in Book 4.
meditations.repro: Open fullbleed.html#p-120 on desktop, resize the window, then click 'XII' in the footer scrubber.
meditations.fix: On resize, capture the current content page's first block/chapter before repaginating, then map it back to the new pagination. Recompute chapterStartSpreads, e.g. move that loop out of init() into a function called after every paginateAll().
verifier_corrections: Status 'new' is fair, but it should say it is related to the audit's 'Deliberately left open' item (#p-N depends on the viewport) and to the old vedas LOW about crossing 768px. The in-session loss of position and the stale chapterStartSpreads are distinct from that item and can be fixed without the hash redesign. One more instance of the same root cause: init() computes chapterStartSpreads with the desktop formula even in mobile mode. So on a phone, with no resize at all, the TOC page numbers for Books V, VIII and XII are off by one (shown 97/205/341, actual first pages 96/204/340).

Line refs are right (resize 1106-1115, chapterStartSpreads loop 998-1006, goToChapter 944-958; add buildTOC 667-682 for the stale TOC numbers). 'Any resize' should read 'any resize that changes pagination', which in practice is nearly all of them because both height and width feed paginateAll(). On a phone that stays below 768px, goToChapter recomputes from contentPages and is not stale; the stale-scrubber problem is desktop, or after crossing into desktop. Note for the report: the 'same #p-N, different text' part is partly the known left-open viewport-dependence, so the fix to highlight is preserving position across resize and recomputing chapterStartSpreads.

meditations.title: theater.html: no way to jump between books; 486 passages reachable only by prev/next
meditations.detail: The theater controls are prev, position, next, the Greek toggle and theme dots. There is no book list, and the progress bar and position readout are not interactive. Home/End exist only on a keyboard. On a phone, reaching Book XII from the start takes 451 taps; the only shortcut is hand-editing #m-B.N in the URL. meditations.title: reader.html: Greek toggle freezes the page for seconds; 29,190 always-generated .gw::after tooltips dominate the cost
meditations.detail: reader.html is 3.15 MB (600 KB gzipped) with 41,609 DOM nodes, against 8,856 in reader-casaubon. 29,190 of those nodes are .gw word spans. Each carries its transliteration twice (data-t and title), which accounts for 1.37 MB of markup, 424 KB of it the duplicate title attributes. Each span also gets a permanent `::after{content:attr(data-t)}` box, hidden only with opacity:0. When Greek is turned on, all 29k pseudo-elements are created and laid out at once. On a mid-range phone the page freezes for about 10 s after tapping Γγ. A reader who has Greek saved in prefs pays this on every load (loadPrefs applies it at end of body).
meditations.evidence: Measured at CPU 1×: Greek toggle to next paint 2,205 ms on desktop and 1,868–2,451 ms at phone viewport. With `.gw::after{content:none}` injected: 464 / 388 ms, so the pseudo-elements are about 80% of the cost. At 4× CPU throttle, phone viewport: Greek toggle 9,629 ms, opening a single detail panel 982 ms. Full load with the Greek pref off: first interactive frame at 1,415 ms, 871 ms of long tasks. With the Greek pref on: 8,130 ms, 7,610 ms of long tasks, the longest single task 5,898 ms.
meditations.repro: Open reader.html on a phone (or DevTools with 4× CPU throttle) and tap Γγ. The page is unresponsive for several seconds. Reload: the same stall happens during load.
meditations.fix: Generate the tooltip only on demand, e.g. `.gw:hover::after,.gw:active::after{content:attr(data-t)}` with no base `content`, or use one delegated tooltip element positioned on pointerover. Drop the duplicate `title` attribute (−424 KB). Better still, compute the transliteration client-side from the word (the map is ~25 chars) and emit plain text. That removes 29k spans and about 1.3 MB.
verifier_corrections: The magnitudes differ slightly on this machine. The 4x-throttle phone toggle measured about 6.7 s, not about 9.6 s or '~10 s'. The Greek-pref-on load measured about 8.4 s with a longest task of about 5.4 s. The conclusion is unchanged.

Magnitudes: I measured 1.5-1.7 s at 1x CPU and about 6 s at 4x CPU in this headless sandbox, against the finding's 2.2 s and 9.6 s. The '~10 s on a mid-range phone' figure is an extrapolation from the throttle, not a device measurement. The ::after share came to about 50-75% of the toggle cost, not 80%. Drop the duplicate title only if another non-hover route to the transliteration remains, since the code deliberately keeps it as the fallback.

meditations.title: Saved theme/Greek/size prefs apply only after the whole 3 MB reader has parsed: light-theme flash and a layout jump on every load
meditations.detail: loadPrefs() runs in the end-of-body script. The browser paints the book in the default light-purple theme while the rest of the file streams in, then switches theme, Greek columns, font, size and width at the end. A dark-theme reader sees a bright page for the whole download on a phone. Anyone with Greek/size prefs sees the layout reflow under them, and a reader who has started scrolling loses their position.

verifier_corrections: Line refs are correct. Drop the claim that a reader's position is lost on deep links: #ch-N is re-applied on `load`. It is only lost if the user interacts before prefs apply. The 16.8 s timing assumes an uncompressed 3.1 MB transfer; GitHub Pages serves about 600 KB gzipped. The flash is extended by `body { transition: background-color 0.3s }` (reader.html:16). Any early <head> fix must also override the hard-coded `data-theme="light-purple"` on <body>, which the [data-theme] var rules resolve against. reader.html is generated from reader-casaubon.html by data/assemble-reader.py, so the fix belongs in reader-casaubon.html.

The line numbers are right. Four scope fixes. (1) Only reader.html has a Greek pref. reader-casaubon's prefs are theme/font/size/width. (2) The same root cause affects every Meditations format, not just the two scrolling readers. mobile.html:123, pdf-reader.html:132, theater.html:85 and fullbleed.html:1102 read prefs inside the end-of-body inline script, which carries a 0.4–1.2 MB payload. Their chrome paints in the default theme for the whole download: about 6.4 s at 1.5 Mbps for mobile/pdf-reader, and mobile.html is the phone format. (3) It is a repo-wide pattern: no reader in any book applies prefs in <head>. It is worst here because reader.html is 3.1 MB. (4) Fix note: body carries a hard-coded data-theme, so a head script must set the attributes on <html> and the body attributes/CSS must be changed. Otherwise body's light-purple variables still win for all descendants. I did not reproduce the claim that a reader who is already scrolling loses their place. prophet.title: pdf-reader hides large parts of the text: pagination is a fixed character-count estimate, not measured, and overflow is clipped
prophet.detail: splitChapterIntoPages() assumes every page holds 22 lines of 55 characters (scaled only by zoom). It never measures the page card, which resizePageCard() sizes to the viewport (638x826 at 1440x900, 362x468 at 390x844, 292x378 at 320x640). Stanzas are never split. Anything past the card is cut off by `#pageInner .content-area { overflow:hidden }`, so readers never see it: the next page starts with the next stanza. A second effect of the estimate: when the first stanza is judged too big to fit after the chapter header, the code emits a header-only page. As a result, 24 of 28 chapters open on a page showing only the title (for example p.23 'On Giving'). The TOC's .toc-list is also overflow:hidden, so its last entries are cut.

A Playwright script called goToPage(i) for all 113 pages and counted

elements whose top lies below the clip edge. At 1440x900: 11 pages clipped and 49 of 806 paragraphs never visible (p.24 alone hides 17 paragraphs, 983px of overflow).
