Measured numbers are close but not identical: #chapterSelect is 24px at 390 and 18px at 320, and the toolbar scrollWidth at 320 is 375. Also, `#zoomOut + .toolbar-sep` matches nothing, because #zoomLabel sits between them.

prophet.title: reader.html: 28 invisible sidebar links come first in tab order; the chapter scrubber is 28 buttons nested inside a button and shown only on hover
prophet.detail: The closed chapter sidebar is only translated off-screen (translateX(-100%)), with no inert/visibility/aria-hidden. Its 28 links are the first 28 tab stops, before the top bar. Opening it does not move focus in, and closing it does not return focus. The .ch-scrubber (28 <button>s) is built inside <button id="back-to-top">, which is invalid nested interactive content: the accessibility tree shows a 'Back to top' button containing 28 buttons. It appears only on #back-to-top:hover, with no :focus-within or touch path (breaking the house baseline), yet all 28 buttons are focusable while invisible. Back-to-top itself is focusable at opacity 0.
prophet.evidence: Tab walk at 1440x900: stops 1–28 are the off-screen sidebar links, and 65 of the first 70 stops are invisible. `document.querySelectorAll('button button').length` is 28. After pressing Enter on 'Open chapter list', activeElement is still #sidebar-toggle. The accessibility snapshot shows a 'Back to top' button with 28 button children.
prophet.repro: Open reader.html and press Tab repeatedly: focus disappears for 28 presses before reaching the ☰ button.
prophet.fix: Set `inert` (or visibility:hidden) on the closed sidebar and remove it on open; focus the first/active link on open and return focus on close. Move .ch-scrubber out of the button into a sibling, reveal it on :focus-within and via a tap, and make it inert while hidden.
verifier_corrections: Minor: my walk found 66 of the first 70 stops invisible, not 65. The count of 28 invisible sidebar stops before the ☰ button is exact.

The scope is wider than Prophet. The same scrubber-inside-#back-to-top markup with a hover-only reveal is in alice-in-wonderland/reader.html:1732, aurelius-meditations/reader.html:7692 (and reader-casaubon.html), khayyam-rubaiyat/reader.html:884 (plus data/reader-template.html) and vedas/reader.html:742. The transform-only off-canvas sidebar pattern also appears in the meditations, khayyam and vedas readers. The scrubber part is a library-wide root cause and should be fixed in the templates and in each reader, not only in Prophet. The line numbers given are correct.

prophet.title: mobile.html: Tab moves through off-screen chapters and scrolls the pager, so the shown text no longer matches the header or hash
prophet.detail: All 29 slides stay live in the DOM and the accessibility tree. Each .ch-slide is a scroll container with no focusable children, which Chrome makes keyboard-focusable, and the title slide's two links stay focusable from any chapter. When an off-screen slide gets focus, the browser scrolls #pager (overflow:hidden) sideways to reveal it. The chapter on screen then differs from curIdx, the header, the counter and #ch-N. Screen readers also read all 28 chapters linearly.
prophet.evidence: At #ch-3 (390x844), 12 Tab presses: stops 3–4 are the hidden 'Reader'/'Book Spread' links, then slides 1…8. pager.scrollLeft goes 390→1950 and chapter 8's text is shown while the header still reads 'On Marriage 3/28'. Pressing → then shows chapter 9's text under the header 'On Children 4/28' (mob-desync.png).
prophet.repro: Open mobile.html#ch-3 with a keyboard (desktop, or a tablet with a keyboard), press Tab about 10 times, then →.
prophet.fix: In goTo(), set `inert` on every slide except the current one (and on the title slide when it isn't current). Reset #pager.scrollLeft to 0 on scroll. Give the current slide tabindex=0 so keyboard users can still scroll it.
verifier_corrections: Reproduces identically on desktop at 1440x900. index.html:419 links mobile.html for desktop visitors too, so keyboard users there hit it directly.

Minor: in my run, Tab stops 1-2 were the top-bar buttons and the hidden title-slide links were stops 3-4, which matches the finding. The finding cites line 93 for #pager, but overflow:hidden is on mobile.html:91; the #pager rule spans 86-92. Otherwise the scope and lines are correct.

prophet.title: Global keyboard shortcuts steal Space from focused buttons (reader, fullbleed, theater, mobile)
prophet.detail: The document keydown handlers preventDefault Space (and the arrow keys) whatever has focus. Only INPUT/TEXTAREA/SELECT are exempt, and mobile exempts nothing, so Space never activates a focused button and navigates instead. In mobile.html this happens even behind the open aria-modal TOC dialog.
prophet.evidence: reader: Space on the focused 'Open chapter list' leaves the sidebar closed and scrolls the page 0→765. fullbleed: Space on the focused 'Sepia theme' dot flips spread 6→7 and leaves the theme unchanged. theater: Space on the focused '← Prev' at ch10 goes to ch11. mobile: with the TOC open and focus on '3 On Marriage', Space moves the pager ch20→21 behind the dialog, which stays open; Enter works.
prophet.repro: In theater.html#ch-10, Tab to '← Prev' and press Space: you move forward to chapter 11.
prophet.fix: At the top of each handler, return when `e.target.closest('button, a, input, select, textarea, [contenteditable]')`, when a modal/overlay is open, or when ctrl/meta/alt is held.
verifier_corrections: Exemptions are stated imprecisely. reader.html exempts only INPUT and TEXTAREA. fullbleed.html exempts only INPUT and SELECT. theater.html exempts nothing, like mobile.html. Wider scope, from grep only and not checked in the browser: the same kind of document-level Space handler appears in alice-in-wonderland (reader, fullbleed, mobile, scroll, web-reader), aurelius-meditations (reader, reader-casaubon, fullbleed, index), khayyam-rubaiyat (reader, fullbleed, mobile, theater and their data/ templates) and vedas (reader, fullbleed). Only the tag-name exemptions were checked there, none of which covers buttons, so this is probably one suite-wide root cause.

Wording fix: it is not that 'INPUT/TEXTAREA/SELECT are exempt'. Reader exempts INPUT/TEXTAREA, fullbleed exempts INPUT/SELECT, and theater and mobile exempt nothing. pdf-reader and illustrations are not affected, since neither binds Space. The mobile dialog case also covers the arrow keys and j/k, not only Space. The cited lines are correct.

prophet.title: Click-only <div>/<span> controls have no keyboard path: fullbleed chapter navigation, the illustrations lightbox, pdf thumbnails
prophet.detail: fullbleed: the 28-chapter scrubber is <span>s, Contents entries are <li>s, and the editable page number is a <span>. None is focusable, so keyboard users can only page linearly through 80+ pages. illustrations: plates are <div>s with click handlers, so a keyboard user cannot open any plate. The lightbox has no role=dialog, no close button and no focus handling; Escape does close it. pdf-reader: the thumbnails are <div>s (the chapter <select> covers chapter jumps).
prophet.evidence: Counts of tabIndex>=0: fullbleed scrubber spans 0/28, TOC items 0/28, #page-num tabIndex -1. illustrations plates 0/29; with the lightbox open, activeElement is BODY and #lightbox has no role. pdf thumbs 0/113.
prophet.repro: In fullbleed.html with keyboard only, try to reach chapter 20. In illustrations.html (with hosts reachable), try to open a plate with Tab/Enter.
prophet.fix: Use <button type=button> (with aria-label, e.g. 'Chapter 20: On Talking') for scrubber items, TOC entries, the page number, plates and thumbnails. Give the lightbox role=dialog aria-modal=true and a close button, move focus in on open and restore it on close.
verifier_corrections: The pdf-reader thumbnails and TOC <li>s are low on their own: #pageInput, #chapterSelect and Home/End already give keyboard users random access. The weight of this finding is fullbleed (no chapter or page jump without a mouse) and the illustrations plates and lightbox. Also add fullbleed.html:1469 (the page-num click-only handler) as a location.

pdf-reader.html:640 is the Contents-page TOC entry (<li onclick=goToPage>), not a thumbnail. The thumbnails are at pdf-reader.html:769-771. Both are click-only, but pdf-reader keeps working keyboard jump paths (select, page input, Home/End), so its part is low. The fullbleed TOC markup is built at about fullbleed.html:858-866. The severity is carried by fullbleed, where there is no keyboard chapter jump at all, and by illustrations, where plates cannot be enlarged.

prophet.title: mobile.html turns off pinch-zoom and has no text-size control
prophet.detail: The viewport meta sets `maximum-scale=1,user-scalable=no`, and mobile.html (the page phone users are redirected to) has no font-size setting, only TOC and theme. Readers with low vision cannot enlarge the 18px text. iOS Safari ignores the flag, but Android Chrome honours it by default. This fails WCAG 1.4.4.
prophet.evidence: mobile.html line 5 meta content 'width=device-width,initial-scale=1,maximum-scale=1,user-scalable=no,viewport-fit=cover'. The only controls are toc-btn, theme-toggle-btn and prev/next.
prophet.repro: On Android Chrome, open mobile.html and try to pinch-zoom the chapter text.
prophet.fix: Drop `maximum-scale=1,user-scalable=no` (swipe handling does not need it), or add a text-size option to the theme sheet stored in prophet-mobile-prefs.
verifier_corrections: The same root cause also affects alice-in-wonderland/mobile.html:5. That file is generated from alice-in-wonderland/gen_mobile.py:32, has only a theme button and no text-size control, and the fix belongs in the generator. The finding should also cite gibran-prophet/reader.html:444: the UA redirect forces phone readers onto mobile.html, away from reader.html's size setting, which is what makes the missing control a real barrier.

The same root cause (an identical viewport meta) is also in alice-in-wonderland/mobile.html:5, homer-iliad/mobile.html:5, homer-odyssey/mobile.html:5 and homer-iliad/data/mobile-template.html:5 and homer-odyssey/data/mobile-template.html:5. The khayyam, aurelius and vedas mobile pages allow zoom. Caveat for the proposed fix: the swipe handler at mobile.html:557-576 never checks e.touches.length. After the meta is removed, a mostly horizontal pinch can be classed as a swipe, which calls preventDefault and can change chapter on touchend. The handler should ignore multi-touch.

prophet.title: Secondary text and navigation chrome falls well below 4.5:1 contrast in every theme
prophet.detail: Body text passes everywhere, but functional labels are faded with opacity or dim colours: the fullbleed chapter scrubber (the only chapter navigation there), page numbers and running headers; the pdf page number; mobile's chapter counter; theater's 'Chapter N of 28'; the index chapter numerals.
prophet.evidence: Computed contrast (fg blended with opacity over the effective bg), by theme: fullbleed scrubber 1.38–1.93, page number 1.56–1.73, running header 1.62–2.57; pdf page-num footer 1.85–2.52; mobile #ch-counter 2.14–3.33; theater .chapter-num 2.06–3.01; index .ch-num 2.31–3.28.
prophet.repro: Open fullbleed.html in dark-blue and read the footer chapter numbers.
prophet.fix: Drop the opacity (0.35–0.45) on these labels and use --text-muted/--text-secondary values that reach 4.5:1 (3:1 at minimum for large text).
verifier_corrections: Several line refs are off: fullbleed scrubber opacity is at fullbleed.html:395 (rule at :389), page-number opacity at :115 (ok), running-header opacity at :217. The pdf footer opacity is at pdf-reader.html:456, not :463 (:463 is .nav-zone). mobile #ch-counter is at mobile.html:178-179, not :167. theater .chapter-num colour var(--dim) is at theater.html:132. index .ch-num opacity is at index.html:302 (rule at :297). Theater's problem is the dim --dim token, not opacity.

prophet.title: theater on touch: tapping to reveal the hidden controls also advances a chapter
prophet.detail: The controls auto-hide after 2 s. On touch the only way to bring them back is to tap the stage, and the stage click handler calls go(1). So each attempt to reach ← Prev or the theme dots skips a chapter, and a reader who taps while reading loses their place.
prophet.evidence: At 390x844 and at 320x640, open #ch-3 and wait for the controls to hide. A single tap on #stage gives #ch-4 'On Children' with the controls visible.
prophet.repro: On a phone, open theater.html#ch-3, wait 3 s, tap the text once: chapter 4 opens.
prophet.fix: In the stage click handler, if the controls were hidden (or the pointer was touch), only show them. Advance via swipe or the Next button, or limit tap-to-advance to the right third of the stage.
verifier_corrections: 'The only way to bring them back is to tap the stage' is wrong: any touch, including a scroll or drag, reveals the controls without advancing (theater.html:479). The real cost is the reset scroll position: all 28 chapters overflow a phone screen and render() sets scrollTop=0, so one tap loses the reader's place within a long chapter. Tap-to-advance also exists in aurelius-meditations/theater.html:129, khayyam-rubaiyat/theater.html:549 and vedas/theater.html:115; whether those auto-hide their controls the same way was not checked.

Scope: khayyam-rubaiyat/theater.html:550-562 has the same pattern (a stage click that always calls go(1), plus touchstart->showControls with a 2.4 s auto-hide), and so do homer-iliad/theater.html:262-264 and homer-odyssey/theater.html:265-267. A tap on the bottom strip also advances, because hidden controls are translated off-screen, so even aiming at the Prev position skips forward.

prophet.title: Touch targets well under 40px on primary phone navigation (fullbleed footer, mobile top bar, pdf toolbar)
prophet.detail: The house baseline asks for 40px interactive targets on touch. The fullbleed phone footer is now reachable, but its controls are tiny: prev/next 26x24, theme button 24x24, and the chapter numbers 6x15px in a scrolling row. mobile.html (the phone format) has a 22x28 TOC button, an 18x26 theme button and 44x36 prev/next. Every pdf-reader toolbar button is 27x23 and the select is 19x25. The narrow theme-dot hit areas are a separate known open item in todo.md.
prophet.evidence: Measured bounding boxes of visible controls at 390x844: fullbleed 31 controls under 40px (btn-prev 26x24, scrubber '1'…'28' 6x15); mobile toc-btn 22x28, theme-toggle-btn 18x26, prev/next 44x36; pdf sidebarToggle 29x25, prev/next/zoom 27x23, chapterSelect 19x25.
prophet.repro: On a 390px phone, try tapping chapter '7' in fullbleed's footer row, or the ◐ button in mobile.html.
prophet.fix: Give these buttons min-width and min-height of 40–44px (padding, or a transparent ::before hit area as the baseline suggests). For the fullbleed scrubber, add horizontal padding so each number gets a 32–40px slot (the row already scrolls).
verifier_corrections: Add that #chapterSelect at 600px or narrower (pdf-reader.html:518) collapses to about 19px wide and shows no chapter text on phones: an unreadable control, not just a small one. Cited lines are right, though the fullbleed.html:390 styles live in the .chapter-scrubber span rule at 390-399. Arguably this is 'fix incomplete' more than 'new': .project/todo.md marks the a11y sweep done with '40px-tall hit areas', but the footer, top-bar and toolbar buttons were not covered.

The cited lines are correct. The fullbleed theme button rule is at fullbleed.html:472. Two related defects I observed are separate root causes and are not covered by this finding. (1) At 320x640 the pdf-reader toolbar overflows (#toolbar scrollWidth 380 vs 320, overflow visible), so the dark-violet and dark-blue theme dots render at x=337 and x=356, off-screen and unreachable. (2) #chapterSelect is crushed to 18-19px wide on phones by min-width:0 in a flex row (pdf-reader.html:91), so its label is invisible, not merely a small target.

prophet.title: reader.html #ch-N restore lands on chapter 1: the observer overwrites the hash before restoreHash() reads it
prophet.detail: On a fresh load of reader.html#ch-N, the browser starts its native fragment scroll, which is smooth because of `html{scroll-behavior:smooth}`. The first scroll event sets userHasScrolled. The IntersectionObserver then fires for chapter 1, which is still in view, and replaceState writes '#ch-1'. restoreHash() waits for document.fonts.ready + 50 ms, and parseHash() then reads the overwritten hash and scrolls to chapter 1. This is the same race that was fixed in alice/reader.html in the last audit (target captured up front, observer writes suppressed until the restore lands), but the fix was never ported here. Reload of an open tab works only because the browser restores the scroll position itself. Bookmarks, shared links, new tabs and cross-page links all fail. CLAUDE.md says the position is 'restored on load'.
prophet.evidence: Fresh loads of reader.html#ch-2 … #ch-28 at 1440x900 (fonts blocked): 27/27 ended on chapter 1 with the hash rewritten to #ch-1. Trace: replaceState('#ch-1') at t=126 ms with scrollY=23; final scrollY=308, which is chapter 1's top minus 56. With a simulated font CDN, 6 loads per latency: 0/6 restored at 0, 50 and 150 ms; at 400 ms loads land on wrong chapters (5→2, 8→5, 20→12); only at 1000 ms are 6/6 correct. It also fails under prefers-reduced-motion.
prophet.repro: In a new tab, open gibran-prophet/reader.html#ch-12. The page shows 'The Coming of the Ship' and the URL becomes #ch-1.
prophet.fix: Port the Alice fix: read the target from location.hash when the script starts, suppress observer hash writes until the restore scroll has landed, and restore with scrollTo({top, behavior:'instant'}). Do not rely on the native fragment scroll.
verifier_corrections: Scope: the failure is deterministic-looking on desktop here but a race that passed 5/5 at 390x844 in the sandbox; it likely also fails on phones once real web fonts delay fonts.ready. No cross-page deep links exist, so the affected cases are bookmarks, shared links and new tabs. Severity medium: the workaround is sidebar/scrubber navigation, matching the old audit's MED for missing position persistence.

'27/27 fail' and '0/6 restored at 0 ms' hold only for desktop. At 390x844 with fonts blocked, restore worked 5/5; phones fail only when font loading takes about 100-500 ms, which is typical in production. 'Cross-page links all fail' is moot: no page in the repo currently links to reader.html#ch-N. The failure applies to bookmarks, shared links and new tabs. Reload works because the browser restores the scroll position itself.

prophet.title: fullbleed Contents page: clicking a chapter flips to page 1, because the invisible click zone covers the TOC
prophet.detail: #click-left and #click-right (.click-zone: absolute, 50% wide, full height, z-index 8) sit above the page content. attachTOCHandlers() binds clicks on the TOC <li>s, but those clicks never reach them: the zone takes the click and calls flipForward(). All 28 Contents entries therefore open page 1, on desktop and phone.
prophet.evidence: At #s-2 (1440x900), elementFromPoint at the centre of '10. On Clothes' returns #click-right. Clicking it gives spread 3, #p-1, chapter 1. Same result tapping at 390x844.
prophet.repro: Open gibran-prophet/fullbleed.html#s-2 and click 'On Clothes' in Contents. You land on page 1 (The Coming of the Ship).
prophet.fix: Stack the TOC above the zones (e.g. `.toc-page{position:relative;z-index:9}`), or have the zone handlers ignore clicks at points over a TOC entry. Making the entries <button>s also fixes keyboard access (see the click-only controls finding).
verifier_corrections: Phone scope: tapping the left half of an entry goes back to the title page (#s-1), not to page 1. Related but separate: at 1440x900 and 390x844 the TOC list runs past the page bottom (last li bottom 1278px vs a 900px page, overflow visible/clipped), so entries after about 19 are not visible at all. The TOC <li>s also have tabIndex -1, so they are not keyboard-reachable.

Phones: the entries span both zones, so tapping the left part (the number) goes BACK to the title page (#s-1), not to page 1. 'All 28 entries open page 1' holds for desktop only. Related defect on the same page: the Contents is one page clipped by .page-inner overflow:hidden. Only 17 of 28 entries are visible at 1440x900 (16 at 390x844, 21 at 1920x1080), so chapters 18-28 cannot be seen there at all. Outside this book, the same zone-over-TOC hit test fails in alice-in-wonderland/fullbleed.html (click-zone at :484, TOC li hits click-right) and khayyam-rubaiyat/fullbleed.html (:490). Line refs are correct.

prophet.title: fullbleed page-number box lands one spread early, and the last spread writes an out-of-range #p-N that reloads to the cover
prophet.detail: The click-to-edit page number maps page to spread with a different formula than the hash restore: `ci===0 → spread 2` (the Contents spread) and `3 + floor((ci-1)/2)`, one spread short. This is the same class of bug fixed in the Meditations fullbleed last audit. Separately, writeHashForSpread() uses the right-hand page index whenever it is >= 0, even when it is past the end. On the last spread it writes #p-(N+1), which init() rejects as out of range, so the next load opens the cover.
prophet.evidence: At 1440x900 (80 content pages): typing 1 shows Contents (#s-2), typing 10 shows pages 8–9 (#p-9), typing 41 shows pages 38–39. Going to the last spread gives hash #p-81; after reload the reader is on spread 0 (cover). Loading #p-80 immediately rewrites the hash to #p-81. A round-trip check over all spreads fails only on spread 43.
prophet.repro: Open gibran-prophet/fullbleed.html#p-5, click the '5' in the footer, type 10 and press Enter: the footer shows 9. Then press End-equivalent (→ until the last spread) and reload: you get the cover.
prophet.fix: Reuse init()'s mapping in the input handler (`ci===0 ? 3 : 3 + Math.floor((ci+1)/2)`). In writeHashForSpread, use `ri < contentPages.length ? ri : li`.
verifier_corrections: The line refs point one to two lines early. The wrong formula is at gibran-prophet/fullbleed.html:1493-1494 (commit() in initPageNumClick). The wrong pick is at :965-968 inside writeHashForSpread (the function starts at :959). Scope: desktop two-page mode only. The out-of-range hash appears only when the padded page count is even (for example at 1440x900), so it depends on the viewport.

Desktop two-page mode only: the phone mapping (ci+3) is correct. The last-spread hash bug appears only when the content page count is even, which depends on the viewport (80 at 1440x900 fails, 91 at 1280x720 passes). Precise lines: the wrong formula is at 1493-1494 (the finding cites 1491) and the out-of-range pick at 967. alice-in-wonderland/fullbleed.html:1484-1485 carries the identical page-box formula.

prophet.title: fullbleed resize or phone rotation jumps to a different chapter, and chapter links go stale
prophet.detail: The resize handler re-paginates but keeps the old numeric currentSpread. Spread numbers mean different things in single-page mode (<=768px) and two-page mode, and change with viewport height. chapterStartSpreads, used by the scrubber and TOC, is built only once in init() and never rebuilt, so chapter jumps after any resize go to the wrong place.
prophet.evidence: On a 390x844 phone at #p-40 (ch14 'On Freedom'), setViewportSize(844x390) (landscape) gives #p-79, ch25 'On Beauty'. At 1440x900, resizing to 1280x720 and clicking scrubber '20' opens chapter 18 'On Teaching'.
prophet.repro: On a phone, open fullbleed.html#p-40 and rotate to landscape: the reader jumps 11 chapters ahead. On desktop, shrink the window and click a chapter number in the footer.
prophet.fix: Before re-paginating, record the current page's chapter and its first block index; after re-paginating, rebuild chapterStartSpreads (move lines 1402–1415 into a function) and map the recorded block back to a spread in the new mode.
verifier_corrections: Context for the status: the same class (breakpoint crossing) was an old-audit item for vedas/fullbleed and is fixed there at vedas/fullbleed.html:876-886, which is a precedent to copy. Prophet also needs block-anchored remapping because its pagination depends on height. The desktop scrubber goes wrong only after a resize that changes pagination. The mobile goToChapter path scans contentPages, so it stays correct.

Additional instance of the same stale or incorrect map: on phones the Contents page numbers are wrong even without a resize. chapterStartSpreads is computed with the two-page spread formula over single-page (non-recto) pagination, so at 390x844 chapters 2, 6, 10, 14, 17, 18, 23, 24 and 25 show a page number one too high (e.g. ch 2 shows 11, starts on 10). Line refs are correct.

prophet.title: reader.html phone redirect to mobile.html drops #ch-N, and 'Reader' links on phones bounce back
prophet.detail: A head script runs `location.replace('mobile.html')` for phone user agents narrower than 768px, discarding the hash, even though both formats use #ch-N. A reader.html#ch-12 link shared from desktop or bookmarked opens the mobile title card instead of chapter 12. On phones, every 'Reader' link (index format list, the mobile title slide's 'Reader' chip, the illustrations title link) silently lands on mobile.html; the mobile title slide's 'Reader' link just reloads mobile.html. CLAUDE.md does not document the redirect.
prophet.evidence: With an iPhone UA at 390x844: goto reader.html#ch-12 ends at http://localhost:8111/gibran-prophet/mobile.html with curIdx 0 (title slide). Tapping 'Reader' on the mobile title slide also ends at mobile.html.
prophet.repro: On a phone, open lib.sadh.app/gibran-prophet/reader.html#ch-12: you get the mobile title card, not 'On Crime and Punishment'.
prophet.fix: Carry the hash across: `location.replace('mobile.html' + location.hash)`. Add an opt-out (e.g. ?view=reader, remembered per session) so the Reader link means something on phones, or drop the 'Reader' chip from mobile's title slide. Document the redirect in CLAUDE.md.
verifier_corrections: Scope: pdf-reader.html:576 ('← Reader' backLink) and theater.html:378 ('↩ Reader') also link to reader.html and would bounce the same way on phones. I did not check these in the browser: theater's .ctrl-back was not clickable in the phone context. Only phone UAs narrower than 768px are affected; iPad Mini at 768 is not redirected.

The 'undocumented redirect' part overlaps with prophet finding 25 (docs drift lists the undocumented redirect), so count the docs aspect only once. The illustrations.html:284 link is a book-title link rather than a format chooser, so landing on mobile.html there is harmless; the self-defeating cases are the mobile title-slide 'Reader' chip (mobile.html:367) and the index format list (index.html:407). Side note for the orchestrator: on desktop, reader.html#ch-12 also lost its position in 6 of 8 loads (it landed on #ch-1). That is prophet finding 2 and should not be merged into this one.

prophet.title: pdf-reader: each wheel event flips a page, so one trackpad gesture skips dozens of pages
prophet.detail: The pageCard wheel listener calls nextPage()/prevPage() on every wheel event, with no delta accumulation or cooldown. Trackpads and smooth-scrolling mice send tens of small events per gesture.
prophet.evidence: At #p-10 (1440x900), 25 wheel events of deltaY=4 (one gentle two-finger scroll) left currentPage at 35.
prophet.repro: On a laptop trackpad, open pdf-reader.html#p-10 and scroll slightly over the page: the reader lands 20+ pages ahead.
prophet.fix: Accumulate deltaY and flip only after a threshold (e.g. 80px), then ignore wheel input for about 300 ms. Or let the page card scroll and flip only at the top/bottom edges.
verifier_corrections: Same root cause also in alice-in-wonderland/pdf-reader.html:962 and :967, so the fix should cover both files.
Scope: identical handlers exist in alice-in-wonderland/pdf-reader.html:962-971, on both #pageCard and #pageCard2. The khayyam, vedas and meditations pdf-readers have no wheel handler.

prophet.title: pdf-reader shows a blank page when localStorage is blocked (unguarded getItem/setItem)
prophet.detail: init() calls localStorage.getItem and setTheme() calls localStorage.setItem without try/catch. When site data is blocked, accessing localStorage throws SecurityError: init() aborts before pagination and no pages render. The other six Prophet pages wrap storage in try/catch and work.

On the dedicated phone format, readers open a quatrain and see the middle of the notes, not the poem.

khayyam.title: fullbleed.html: facing notes can't be scrolled because transparent click zones cover the page (phones and desktop verso)
khayyam.detail: #click-left and #click-right (position:absolute, 50% width, 100% height, z-index 8) sit above both page halves. On phones (≤768px) the recto's .page-inner is the only scroll container for the quatrain plus the inline 'Facing notes'. On desktop the verso .gloss-page is overflow-y:auto with a hidden scrollbar. Wheel and touch gestures hit the click zone, whose ancestors (#book, body) are overflow:hidden, so nothing scrolls. A tap only turns the page. The facing apparatus is the format's main feature, and on phones it is mostly unreadable.

Desktop verso overflow: 116 spreads at 1440x900 (up to 258px hidden) and 253 at 1280x720 (up to 438px). Wheel over the verso leaves gloss scrollTop at 0 because the top element is click-left. For FG5 XII at 1280x720, 'Other historical translations', 'FitzGerald · 1st · 11' and 'Whinfield · 1883 · 404' are entirely below the fold (shots/fb-1280-p12.png, fb-m-p12.png).
khayyam.repro: Open fullbleed.html#p-12 at 390x844 and try to scroll to the Modern rendering in the notes. Or open it at 1280x720 and wheel over the left page.
khayyam.fix: Don't overlay the text. Limit the click zones to narrow edge strips (e.g. 12–15% width) or to non-scrolling areas, or listen for clicks on the page halves and ignore clicks that end a scroll or text selection. Also give the gloss a visible scroll affordance or fade.

khayyam.title: reader.html: scroll observer overwrites the incoming hash before restoreHash() runs, so bookmarks and reloads on phones land at group 1 or in the wrong edition
khayyam.detail: restoreHash() waits for fonts.ready + 50ms or 400ms. Before then, the browser's own smooth fragment scroll (html{scroll-behavior:smooth}) or reload scroll restoration fires 'scroll'. That sets userHasScrolled=true, and the IntersectionObserver calls replaceState('#chg-<activeEdition>-N') for whatever group passes the band. That group is often group 1, and in the saved or default edition rather than the hash's edition. restoreHash then parses the overwritten hash. The earlier audit's '#chg- never script-restored' fix added a script restore but left this race, which AGENT_README specifically warns about. Separately, even when restore succeeds, a #q-<ed>-N deep link is downgraded to a group hash within about 200ms. That hash sometimes names the next group (#q-nicolas-400 becomes #chg-nicolas-41, and a reload lands on 401).
khayyam.evidence: Instrumented replaceState and scroll events during a 390x844 reload: scroll at 114ms (y=32→130), replaceState('#chg-fifth-1') at 131ms, then the restore lands on q-fifth-1. 'Open #q-<ed>-N then reload' trials: 390px 6/6 lost place (q-nicolas-400 and q-whinfield-137 both land on q-fifth-1 with hash #chg-fifth-1); 1440px 1/6. New tab with a bookmark into the saved edition: 320px #chg-whinfield-14 3/3 land on q-whinfield-1 (hash rewritten to #chg-whinfield-1); 390px #q-persian-100 2/3 land on q-persian-1; 1440 1/3. Fresh-context deep links (no prior state) do work.
khayyam.repro: At 390x844, open reader.html#q-whinfield-137, wait 2s, then reload: you land on FG5 quatrain I. Or click 'Wh' once, then open reader.html#chg-whinfield-14 in a new tab at 320x640: you land on Whinfield 1.
khayyam.fix: Capture the target from location.hash synchronously at script start. Set history.scrollRestoration='manual'. Suppress observer writes (or setupChapterObserver) until the restore has scrolled. Restore immediately with behavior 'instant' instead of waiting for fonts, re-anchoring after fonts.ready. Consider writing #q-<ed>-N per quatrain, as mobile and theater do.
verifier_corrections: The line citations are correct. Reload on phones fails every time in my runs. The new-tab bookmark case is intermittent (1 of 3 failures at 320, none at 390 in my runs), so it is less frequent than the finding suggests. The two defects are separate: the observer overwriting the hash before restore, and the #q-→#chg- downgrade off by one group. The second is a lower-severity accuracy problem on its own.

The reload failure at phone width is deterministic (4 of 6 lost the edition and landed on FG5 I, the other 2 landed on the wrong quatrain). The new-tab bookmark-into-saved-edition failure is intermittent (about 1 in 3 at 390 and 1440, 0/3 at 320 in my runs), not 3/3. At desktop, the #q→#chg downgrade alone moves a reload to the start of the group or to the next group's first quatrain.

khayyam.title: Language markup: English apparatus inside lang="fa", Persian headings tagged English, and an invalid 'en-fa-Latn' tag on every transliteration line
khayyam.detail: In reader.html the Persian edition puts dir="rtl" lang="fa" on the whole <article>, which also contains the English detail panel (modern renderings, notes, Whinfield/FitzGerald alternates, 'Show details'), so screen readers voice English with Persian rules. The reverse: Persian group titles ('رباعیات ۱–۱۰' in chapter dividers, sidebar, top-bar indicator), Persian-digit ordinals and the 'فا' prefixes in theater and mobile inherit lang="en". Transliteration lines use lang="en-fa-Latn", which is not well-formed BCP 47 (a 2-letter subtag after the language is a region and cannot precede a script), so AT ignores it. The intended tag is fa-Latn. CLAUDE.md documents the bad tag.
khayyam.evidence: Text-node probe with Details on at reader.html#q-persian-1: 4,055 Latin-script nodes whose nearest [lang] is 'fa'. 110 Persian-script nodes under lang='en' (SPAN.ch-title etc.). theater: 2 ('۱', 'فا'); mobile: 21 (q-num, q-ord, jump rows). Intl.getCanonicalLocales('en-fa-Latn') throws RangeError while 'fa-Latn' is fine. 'en-fa-Latn' occurrences: reader 2256, fullbleed/mobile/pdf 1484, theater 712.
khayyam.repro: reader.html → click فا → toggle Details (i) → inspect any .q-detail: its closest [lang] is the article's lang=fa.
khayyam.fix: Put lang/dir on .q-main/.q-verse (or add lang="en" dir="ltr" on the .q-detail aside). Wrap Persian titles, ordinals and 'فا' in <span lang="fa" dir="rtl">. Replace en-fa-Latn with fa-Latn in build_reader.py and CLAUDE.md, then rebuild.
verifier_corrections: The '110 Persian-script nodes under lang=en' figure is inflated. 72 of them are p.translit lines whose lang is en-fa-Latn and which contain a leftover U+0654 hamza (e.g. 'trbkhanhٔ'), not Persian headings. The real count of Persian-script headings under lang=en in reader.html is 38: 18 span.ch-title in the sidebar, 18 div.ch-title dividers, 1 chapter-indicator and 1 edition-caption. 'AT ignores it' was not verified. Many screen readers fall back to the primary subtag 'en', so the practical harm of the bad tag is mostly well-formedness and docs drift. The claim that AT 'ignores' the bad tag is unverified. Chromium passes the raw string through, and some screen readers will key off the leading 'en' subtag. The real defect is that the tag is ill-formed and does not say what the author meant (fa-Latn), so rate that sub-part low. The CLAUDE.md reference is in the Accessibility section, around line 190 of khayyam-rubaiyat/CLAUDE.md. Scope, files and lines are otherwise correct.

vedas.title: Complete Rigveda, Mandala 8: 24 sūktas are empty and 28 more show the English and title of a different hymn
vedas.detail: Sūktas 8.68-8.80, 8.92-8.94 and 8.96-8.103 have v:[] and no title, about 385 verses in all. rigveda.html renders them as stacked headers with nothing under them, and the hash drifts between them (#8.70 loads as #8.71 on desktop). In 8.49-8.59, 8.61-8.65, 8.81-8.91 and 8.95 the English column and the sūkta title belong to a different hymn than the Sanskrit and Bengali beside them. The source uses Griffith's numbering, which moves the 11 Vālakhilya hymns to an appendix, so it runs 11 ahead. Examples: 8.49 has the Sanskrit 'abhi pra vaḥ surādhasam indram arca' and Bengali about Indra, but the English reads 'AGNI, come hither with thy fires…' (that is 8.60.1, which shows the same verse in another translation), and it is titled 'Agni'. 8.51's Sanskrit 'yathā manau sāṃvaraṇau somam indrāpibaḥ' has its translation shown under 8.95 ('As with Manu Samvarani, Indra…'). 8.91 (the Apālā hymn) is titled 'Agni' and shows 8.102's English. About half of Mandala 8 is therefore missing or wrong. index.html, CLAUDE.md and README still say 'all 1,028 sūktas, 10,143 mantras'. The standard count is 10,552, as reader.html's own description says. The Mandala 1 total (1,979 vs the commonly cited 2,006) is also low; I did not track that down.
vedas.evidence: Python over data/mandala-*.json: M8 has 103 sūktas, 1,331 verses (standard 1,716), and 24 empty [68..80, 92, 93, 94, 96..103]. scripts/output/ebanglalibrary_bengali.json does have 8.68-8.103 (19, 18, 15 … 14 verses), so the Bengali source is complete and the English/Sanskrit fetch or parse dropped these sūktas. First-line comparison of 8.41-8.95 shows the 11-hymn offset. Screenshots: work/vedas/rv-8.70.d.png (empty 'SŪKTA 69 / 70 / 71' headers) and rv-8.49.d.png (Agni English next to Indra Sanskrit/Bengali).

vedas.title: Complete Rigveda Sanskrit is corrupted in all three scripts: viramas dropped, vocalic ṛ lost, IAST inherits the errors
vedas.detail: The Devanagari scraped for rigveda.html has lost its viramas. Consonant+r clusters become separate syllables (प्र→पर, त्व→तव, श्रु→शरु), vocalic ṛ is written as र्/र (ऋत्विजम्→रत्वीजम), and final consonants lose the halant (तत्→तत, प्रचोदयात्→परचोदयात). The Bengali-script Sanskrit is a Unicode-offset copy of this, and the IAST column is generated from it by devToIAST, so all three Sanskrit streams are wrong in nearly every verse. The Gayatri (3.62.10), which index.html points readers to, shows IAST 'tata savitur vareṇyaṃ bhargo devasya dhīmahi | dhiyo yo naḥ paracodayāta ||'. 1.1.1 reads 'devaṃ ratvījama'. Verse ends are ASCII '|'/'||', not ।/॥. index.html's own featured Gayatri (hand-written) is correct, so the landing page and the reader visibly disagree.
vedas.evidence: Across 10,143 verses: word-initial 'प्र' 0 vs 'पर' 5,262; 'ऋ' 0; 'ृ' 6 (the 95 curated verses have 60 'ृ' and 6 'ऋ'); 7,001 bare final consonants before a danda vs 6 with a virama; 'कष' 489 where 'क्ष' is expected. Running devToIAST on the stored 3.62.10 and 1.1.1 gives 'paracodayāta' and 'ratvījama'. The build strips the source's per-word <span class="transliteration-word"> (build_rigveda.py:117).
vedas.repro: Open /vedas/rigveda.html#3.62, open settings, turn on IAST, scroll to 3.62.10. Compare with the Gayatri box on /vedas/index.html.
vedas.fix: Take the Sanskrit from a source that keeps viramas and vocalic ṛ (for example the Aufrecht/VedaWeb or GRETIL text), or rebuild Devanagari from the source's per-word transliteration spans instead of stripping them. Use real dandas. Add a build-time sanity check (for example, fail when word-initial प्र is 0).
verifier_corrections: Restate the mechanism. Viramas are not lost wholesale (83,999 remain, and mid-word conjuncts are intact). The errors are in word-initial consonant clusters, word-final halants and vocalic ṛ/ṝ. The rendered IAST is 'tata saviturvareṇyaṃ …' (no space between savitur and vareṇyaṃ). IAST is off by default, but the default-on Devanagari and Bengali-script columns carry the same errors. 'Nearly every verse': at least 56% by the final-halant check alone.

Narrow the root cause. The viramas lost are those in C+र clusters and word-final position, plus vocalic ṛ; other conjuncts are intact. Drop the ASCII '|'/'||' point, because that is documented at vedas/CLAUDE.md:105. The IAST actually rendered is 'tata saviturvareṇyaṃ' (no space) and 'devaṃ ratvījama'. The build lines are build_rigveda.py:110-118 (the sanskrit-word extraction, with the span strip at 116-117) and 37-50 (dev_to_bengali). 'Nearly every verse' should be 'most verses (at least 56-70% by simple markers)'.

vedas.title: rigveda: switching mandala after scrolling lands on the wrong sūkta (the old load race, now on tab clicks)
vedas.detail: goToSukta() sets mIdx/sIdx and replaces the content with 'Loading…', but leaves renderedUpTo at the old mandala's value and keeps the bottom-sentinel observer attached while the new mandala's 0.5-2.3 MB file loads. The now-short page brings the sentinel into view, and appendNextSukta() passes its renderedUpTo<0 guard (that guard only covers the first render). It appends stub sūktas of the not-yet-loaded mandala, and suktaObserver overwrites sIdx before render() reads it. Clicking the 'Mandala 10' tab (or number keys 1-0, or the progress bar) after reading a few sūktas lands deep inside the new mandala instead of on sūkta 1. This happens locally without any throttling, and a real network makes it worse.
vedas.evidence: 1440: scrolled to #1.14, clicked Mandala 10 → #10.15 'Fathers' (expected 10.1). Clicked Mandala 5 from the bottom with a 1.5s data delay → #5.17. 390: #1.8 → Mandala 10 tab → #10.10 'Yama Yami'. Reproduced with no artificial delay for Mandala 10 (1440 → 10.15, 390 → 10.10).
vedas.repro: Open /vedas/rigveda.html#1.1, scroll down through about 10 sūktas, then click 'Mandala 10'. The header shows Sūkta 11-15 instead of 1.
vedas.fix: In goToSukta/render, before the await: set renderedUpTo=renderedFrom=-1, call scrollObserver.disconnect() and suktaObserver.disconnect(), and capture the target (mi, si) in locals that the observers cannot change. Guard appendNextSukta/prependPreviousSukta with RV.m[mIdx]._loaded.
verifier_corrections: Broader than stated. It happens even without scrolling first: a fresh #1.1 load followed by a Mandala 10 click lands on #10.2. It is timing dependent (1 of 6 runs landed correctly). The same line numbers apply to the served vedas/rigveda.html, whose only difference from the template is the one-line RV_META.

The line refs are right: 391 goToSukta, 323/327 appendNextSukta and its guard, 357 scrollObserver, 369 suktaObserver. It can also trigger with little or no scrolling (#9.1 → #10.2). Status is arguably 'new, same root cause as the fixed init race' rather than a regression: the old report fixed and claimed only the first-render path, and this goToSukta path was never reported. 'Fix incomplete' is acceptable.

vedas.title: fullbleed: every table-of-contents click lands on the wrong page, and the TOC cannot be used from the keyboard
vedas.detail: attachTOCHandlers() renders the chosen sūkta but does not stop propagation. The click then reaches #book's page-turn handler, which flips forward or back depending on the tap's x position. On desktop the TOC sits in the right half, so every entry skips the sūkta's opening page (header, ṛṣi/devatā, first mantra) and opens on its second mantra. On phones, a tap on the title (left half) goes back to the previous sūkta's last meaning page, and a tap on the page number (right half) opens the meaning half with the header skipped. The chapter scrubber calls stopPropagation and works. The TOC rows are plain <li> elements with click handlers (tabIndex -1, no role), so keyboard users cannot use the TOC at all. The TOC's page numbers (content index +1, e.g. '10' for 3.62) also do not match the page numbers printed on the spread (19/20).
vedas.evidence: Desktop: TOC '3.62 … 10' → '#p-11', mantra 3.62.11; Samaveda '1.1 … 50' → 1.1.2; '19.53 … 87' → 19.53.2. 390px and 320px: tap on the title → 3.62 opens 1.1.9, Samaveda 1.1 opens 10.191.4, 19.53 opens 12.1.63; tap on the page number → the meaning page of mantra 1. Tab order on the TOC spread skips every TOC row.
vedas.repro: Open /vedas/fullbleed.html#s-2 and click 'সাবিত্রী সূক্ত 3.62'. The spread shows 3.62.11, not the sūkta header with 3.62.10. On a phone, the same tap shows Rigveda 1.1.9.
vedas.fix: Call e.stopPropagation() in the TOC handler, or have the #book click handler ignore clicks inside .toc-list. Make the rows <button>s (or <a href="#p-N">). Print TOC numbers in the same system as the page numbers.
verifier_corrections: The TOC page-number mismatch applies to desktop only: the TOC's 10 vs the spread's 19/20. On mobile the TOC numbers match the printed page numbers. For keyboard users, the chapter-scrubber buttons are a keyboard-reachable alternative, so that part is an a11y defect with a workaround. The broken click routing alone justifies high.

Page-number sub-claim applies to desktop only. The TOC number (suktaStartPages+1, e.g. 10 for 3.62) does match the footer counter (#page-num = pi+1) and the #p-N hash. It differs only from the desktop corner page numbers, which print pi*2+1 and pi*2+2 (19/20). On phones the corner number prints pageIdx+1, which matches the TOC. The primary line is vedas/fullbleed.html:740 (the click listener). The trigger is lines 770-774. Line 671 (renderSpread's desktop TOC branch) is incidental. Keyboard users have a workaround: the footer scrubber buttons are focusable.

vedas.title: Invisible controls take keyboard focus: closed reader sidebar, hidden back-to-top scrubber, closed mobile sheets
vedas.detail: reader.html: #chapter-sidebar is closed by translateX(-100%) only, and comes before the top bar in the DOM. The first 13 Tab stops are therefore invisible sidebar links, before the menu button. #back-to-top is a <button> that contains a scrubber with 13 more <button>s (buttons inside a button is invalid HTML). While hidden (opacity 0) the button and all 13 nodes still take focus. The scrubber appears only on :hover, with no focus or touch path, which breaks the house rule. The button's accessible name is '↑ Agni Sukta অগ্নি সূক্ত Savitri Sukta …', every sūkta title strung together. mobile.html: the three closed sheets are translateY(100%) with aria-hidden="true", yet their 13 sūkta rows, 5 script chips and 5 theme dots stay in the Tab order. Focus moves onto controls that are both off-screen and hidden from screen readers.
vedas.evidence: Tab order on reader.html (1440 and 390): 13 × sidebar-chapter [hidden] → menu → theme → … → settings → back-to-top [hidden] → ch-node × 13 [hidden]. The accessibility tree names back-to-top '↑ Agni Sukta অগ্নি সূক্ত Savitri Sukta (Gayatri Mantra) …'. mobile.html Tab order: toc/scripts/theme/slide/prev/next, then row × 13 flagged [OFFSCREEN][ARIA-HIDDEN].
vedas.repro: Open /vedas/reader.html and press Tab. Nothing visible is focused for 13 presses. Open /vedas/mobile.html and press Tab 7 times: focus goes into the closed sūkta sheet.
vedas.fix: Add visibility:hidden (or the inert attribute) to the closed sidebar and closed sheets, removing it on open. Move the scrubber out of #back-to-top, give back-to-top aria-label="Back to top", and reveal the scrubber on :focus-within, with tabindex=-1 on its nodes while it is hidden.
verifier_corrections: Small fix to the repro. On first load at sūkta 1, #prev is disabled, so on mobile.html the hidden .row buttons start at Tab 6, not Tab 7. The observed order is toc, scr, thm, slide, next, then the rows. The closed reader sidebar links are not aria-hidden, so they appear in the AX tree while closed. Only the mobile sheets have the aria-hidden-with-focusable-content problem. All cited lines are accurate: reader.html 669/675/742/744 and mobile-template.html 73/117-119.

Line numbers are correct. One minor detail: on the first sūkta, #prev is disabled, so focus enters the closed sheet on the 6th Tab press, not the 7th. It is the 7th only when #prev is enabled. Also note that aria-hidden=true with focusable descendants is itself an ARIA violation (WCAG 4.1.2), and the sheets are marked aria-modal but have no focus trap. That last point is outside this finding's scope.

vedas.title: Key and tap handlers override normal behaviour: Space won't press buttons, PageDown skips a whole sūkta, a tap on theater text jumps ahead
vedas.detail: reader.html prevents the default for Space and the arrow keys no matter what has focus, so Space on a focused button scrolls the page instead of pressing it. fullbleed does the same globally (Space or arrows flip pages even while a theme dot or scrubber button has focus). theater maps Space to 'next sūkta', and any click or tap on #stage also advances, including a tap on the text while reading a long, scrollable sūkta. pdf-reader maps PageDown/PageUp to next/previous sūkta, so a reader can never page through a long sūkta card (Purusha Sūkta is about 5,400px). The single-letter shortcuts (d/i in reader, d/g in rigveda) also fire with Ctrl or Cmd held, so Ctrl+D (bookmark) toggles Devanagari.
vedas.evidence: reader.html: focus #sidebar-toggle, press Space → sidebar stays closed and scrollY moves to 765 (Enter opens it). theater at 390: #s-rigveda-90 with the view scrolled to 2000px, one tap on the text → #s-rigveda-129 with scrollTop 0. pdf-reader at 1440/390/320: PageDown on #s-rigveda-90 → #s-rigveda-129 and scrollTop 0.
vedas.repro: On /vedas/pdf-reader.html#s-rigveda-90 press PageDown to read further. It jumps to the Nāsadīya sūkta.
vedas.fix: Return early when e.target is a button/select/a (or closest interactive element), and when e.ctrlKey, e.metaKey or e.altKey is held. Let PageDown/Space scroll the #vp/#view scroller and only advance once it is at the bottom. Restrict theater's click-to-advance to empty stage margins, or drop it.
verifier_corrections: The cited lines are right. Extra evidence worth adding: in theater, Space on a focused Previous button moves forward to the next sūkta. rigveda-template.html:508 (Ctrl/Cmd+G, which is 'find next' on Mac, opens the sūkta grid) should be listed next to 507. The generated theater.html, pdf-reader.html and rigveda.html carry the same code at nearby lines. The Ctrl+D effect was observed in the page's handler; in headless mode I could not observe the browser's bookmark dialog itself.

Lines are correct. Add rigveda-template.html:508 ('g'/'G' → toggleGrid, so Ctrl+G, find-next, opens the grid) beside line 507. Note that theater's stage click-to-advance and pdf's PageDown-as-next-page are house-wide patterns shared with the other books. The defect is specific to Vedas because each sūkta is a long scrollable card. In pdf-reader and theater, Space and ArrowDown also fail to scroll the card until the scroller has been clicked or tabbed into (the body is overflow:hidden), so the keyboard reading path for a long sūkta is worse than stated.

vedas.title: Missing accessible state and names: script toggles, menu/settings buttons, strip arrows, sūkta grid; no reduced-motion support
vedas.detail: The rigveda script toggles (5) and reader toggles (2) have no aria-pressed, so their on/off state is only shown by colour. The settings and sidebar buttons lack aria-expanded. rigveda's ◂/▸ strip buttons have no aria-label or title, so they are announced as 'black left-pointing small triangle'. The active mandala tab and sūkta pill have no aria-current. The sūkta grid overlay has no role=dialog and does not move focus. prefers-reduced-motion appears nowhere in reader, rigveda, fullbleed or pdf-reader, even though reader and rigveda set html{scroll-behavior:smooth} and scroll with behavior:'smooth' in script.
vedas.evidence: DOM query: .toggle-btn aria-pressed null ×5, #settings-btn aria-expanded null, .scroll-btn aria-label null and title '', .m-tab.active aria-current null. grep -c prefers-reduced-motion: reader 0, fullbleed 0, rigveda 0, pdf-reader 0.
vedas.repro: Open /vedas/rigveda.html with a screen reader, open settings and focus 'IAST'. No pressed/not-pressed state is announced.
vedas.fix: Set aria-pressed on the toggles (update it in the click handlers and loadPrefs), aria-expanded on the menu and settings buttons, aria-label on the strip arrows, and aria-current on the active tab and pill. Give the grid role=dialog and move focus into it. Wrap smooth scrolling in @media (prefers-reduced-motion:no-preference).
verifier_corrections: Minor evidence fix: the strip buttons have no title attribute at all (null, not ''). fullbleed's reduced-motion gap covers its 3D page-flip animation (fullbleed.html:390-405), not only scrolling. The reader.html toggles are at lines 732-733.

vedas.title: rigveda phones: swiping the mandala tabs or sūkta strip turns the page instead of scrolling the row, so the far mandalas are still out of reach
vedas.detail: The previous P0 fix made #mandala-row scrollable. But a document-wide touchend handler treats any horizontal movement over 60px as prev/next sūkta, including swipes on the tab row, on the sūkta strip, and vertical reading scrolls that drift sideways. The handler calls render(), which jumps to the new sūkta's top (the reader loses their place), and scrollActiveTabIntoView() smooth-scrolls the tab row back to the active mandala. From Mandala 1 on a phone, a normal swipe cannot bring Mandalas 6-10 into view, and from Mandala 10 it cannot reach 1-2. Only several sub-60px nudges work. The workarounds (number keys, progress bar) are unavailable on phones: there is no keyboard, and the progress bar is covered by the nav strip. Browsing the 191-pill strip by swipe fails the same way. mobile.html already guards its swipe with |dx|>|dy|; rigveda does not.
vedas.evidence: CDP touch swipes at 390: from #10.1, 4 full L→R swipes on the tab row leave scrollLeft at 322/315/322/314 and the Mandala 1 tab at x=-318; six 55px swipes do reach it (scrollLeft 0). From #1.5, 3 R→L swipes on the row move the reading position 1.5→1.7→1.9→1.10 while scrollLeft stays 0 and the Mandala 10 tab stays at x=633-708 (same at 320px). A swipe on the sūkta strip at #3.10 changed the sūkta to 3.11. A diagonal reading scroll (dx=-100, dy=-400) at #1.1 jumped to 1.2.
vedas.repro: Phone (390px): open /vedas/rigveda.html#1.5 and swipe the 'Mandala 1 … Mandala 5' row right-to-left to reach Mandala 10. The row snaps back and the text jumps to the next sūkta.
vedas.fix: Ignore touches that start inside #nav-strip, #settings-panel or #sukta-grid (check e.target.closest). Require |dx| > |dy| (and ideally |dy| < 40). Do not call scrollActiveTabIntoView when the mandala has not changed.
verifier_corrections: The far mandalas are reachable by tapping intermediate visible tabs (two hops from M1 to M10), by sub-60px nudges, and through the ◂ ▸ strip buttons and the sūkta grid for sūktas, so they are not 'out of reach'. The confirmed defects are: full-length swipes on the tab row or strip turn the sūkta and snap the row back; vertical reading scrolls with more than 60px sideways drift turn the sūkta and lose the place; and the progress bar is hidden under the nav strip on phones. Severity: medium.

The touch handlers are at data/rigveda-template.html:519 (touchstart) and 520 (touchend), not 518/520. Downgrade to medium: the far mandalas remain reachable by tapping the edge tab, which auto-centres and reveals the next ones. The real impact is that (a) the tab row and sūkta strip cannot be browsed by swiping, since they snap back and the sūkta changes, and (b) any stray horizontal gesture over 60px while reading turns the sūkta and loses the reader's place. Status is better described as 'new (defeats the old mobile-row fix on touch)' than a pure regression.

vedas.title: Touch targets below 40px: theme dots with no enlarged hit area, fullbleed arrows, pdf-reader select
vedas.detail: The Resolution says theme dots have '≥40px hit areas across every book', but fullbleed's .td dots are 14×14 with no ::before hit-area expander, and those are the only theme control there. The new theater and pdf-reader repeat the 14px dots (theater hides them entirely ≤480px), and mobile's sheet dots are 26px. fullbleed's ←/→ page buttons, the main page controls on a phone besides swiping, are 26×24. pdf-reader's sūkta <select>, its main navigation, is 24px tall. The fullbleed scrubber (20×11) is already tracked in the vedas todo.
vedas.evidence: Measured at 390: fullbleed .td 14×14 with no ::before, footer-nav ← 26×24 and → 26×24, scrubber 20×11. pdf-reader 'Choose sukta' 173×24 and dots 14×14. theater dots 14×14 at 1440 and display:none at 390. mobile .dot 26×26 (CSS).
vedas.repro: Open /vedas/fullbleed.html#p-10 on a phone and try to tap the Sepia dot or the → arrow.
vedas.fix: Reuse the vertical ::before hit-area expander from rigveda/reader (.theme-dot::before{height:40px}) for .td and .dot. Pad .footer-nav buttons to 40×40 on coarse pointers. Give #sel min-height:36-40px on phones. Show the theater theme dots, or a theme button, on phones.
verifier_corrections: The pdf-reader <select> is not its only navigation: prev and next buttons sit next to it in #tb. Those buttons are also just under the rule, 34x34 on desktop and 38x38 at ≤768px (pdf-template.html:42,67). The select is 24px tall at every viewport, not only on phones. The 'theater hides dots ≤480px' item is really a missing-control problem (no way to change theme on a phone), not only a touch-target problem.

fullbleed also has tap-to-flip zones on the whole #book (lines 770-774), so the 26×24 arrows are not the only non-swipe page control. Add the stronger symptom: a tap that just misses a 14px theme dot flips the page, because #footer has pointer-events:none, so the miss falls through to the #book click zone. Also worth noting: pdf #prev/#next are 34×34 on desktop and 38×38 on phones, just under the 40px rule. The theater phone case (dots display:none at ≤480px, so no theme control at all) is a missing-control problem rather than a target-size one; it could be split out or kept here as grouped.

vedas.title: rigveda sūkta pills and mandala tabs are still small on touch screens; the fix is phone-only
vedas.detail: This is a tracked todo item: pills are 36px on phones. The part not tracked: the larger targets sit behind @media(max-width:768px), not (pointer:coarse). Touch tablets such as an iPad (820 or 1024 wide) still get 28×22 pills, 26px-tall mandala tabs, 24×24 strip arrows and 32×32 theme/settings buttons, the sizes the previous audit flagged.
vedas.evidence: 820×1180 and 1024×768 with hasTouch (pointer:coarse true): pill 28×22, tab 78×26, strip button 24×24, settings 32×32. At 390: pill 36×36.
vedas.repro: Open /vedas/rigveda.html#8.1 on an iPad-sized touch viewport and tap individual sūkta numbers.
vedas.fix: Add @media (pointer:coarse){…} with the ≥40px sizes (pills 40px min-height, or a ::before expander), independent of width.
verifier_corrections: Status: only the 36px-on-phones part is tracked. The tablet part is an incomplete version of the prior audit's MED fix, so it is better classed as a regression (fix incomplete) than as still-open. Add a location: the sukta-grid tiles (.s-tile, vedas/data/rigveda-template.html:107) are 38x32 at every width, phones included, so the grid 'workaround' is also below 40px. The mobile overrides are at rigveda-template.html:147-158.

vedas.title: Public site serves broken template pages and about 48 MB of unlinked build output
vedas.detail: The previous audit's 'raw template deployed at book root' item was closed by moving the template into data/. With .nojekyll, data/ is just as public: lib.sadh.app/vedas/data/rigveda-template.html (and the three new mobile/theater/pdf templates) load as blank pages that throw ReferenceError. AGENT_README claims only the book root is publicly reachable, which is wrong. No page links to seeds/rigveda-complete.json (13.1 MB; 3.2 MB gzip) or rigveda-samhita.md (11.6 MB; 3.1 MB gzip), and both carry the same corrupted Sanskrit and Mandala 8 gaps. scripts/output (23.6 MB: scraper intermediates, OCR, LLM batch files) and the scraper and build scripts are published too. build_rigveda.py sits at the book root, although AGENT_README says build scripts belong under data/. vedas/ holds 72.6 MB of tracked files.
vedas.evidence: smoke.json: data/*-template.html pages error with '__META_JSON__ is not defined' or '__DATA__ is not defined' (textLen 3-28). du/stat sizes above. grep across *.html finds no page linking rigveda-samhita.md, rigveda-complete.json or scripts/output. No secrets found in the scripts.
vedas.repro: Open http://localhost:8111/vedas/data/rigveda-template.html: blank page with a console ReferenceError.
vedas.fix: Keep build-only files out of the Pages artifact: publish from a docs/ or build branch, or add a Pages workflow that copies only the reader files. At minimum, correct AGENT_README's 'only root is public' statement. Either link the .md/.json as downloads (after fixing the text) or move them out of the served tree.
verifier_corrections: Status should be new (docs and build-output hygiene) rather than regression. Serving data/*-template.html as broken pages is repo-wide (every book keeps templates in data/, e.g. aurelius-meditations/data/mobile-template.html also throws). AGENT_README contradicts itself: the 'build scripts belong under data/' rule (lines 77-79) versus the tree listing vedas/build_rigveda.py at the root (line 71). The vedas CLAUDE.md documents rigveda-samhita.md and rigveda-complete.json as intended outputs, so the fix should be deliberate: link them as downloads or stop publishing them.

vedas.title: Bengali meanings misaligned or OCR-garbled in some verses; small errors in the curated text
vedas.detail: The Bengali column of the complete Rigveda occasionally belongs to another hymn or is raw OCR. 1.137.1-3 (a Mitra-Varuṇa Soma hymn) shows a Pūṣan hymn's meaning ('বহুজন পূজিত পুযার শক্তির মহিমা…', 'হে পূষা!…'). 5.24.1-3 (Agni) shows OCR text of an Indra hymn with garbage ('হেইন্্র! … মকণ্খণের', 'ছুই', 'আমর!', 'সোঁম'). About 30 verses contain OCR artifacts: double virama (1.10.11, 4.2.20, 4.17.9…), '!' inside words (1.45.8, 4.35.5…), and '- ' line-break hyphens (1.2.6, 2.1.1…). Curated data: RV 10.90.5 Bengali-script Sanskrit contains a Devanagari 'ळ' ('বিরাळজায়ত'), 1.1.1 IAST has the non-IAST 'hōtāraṁ', and fullbleed's cover says 'c. 1500 – 500 BCE' while its title page says 'c. 1500 – 1200 BCE'.
vedas.evidence: Printed 1.137 and 5.24 verse by verse. 'হেইন্্র' appears in scripts/output/archive_ocr_bengali.json. Regex counts over the mb fields: double-virama 9, bang-in-word 9, hyphen-break 12. Curated scan: one Devanagari character inside sa_bengali (rigveda 10.90.5), one 'ō'.
vedas.repro: Open /vedas/rigveda.html#5.24. The Bengali under 'O AGNI, be our nearest Friend' addresses Indra and contains broken characters.
vedas.fix: Re-run the merge with a check that each Bengali meaning belongs to the same hymn as its Sanskrit, prefer ebanglalibrary over archive OCR for 5.24 and 1.137, and flag verses matching the OCR-artifact regexes for manual cleanup. Fix the three curated typos in reader.html VEDAS_DATA (the canonical copy), then rebuild mobile/theater/pdf and sync fullbleed.
verifier_corrections: The '!' inside words class (1.45.8, 4.35.5, 8.4.17, 10.92.13…) is mostly a missing space after a vocative '!', which is cosmetic. Real garbling ('আমর!') appears only in the 5.24 OCR. The fullbleed dates are at fullbleed.html:452 (cover) and :594 (buildTitlePage), not :111. The two curated typos also appear in seeds/hymns.json and the three generated readers, which pick them up on rebuild.

vedas.title: Vedas docs have drifted from the code: sizes, settings, script-toggle claims, trees, stale inline template
vedas.detail: (1) CLAUDE.md:33/135 and index.html:664 say mandala files are 264 KB–1.1 MB ('Mandala 2 costs 264 KB'). They are actually 543 KB–2.3 MB raw (149–628 KB gzip). (2) CLAUDE.md:24 lists reader.html settings as font/size/width, but there is no font picker. (3) CLAUDE.md:55 says theater and pdf-reader script toggles are 'inherited from prefs'. Each has its own key (vedas-theater-prefs / vedas-pdf-prefs) and no toggle UI, so IAST can never be shown there. theater also has no theme control on phones (.dots{display:none} ≤480px). (4) AGENT_README.md:68-73 lists only 'reader / fullbleed / rigveda' for vedas. (5) The root .project/todo.md, which the Resolution says was reconciled, still reads 'vedas/ 3 formats + build script', 'rigveda-samhita.md 3.8 MB', 'rigveda-complete.json 5.1 MB', and a Books table row '2 (reader, fullbleed)'. (6) index.html:858 and the sources section credit 'Griffith, 1896' for all the English, but some verses (for example 8.60, 8.66, 8.67) use a different, modern-prose translation. (7) build_rigveda.py:375-780 still contains the old inline template (4 themes, rv-prefs storing the position, pre-fix observers). If data/rigveda-template.html is ever missing, the build silently falls back to it at :842 and brings back all the P0 bugs.
vedas.evidence: stat sizes vs the quoted figures. reader.html settings panel contains Text Size / Page Width / Show-Hide only. theater/pdf templates have no toggle UI and use separate keys. grep of AGENT_README and the root todo. build_rigveda.py:842 falls back to HTML_TEMPLATE.
vedas.repro: Compare vedas/CLAUDE.md with `ls -la vedas/data` and with the reader.html settings panel.
vedas.fix: Update the sizes and feature lists. Document theater/pdf as having fixed script defaults, or add toggles or share one prefs key. Update the AGENT_README tree and the root todo rows. Remove the inline HTML_TEMPLATE and fail the build if the template is missing. Credit the English per verse or as 'Griffith (with other translations in places)'.
verifier_corrections: The status is mixed, not simply 'regression'. Only the root todo items (5) are a true regression: the old audit flagged them and the Resolution says the todos were reconciled. Items (1), (2), (3), (7), the Griffith credit in (6), and the AGENT_README tree drift in (4) are 'new'. Most of that drift came in with the 2026-08-27 commit that added mobile, theater and pdf-reader, after the audit. Small precision fixes. In (7) the fallback is not fully silent: it prints 'Using inline template (external not found)', but the build still succeeds and ships the old template. In (6) the substitute English is Wilson/Sāyaṇa-style 19th-century prose (e.g. 1.179, which Griffith left in Latin), not 'modern' prose. It also carries OCR run-ons such as 'ourofferings', 'hiding-plural ce' and 'north firm gods'. Also stale: vedas/CLAUDE.md:33 and :128 say the shell is ~44-45 KB (it is 47 KB), and todo:37 says rigveda-complete.json is 5.1 MB (it is 13.1 MB). Line numbers are correct as cited.

vedas.title: rigveda phones: the progress bar is covered by the sūkta strip
vedas.detail: #progress-track is fixed at top:102px (z-index 997). At ≤768px the mobile rules grow #mandala-row and #sukta-row to 40px each, so #nav-strip (z-index 998) runs from 44px to 125px and covers the bar. Phone readers get no progress indicator and no tap-to-jump bar, which is also one of the few ways to change mandala without swiping the tab row.
vedas.evidence: At 390 and 320: progress top=102, nav-strip bottom=125. document.elementFromPoint at the bar's y returns a .s-pill. At 1440 it returns #progress-track (nav bottom 103).
vedas.repro: Open /vedas/rigveda.html#5.40 at 390px. No accent progress line is visible under the nav.
vedas.fix: Inside @media(max-width:768px) set #progress-track{top:124px} (or derive it from the nav height), and raise #content padding-top to match.
verifier_corrections: Status 'new' is acceptable, but this is a side effect of the 2026-08-20 P0 fix (commit c9cb7d0). That fix raised the mobile nav rows to 40px and #content padding-top to 138px, but left #progress-track at top:102px. The fix is to set #progress-track{top:124px} inside the same @media(max-width:768px) block (lines 146-157).

Affects every width ≤768px, including tablets at exactly 768, not just phones. Introduced by the previous audit's fix commit c9cb7d0, so it could be labelled a side-effect regression, though 'new' (not previously reported) is acceptable. The claim that it removes 'one of the few ways to change mandala' is overstated: the bar is 2px tall and was never a viable touch target. The primary line is rigveda-template.html:104, with the conflicting rules at 153/155. Regenerate rigveda.html after fixing.

vedas.title: fullbleed phones: the book-spine line runs down the middle of every single-page view
vedas.detail: On phones only the right half is shown, at 100% width. #book::after (a 1px spine at left:50%) is still drawn, so a vertical rule cuts through the Sanskrit and meaning text on every page.
vedas.evidence: At 390, #book::after is at left=195px, width 1px, background var(--spine). Screenshot work/vedas/fb-p10.m.png shows the line crossing the Gayatri text.
vedas.fix: Add #book::after{display:none} (and hide the left-page shadow) inside @media(max-width:768px).
verifier_corrections: Also hide the #right-half::before spine shadow on phones (fullbleed.html:97-102). This was introduced by the prior audit's single-page phone fix, so it is a side effect of that fix rather than an unrelated new bug.

vedas.title: rigveda has no hashchange handler, so the URL and the content fall out of step (reader and fullbleed too)
vedas.detail: parseHash() runs only once, at load. If the reader edits the hash, opens a bookmark or shared #M.S link in a tab already on rigveda.html, or a script sets location.hash, the address bar changes but the page stays on the old sūkta. A link copied at that point does not match what is on screen. reader.html (#ch-N) and fullbleed.html (#p-N) behave the same way. mobile, theater and pdf-reader all handle hashchange.
vedas.evidence: On rigveda.html#1.1, location.hash='#10.129' → hash '#10.129' but the header still reads 'MANDALA 1 · SŪKTA 1 Agni'. A same-document page.goto from #3.62 to #10.129, #1.1 or #8.70 left 3.62 on screen every time.
vedas.repro: Open /vedas/rigveda.html#1.1, change the address bar to …#10.129 and press Enter. The Nāsadīya hymn does not appear.
vedas.fix: Add window.addEventListener('hashchange', ()=>{ const [m,s]=[mIdx,sIdx]; parseHash(); if(m!==mIdx||s!==sIdx) render(); }). Do the same with restoreHash / spreadFromHash in reader and fullbleed.
verifier_corrections: Severity low rather than medium: the scenario is niche, it corrects itself on the next navigation, and no house convention requires a hashchange handler. Scope: the same omission exists in alice-in-wonderland/{fullbleed,mobile,pdf-reader}.html, aurelius-meditations/{reader,fullbleed}.html and gibran-prophet/{fullbleed,mobile,pdf-reader,theater}.html, so a fix belongs in the library-wide hash guidance (AGENT_README URL Hash State), not only in vedas.

Severity low, not medium. AGENT_README only mandates write-on-navigate and restore-on-load, which all three pages do. No in-page link triggers the bug, and a reload fixes it. The same gap exists in other books' fullbleed/index pages, so this is not vedas-specific. The cited fullbleed line 703 is the #s- regex. The function starts at 697 (spreadFromHash). Relevant init call sites: rigveda-template.html:541, fullbleed.html:866-867, and reader.html's restoreHash call site.

vedas.title: rigveda loading: two quick mandala switches in fallback mode load the wrong mandala; a failed load leaves a blank page
vedas.detail: The <script> fallback, used for file:// and whenever fetch fails, keeps a single global window._rvLoad. When two mandala loads overlap, the second overwrites the first's callback. The first file then puts its data into the second mandala's slot, and the second file throws 'window._rvLoad is not a function'. After that the 'Mandala 7' tab shows Mandala 5's text for the rest of the session. If both fetch and script fail (for example a dropped connection partway through a 2 MB mandala), the promise rejection is unhandled. The page stays blank on first load, or stuck on 'Loading Mandala N…', with no message or retry.
vedas.evidence: JSON blocked: clicking Mandala 5 then Mandala 7 together → header 'MANDALA 5 · SŪKTA 63', RV.m[6]._loaded true, RV.m[4]._loaded false, pageerror 'window._rvLoad is not a function'. JSON and JS both blocked: #content '' and indicator '', pageerror 'Cannot load mandala 3'. The normal fallback path works (json blocked → 3.62 renders; file:// → 10.129 renders).
vedas.repro: Open file:///…/vedas/rigveda.html, click Mandala 5 and then Mandala 7 quickly. The Mandala 7 tab is active but shows Mandala 5 hymns.
vedas.fix: Have the .js files call window._rvLoad(n, data), dispatch to a per-mandala resolver map, and check data.n. Catch load errors in render()/goToSukta(), show an error message with a retry button, and restore the previous mandala.
verifier_corrections: Repro: use HTTP with the JSON blocked (or a flaky network), not file://; on file:// the race window is a few ms and did not trigger the wrong mandala in testing. Extra symptom: a failed tab switch leaves an inconsistent state. The bottom scroll observer (still attached) appends an empty 'Sūkta 2' stub under 'Loading Mandala N...' and rewrites the hash to #N.2, while the tabs and strip still show the previous mandala. Relevant lines: rigveda-template.html:224-243 (ensureMandala), 297-320 (render), 391-395 (goToSukta), 541 (init).

site.title: Catalog dark theme: chip labels, author lines and meta text fail contrast (2.96:1)
site.detail: In the dark theme the catalog's main navigation (48 reader chips, 11-12px uppercase mono) plus the author/year lines (11px), the header meta (10px) and the footer (10px) all use --dim #546080. On the #0f1322 card that is 2.96:1, and on the #0b0e18 page background 3.08:1; small text needs 4.5:1. Since the last audit's fix, dark is chosen automatically for every visitor whose OS is in dark mode, so this is the default look for many readers. The light theme passes (5.06:1 on the card).
site.evidence: Playwright with colorScheme 'dark' at 1440, 390 and 320: chip computed color rgb(84,96,128) on card rgb(15,19,34), and the computed WCAG ratio is 2.96. Screenshot work/site/catalog-m320-dark.png. Dark --text #8490aa would give 6.01:1.
