site.title: JavaScript smooth scrolling ignores prefers-reduced-motion everywhere, and six pages still run page-flip or slide animations
site.detail: Fourteen pages call scrollTo/scrollBy/scrollIntoView with {behavior:'smooth'}, and none of them checks the reduced-motion setting first; only khayyam fullbleed and theater check it in JavaScript at all. The Meditations and Homer readers have a CSS rule (scroll-behavior:auto !important), but CSS cannot override an explicit 'smooth' in JavaScript, so these pages look compliant yet still glide. With reduced motion on, pressing j animates the scroll in all 10 scroll readers, and a sidebar chapter jump in Meditations glides across about 55,000px. Pages with no reduced-motion rule still run 3D page flips and slide transitions: alice fullbleed and meditations fullbleed (700ms flip), alice mobile (600ms flip), alice single (350ms), alice theater and prophet theater (500ms). CSS `html{scroll-behavior:smooth}` stays on with reduced motion in the prophet index, illustrations and reader; the khayyam index and reader; the vedas reader and rigveda; the alice reader, scroll and web-reader; and odyssey study, whose reduced-motion rule only zeroes transitions. The Alice, Prophet, Meditations and Vedas instances were reported by those books' audit passes. What is new here is that the JavaScript path defeats even the pages that were fixed.
site.evidence: Playwright with reducedMotion:'reduce' (matchMedia confirmed true). Sampling scrollY every animation frame after pressing j: 29 distinct positions (0>2>8>18>32>51…765) in the alice, meditations (both), prophet, homer (both), khayyam and vedas readers and in alice scroll and web-reader. A sidebar jump in the meditations reader went 765>825>1006>1312…55736 over 43 frames. document.getAnimations() 60ms after a page turn, with reduced motion on: transform@flip-overlay 700ms (alice fullbleed, meditations fullbleed), 600ms (alice mobile); opacity+transform@chapter-view 500ms (prophet theater); @passage 500ms (alice theater); @card 350ms (alice single). The Homer and Khayyam fullbleed, theater, mobile and pdf pages, prophet fullbleed and mobile, and the Vedas paged formats ran nothing, so they comply.
site.repro: In DevTools > Rendering, emulate prefers-reduced-motion: reduce. Open aurelius-meditations/reader.html and press j, or pick Book 6 in the sidebar: the page still scrolls with animation.
site.fix: In each page, compute the behaviour once, e.g. const SMOOTH = matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches ? 'auto' : 'smooth', and pass behavior: SMOOTH everywhere. Add @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce){html{scroll-behavior:auto} *{transition-duration:.01ms!important;animation-duration:.01ms!important}} to the pages that lack it. In the flip code, skip the overlay when reduced motion is on, as khayyam fullbleed does.
verifier_corrections: The count of 14 is right, but only if homer-odyssey/study.html's single JS smooth call is included along with the 13 reader-type pages. homer-iliad/index.html and homer-odyssey/index.html also set html{scroll-behavior:smooth}, but they override it correctly under reduced motion and are not affected. The line citations are accurate.

13 served pages, not 14, call smooth scroll from JS: alice pdf-reader, reader, scroll, web-reader; meditations reader and reader-casaubon; prophet pdf-reader and reader; both Homer readers; khayyam reader; vedas reader and rigveda. The data/ templates add more. Add alice-in-wonderland/index.html (a spread reader) to the pages that still animate: with reduced motion on, ArrowRight runs a 600ms transform on .flip-layer plus 600ms opacity on .flip-shadow, and the file has no prefers-reduced-motion rule.

The line ranges are accurate (the Iliad calls are 713-718). The pattern is not Homer-specific. Every reader in the site uses the same keyboard handler with explicit behavior:'smooth', and none has a JS matchMedia guard:
- aurelius-meditations/reader.html:7956-7960 and reader-casaubon.html
- alice-in-wonderland/reader.html:2042-2055
- gibran-prophet/reader.html:2049-2056
- khayyam-rubaiyat/reader.html:1287-1294
- vedas/reader.html:1091-1097
Most of these also use smooth scrollTo for TOC and back-to-top jumps. Those four (not Aurelius) have no prefers-reduced-motion CSS at all, so any site-wide fix should also cover these templates.

site.title: Greek and transliterated Persian lack a valid lang attribute (Meditations, Odyssey study, Rubáiyát reader)
site.detail: AGENT_README:122 requires lang on every change of language. Greek: the Meditations reader has 23,797 Greek word spans (.gw) under lang="en", plus 23 Greek runs in the Casaubon notes, the landing subtitle 'Τὰ εἰς ἑαυτόν' and the pdf-reader intro. Odyssey study.html, whose main content is Greek, has 2,505 Greek word spans (.w) under lang="en" and no grc tag anywhere. Persian: the Khayyam reader tags 236 transliteration lines lang="en-fa-Latn", which is not a valid BCP 47 tag (it should be fa-Latn), and 3,454 English text nodes sit inside lang="fa" containers. Screen readers pronounce the Greek with English rules and read the English notes in a Persian voice. The Meditations and Khayyam instances overlap those books' audit passes; Odyssey study is new.
site.evidence: Playwright walk over every text node, resolving the nearest [lang] and detecting the script by Unicode block. aurelius-meditations/reader.html: 23,797 Greek nodes under en. homer-odyssey/study.html: 2,505 Greek under en (span.w 'ἄνδρα', 'μοι', 'ἔννεπε'). khayyam-rubaiyat/reader.html: 236 Persian-script nodes under en-fa-Latn and 3,454 Latin nodes under fa (h4.qd-label 'Modern rendering'). grep: study.html has no lang attribute other than html's 'en'.
site.repro: Open homer-odyssey/study.html and inspect any Greek word: its nearest lang ancestor is <html lang="en">.
site.fix: Put lang="grc" on the Greek line or block container (in the study-template line renderer and in the Greek block wrapper in assemble-reader.py), once per block rather than per word, and lang="grc-Latn" on transliterations. In build_reader.py change en-fa-Latn to fa-Latn, and wrap the English notes inside fa containers in lang="en".
verifier_corrections: Khayyam: the reader has 2,256 transliteration elements tagged en-fa-Latn, not 236. The 236 'Persian-script nodes under en-fa-Latn' are transliteration strings with a leaked Arabic hamza U+0654 (e.g. 'brsaz tranhٔ v pysh āvr my'), which is a transliteration defect, not a lang one. The transliteration is also a bare consonant skeleton ('my nvsh kh 'mr javdany ayn ast'); treat that as a separate content issue if it is not reported elsewhere. There is one more en-fa-Latn at build_reader.py:501. The English-under-fa source is the article wrapper at build_reader.py:350, which puts the whole detail panel, including its English labels and translations, under lang=fa and dir=rtl. Meditations mobile, theater and pdf-reader already use lang="grc" once each, and reader-template reuse could follow them.

Scope is wider for the Odyssey. Its Greek edition in reader.html, fullbleed.html, mobile.html, pdf-reader.html and theater.html (generated from homer-odyssey/data/*-template.html) also has no grc tag, about 65k Greek characters per page, not only study.html. For Meditations, only reader.html, reader-casaubon.html (about 36 Greek runs, not 23) and index.html are affected; mobile, pdf-reader and theater already use lang="grc". The '236 Persian-script nodes under en-fa-Latn' are not a lang problem: they are stray U+0654 (hamza above) characters the transliterator leaves in 236 lines (e.g. 'brsaz tranhٔ'), a separate content bug. en-fa-Latn is documented at khayyam-rubaiyat/CLAUDE.md:243 and in practice resolves to an English voice, so that sub-item is low. The fix should use a valid tag that AT still reads in an English voice, and should be tested rather than blindly switched to fa-Latn.

site.title: Esc does not close open panels in five pages: an error in Alice's reader, no handling in two PDF readers and Homer's mobile sheets
site.detail: AGENT_README:90 documents 'Esc to close panels', and the Prophet and Khayyam CLAUDE.md files repeat it. (1) alice reader.html: the Escape case calls themeDropdown.classList.remove at line 2062, but themeDropdown is never declared, so it throws a ReferenceError. closeSidebar() on the next line never runs, and the chapter sidebar stays open on desktop and phone. (2) The alice and prophet pdf-readers never close the thumbnail or chapter sidebar on Esc; only the page-number box handles Esc. The meditations and khayyam pdf-readers do close it. (3) Homer mobile.html (both books) has no keydown listener at all, so the book-list and theme bottom sheets stay open. Every other mobile.html closes its sheets and traps focus. Minor: on touch, tapping the theme button adds .expanded to #theme-wrap, and Esc does not clear it in the alice, prophet, khayyam and homer readers or in alice fullbleed (the meditations reader, casaubon and fullbleed do clear it).
site.evidence: Playwright, alice reader: click #sidebar-toggle → #chapter-sidebar open=true at x=0 → Escape → still open, with page error 'themeDropdown is not defined' (at 1440 and 390). alice and prophet pdf-reader: #sidebar gains .open and keeps it after Escape, at both sizes. Homer mobile (both books): #book-sheet and #theme-sheet keep .open after Escape, and grep finds no keydown in either mobile template. Verified closing correctly: all other reader sidebars and settings panels, the meditations and khayyam pdf sidebars, the prophet, meditations, khayyam and vedas mobile sheets, the rigveda sūkta grid, and the study popover.
site.repro: Open alice-in-wonderland/reader.html, click ☰, press Esc: the sidebar stays open and the console shows a ReferenceError.
site.fix: Alice reader: remove the themeDropdown and themeBtnEl lines (or guard them) and clear themeWrap.expanded instead. pdf-readers: add case 'Escape': closeSidebar() to the document keydown handler. Homer mobile: add a keydown handler that closes any open .sheet and returns focus to the button that opened it, reusing the focus-trap code from gibran-prophet/mobile.html.
verifier_corrections: The Homer sheets are role="dialog" aria-modal="true" (homer-iliad/data/mobile-template.html:135,139), so they also lack the focus trap the modal role promises. That is worth stating in the fix. Status 'new' is right: the Alice bug dates from 2026-04-03 and the previous audit missed it.

AGENT_README.md:90 (and prophet CLAUDE.md:58, khayyam CLAUDE.md:170) scope 'Esc closes panels' to reader.html. The pdf-reader part is therefore a general a11y expectation, not a documented house convention. The Homer mobile part violates the documented sheet pattern (khayyam-rubaiyat/CLAUDE.md:263) and its own aria-modal=true. The Alice pdf-reader's page-number box does not handle Esc either; only Prophet's does (:938). Workarounds exist (the overlay click or ☰), which keeps this at medium.

site.title: Rubáiyát: regenerating the Persian seed permanently deletes all its notes, and the inputs to restore them are not in the repo
site.detail: CLAUDE.md says the fetch/parse scripts 'regenerate seeds/ and need network access' and gives no warning. But fetch_persian.py writes seeds/persian.json from scratch, keeping only num, lines and source_title for each quatrain. That drops the literal and poetic renderings, theme, note and _meta, plus the fg_1st/fg_5th/whinfield match refs that link English quatrains to their Persian source. The only script that puts them back, merge_annotations.py, reads /tmp/rubaiyat/annotations_batch_*.json, which were never committed. So one documented command destroys machine-generated notes that cannot be regenerated; only git history can restore them. parse_pg38511.py likewise reads /tmp/rubaiyat/pg38511.txt, which no script downloads; the docs call it a network step, but it needs a hand-placed file.
site.evidence: Line 138 builds out = {source, edition, license, language, direction, count, quatrains} from freshly parsed pages, and line 148 overwrites seeds/persian.json with it. Committed quatrain keys are num, lines, source_title, literal, poetic, theme, note, fg_1st, fg_5th and whinfield. Running in the copy: parse_pg38511.py prints 'ERROR: source file not found: /tmp/rubaiyat/pg38511.txt'; merge_annotations.py prints 'No batch files found in /tmp/rubaiyat'. I then wrote persian.json in fetch_persian's output shape and rebuilt: reader.html fell from 1,910,087 to 965,289 bytes, and fullbleed facing glosses fell from 806 to 589.
site.repro: In a copy: 1) python3 khayyam-rubaiyat/data/fetch_persian.py with network, or emulate its output by keeping only num, lines and source_title per quatrain. 2) python3 data/merge_annotations.py prints 'No batch files found'. 3) python3 data/build_reader.py and data/build_fullbleed.py. 4) Every modern rendering, note and theme is gone from the readers.
site.fix: Make fetch_persian.py merge into the existing seed: load seeds/persian.json and update only lines and source_title per num. Commit the annotation batches under khayyam-rubaiyat/data/annotations/, or delete merge_annotations.py and document persian.json as the hand-curated source of truth. Add the pg38511 download URL to parse_pg38511.py. Add a warning to CLAUDE.md.
verifier_corrections: Minor points. Theater.html is not affected, since it has no Persian apparatus; reader, fullbleed, mobile and pdf-reader all lose roughly half their size. The 965,289 figure is the builder's printed count; the on-disk size is 982,792 bytes. fetch_fitzgerald.py also uses /tmp/rubaiyat as its cache, so every step of the 'regenerate seeds/' pipeline depends on /tmp state that is not in the repo.

Line cite: khayyam-rubaiyat/CLAUDE.md:48 is the 'data/ <- templates + build scripts (never web-served)' line, which is unrelated. The relevant doc lines are CLAUDE.md:45-46 (persian.json holds the annotations), 60-62 (the script list) and 82-84. Line 48's claim that data/ is 'never web-served' is itself false under .nojekyll, but that is a separate docs issue. Scope note: the damage requires running fetch_persian.py, which the docs call non-routine, and then committing. `git checkout seeds/persian.json` recovers it, so this is a maintainer data-loss hazard, not something readers see today.

site.title: 39 of the 43 non-index reader pages have no link to their book's landing page or the catalog; the Meditations landing page also has no link back
site.detail: Only 4 readers link back to their landing page: khayyam-rubaiyat/fullbleed.html, khayyam-rubaiyat/theater.html, homer-odyssey/study.html and homer-odyssey/illustrated.html. Homer theater, pdf-reader and fullbleed link only '← Reader' to reader.html. None of the other readers link to index.html, ../ or lib.sadh.app: all 8 Alice readers, all 6 Meditations readers, all 6 Prophet readers, Iliad and Odyssey reader/mobile, Khayyam reader/mobile/pdf-reader, and all 6 Vedas readers. The Meditations landing (aurelius-meditations/index.html) and Alice's index.html have no link to the catalog, while the Prophet, Iliad, Odyssey, Khayyam and Vedas landing pages do ('← LIB.SADH.APP'). A reader arriving from a shared deep link (the site's whole reading-position model is shareable URL hashes) cannot find other formats, other books or the library without editing the URL. That is not practical in in-app browsers or a home-screen web app.
site.evidence: Link matrix from the Playwright DOM crawl (work/site/links.json): 'root=- landing=- sib=0' for the pages above. grep -cE 'index\.html|href="\.\./?"|lib\.sadh\.app' returns 0 for 39 reader files.
site.repro: Open http://localhost:8111/vedas/rigveda.html#3.62 (or homer-odyssey/mobile.html) and look in every menu, sheet and panel for a link to the Vedas landing or lib.sadh.app. There is none.
site.fix: Add a small '← {Book}' link to index.html (plus 'lib.sadh.app' to ../) in each format's menu, sidebar or settings sheet, via the data/*-template.html sources and rebuild. Add a link to ../ on the Meditations landing and on Alice's index. Add 'every reader links to its landing page' to the AGENT_README baseline.
verifier_corrections: Add alice-in-wonderland/index.html, a reader in its own right, to the affected list (40 readers). Note that the 4 mobile pages marked apple-mobile-web-app-capable (Alice, Prophet, Iliad and Odyssey mobile.html) become true dead ends when launched from a home screen. For Alice, the missing landing page is a known still-open item, so the fix there is a catalog link.

Homer is not the only book whose readers link to reader.html. gibran-prophet/illustrations.html, mobile.html, pdf-reader.html and theater.html also link to reader.html (mobile.html also links to fullbleed.html), but not to the landing page or the catalog. alice-in-wonderland/index.html is not a landing page. It is a reader, and the old audit's Alice consolidation plan documents Alice as having no landing page, so that part overlaps a known open item. The missing link on the Meditations landing is new.

site.title: Homer readers save reading position in localStorage (book/page), which the house rules forbid
site.detail: Nine shipped pages write the reading position into localStorage. fullbleed, mobile and pdf-reader in both books store {"book":N,...} inside {book}-{format}-prefs, and they write it on every page load even when the user does nothing. theater stores the position in a separate iliad-theater-book / odyssey-theater-book key, and splits its settings across three keys (-book, -edition, -theme) instead of one JSON object. Odyssey illustrated stores a global `page` index in odyssey-illustrated-prefs. When a page loads without a hash, init() reads this value and resumes there. So the catalog link, a hashless bookmark, or a second tab opens mid-book for returning readers, and the URL no longer says where they are. AGENT_README:159 explicitly forbids this. The Homer CLAUDE.md files document the -book key, which contradicts AGENT_README. None of the other 42 pages stores position.
site.evidence: Playwright, 1440x900 and 390x844, starting with empty storage, navigating to Book VI. localStorage then held: iliad-fullbleed-prefs {"book":5,"edition":"pope","theme":"light-purple"}; iliad-mobile-prefs {"book":5,...}; iliad-theater-book "5"; odyssey-illustrated-prefs {"theme":"light-purple","page":5}; the odyssey fullbleed/mobile/theater equivalents were the same. Loading the bare URL (no hash) in the same profile then opened at #bk-pope-6 (fullbleed, mobile and theater, both books) and at #bk-1-p5 (illustrated). The theme-change sweep of all 51 pages found position in storage nowhere else.
site.repro: Open homer-iliad/fullbleed.html and click 'Next Book →' five times. Then open homer-iliad/fullbleed.html with no hash (for example from the root catalog): it lands on Book VI. DevTools > Application > Local Storage shows "book":5.
site.fix: Remove `book` and `page` from the settings objects and stop writing *-theater-book (ignore it if found). Merge theater's -edition and -theme into one {iliad|odyssey}-theater-prefs JSON object, reading the old keys as a fallback. Rely on the #bk-… hash alone for position, then rebuild with data/build.py and correct the key lists in both Homer CLAUDE.md files.
verifier_corrections: Drop the claim that 'the URL no longer says where they are'. On resume, the page writes the hash for the restored book or page with replaceState, so the URL is correct. All cited line numbers are accurate.

Drop 'the URL no longer says where they are'. The resumed position is written back to the hash. Add the shared-link overwrite (a write on every load clobbers the saved position) and illustrated's viewport-dependent page index as the concrete harms. Page count and line numbers are correct.

Take the index-page key (homer-iliad/index.html:254, homer-odyssey/index.html:263) out of this Homer finding, or restate it as site-wide: meditations, prophet, rubaiyat, iliad and odyssey index pages all use `{book}-index-theme`. The rest of the file and line citations are accurate. homer-iliad/CLAUDE.md covers 185-186.

site.title: Position fixes were made in one book's copy of a shared template but not in the sibling copy (Alice fullbleed page turns; Prophet reader restore race and phone redirect)
site.detail: (a) alice fullbleed: the desktop page-turn functions flipForward/flipBackward never write the hash; only renderSpread does. Prophet's copy gained writeHashForSpread() and is fixed, yet prophet's CLAUDE.md still calls the gap open. Alice desktop readers therefore lose their page on reload. (b) prophet reader: after the last audit, Alice's copy gained a `restoringHash` guard (it captures the target first and blocks the scroll observer until the restore lands). Prophet's copy of the same restoreHash() did not get it and still sometimes lands on chapter 1. (c) prophet reader: its phone redirect, location.replace('mobile.html'), drops location.hash even though mobile.html uses the same #ch-N form, so a shared chapter link opens the title slide on phones. The Prophet audit pass reports (b) and (c) separately; they are grouped here because the root cause is the same: fixes not carried across template copies.
site.evidence: alice fullbleed at 1440px: load #p-11, press ArrowRight 4 times → page number 19, hash still #p-11 → reload → page 11. Prophet and Meditations under the same test: 19, #p-19, reload 19. Fresh loads of prophet reader.html#ch-14 at desktop size: 2 of 12 ended on #ch-1 (the URL was rewritten to #ch-1, scrollY 308). The Alice, Meditations, Vedas and Khayyam readers failed 0 of 8. With an iPhone user agent at 390px, gibran-prophet/reader.html#ch-14 went to gibran-prophet/mobile.html with no hash.
site.repro: (a) Open alice-in-wonderland/fullbleed.html#p-11 at 1440px, press → four times, reload: you are back on page 11. (c) Open gibran-prophet/reader.html#ch-14 on a phone: it opens mobile.html at the title slide.
site.fix: Copy prophet's writeHashForSpread() calls into Alice's flip functions. Copy Alice's restoringHash and captured-target logic into prophet's restoreHash(). Change the redirect to location.replace('mobile.html' + location.hash). Consider building both books from one shared reader/fullbleed template so fixes cannot drift apart again.
verifier_corrections: Severity should be high, driven by (b). The Prophet reader's hash restore fails on most loads (about 75-100% across my runs), not 2 of 12, so reload and deep links into reader.html usually land on chapter 1. (a) is medium on its own. The Prophet audit pass reports (b) and (c) separately, so dedupe there. Add the docs drift to the locations: alice-in-wonderland/.project/todo.md:49 marks the fullbleed hash as done, and gibran-prophet/CLAUDE.md:70-72 describes a gap that is already fixed in Prophet.

(b) is far more frequent than '2 of 12': in my runs, 11 of 12 fresh desktop loads of a Prophet chapter link landed on chapter 1 with the URL rewritten. It affects opening a bookmark or shared link, not a same-tab reload, which browser scroll restoration saves. On its own, (b) is close to high for the Prophet reader. Also stale: gibran-prophet/CLAUDE.md:70-72 still lists the fullbleed flip-hash gap that prophet's own todo (.project/todo.md:30-31) marks fixed. The cited line numbers are correct.

site.title: Page weight: 20 pages over 1 MB, 31.7 MB of repeated payloads across formats, and the illustrated Odyssey pulls 6.9 MB of 2048px plates on first open on a phone
site.detail: The 51 live pages total 60.1 MB of HTML, plus 0.52 MB of templates. Pages over 1 MB (raw / gzip): homer-odyssey fullbleed, mobile, pdf-reader, reader and theater at 4.42 MB / 1.52 MB each, study.html 5.62 / 1.38; homer-iliad's 5 formats at 2.62 / 0.97 each; aurelius-meditations reader.html 3.15 / 0.60, mobile, theater and pdf-reader 1.22 / 0.38 each, reader-casaubon 1.11 / 0.29; khayyam-rubaiyat reader 1.97 / 0.39, fullbleed 1.54, mobile and pdf-reader 1.50 (about 0.36 gz). The same payload is embedded byte-for-byte in several files: Odyssey EDITIONS (3.87 MB) x5, Iliad EDITIONS (2.58 MB) x5, Khayyam DATA (1.45 MB) x3, Meditations DATA (1.03 MB) x3, Alice CHAPTERS (151 KB) x7. That is 31.7 MB of the 60.6 MB of HTML, and a reader switching formats downloads it again (about 1.5 MB gz each time for the Odyssey). The phone format ships everything: homer-odyssey/mobile.html carries all 6 editions x 24 books to show one book of one edition. The illustrated edition's plates are 2048x2048 JPEGs of 1.6-2.9 MB each. Opening illustrated.html at 390px downloaded 4 JPEGs (6.9 MB) to show a title plate rendered 346px wide. Parsing is not the bottleneck: with 4x CPU throttling, study.html reached DOMContentLoaded in 1.4 s and the Meditations reader (41,609 DOM nodes) in 1.3 s. The cost is transfer on mobile data. Shipping each mandala as both .json and .js (2 x 11.5 MB) is intentional, for file:// fallback.
site.evidence: stat and gzip -6 sizes. md5 of large const literals across pages (script in the session log). work/site/weight.js timings. work/site/illus.js: 'jpeg requests 4 bytes 6909448', naturalWidth 2048 vs a rendered width of 346.
site.repro: Open http://localhost:8111/homer-odyssey/illustrated.html at 390x844 with DevTools Network open: about 6.9 MB of JPEG before the first page turn.
site.fix: Generate 800/1200/1600px WebP or JPEG derivatives of the plates, served with srcset/sizes, and keep the 2048px masters out of the published tree. Limit plate preloading to the next plate only. For the mobile formats, consider splitting payloads per edition or per book, lazy-loaded the way rigveda.html already does with a script-tag fallback for file://. Or accept the self-contained trade-off and record it in the README.
verifier_corrections: The '6.9 MB / 4 JPEGs' figure is inflated. It comes from Playwright request interception disabling the cache, so each plate was counted twice. The real first-open cost is 2 plates, 3.45 MB (4.2 MB with the HTML). Plate sizes range 0.96-3.15 MB across 101 plates, not 1.6-2.9 MB. The cross-format payload duplication should be framed as the documented self-contained trade-off (AGENT_README.md:9-10,173; README.md:118), not as a defect; the actionable defect is the plate sizing and preloading at homer-odyssey/data/illustrated-template.html:714 and :850-856, which is the source for homer-odyssey/illustrated.html. Related scope for the 'keep masters out of the published tree' fix: homer-odyssey/img/attic/ (353 MB, 141 tracked files) and img/characters/ (112 MB, 63 files) are git-tracked and publicly served under .nojekyll, 662 MB of images in all. That exposure may deserve its own finding.

The first open fetches 2 unique plates (3.46 MB), not 4 (6.9 MB); the extra requests were repeats of the same files. The bigger cost is the first page turn: the Book I splash (#bk-1-p1) loads 5 more 2048px plates to display them about 70px wide, for 11.0 MB total after one tap. Payload sizes in bytes: Odyssey EDITIONS 4.40 MB, Meditations DATA 1.21 MB; redundant copies are about 34 MB. The duplication across formats is the documented self-contained convention, so treat that part as a trade-off to record, not a bug. Related, and outside this finding: homer-odyssey/img/ is 662 MB in git, including a 353 MB img/attic/ of prototypes and gemini-originals, all publicly served.

site.title: About 557 MB (66%) of the published site is files no page uses; the site is at about 85% of GitHub Pages' 1 GB cap and on course to pass it
site.detail: Because of .nojekyll, the whole tracked tree is published: 847.04 MB in 535 files. Pages use only 60.1 MB of live HTML, 207.1 MB of illustrated plates and 23.1 MB of Rigveda mandala data. site.title: Meditations: collect_texts.py silently drops all 412 Casaubon passages, and align_casaubon_long.py cannot run
site.detail: CLAUDE.md documents `python3 data/collect_texts.py (stdlib only, no pip deps)` as the pipeline that 'fetches and aligns all three translations' into the canonical aurelius-meditations.json. Casaubon is not fetched, though: it is read from /tmp/meditations_chapters.json, which nothing in the repo produces. When that file is missing, the script prints a warning ('Run the reader build first', but no build writes it) and writes the JSON with every book's casaubon.passages empty. Greek and Long are fetched from `master` rather than a pinned commit, so a rerun today also changes 17 Greek passages (upstream swapped U+0313 elision marks for U+02BC/U+2019), and that change would flow into reader, mobile, theater and pdf-reader on rebuild. The documented `python3 data/align_casaubon_long.py` always fails: its input data/texts/meditations-complete.json is written by no script, since collect_texts now writes ../aurelius-meditations.json. The two are also circular, because collect_texts reads casaubon-long-alignment.json, which align_casaubon_long writes. CLAUDE.md also lists assemble-annotations.py/.js as assemblers. Both rewrite the generated reader.html in place, breaking the 'never edit reader.html' rule, and now convert 0 passages.
site.evidence: In the copy, with CACHE_DIR sent to scratch and GitHub raw reachable: 'WARNING: /tmp/meditations_chapters.json not found ... Casaubon text will be empty' then 'Done! 486 Greek passages, 522 Long passages (484 aligned), 0 Casaubon passages'. JSON diff: Casaubon passages went from 412 to 0 and 17 'greek' fields differ; git diff shows 3,390 deleted lines across aurelius-meditations.json and meditations-complete.md. align_casaubon_long.py prints 'Input not found: .../data/texts/meditations-complete.json / Run collect_texts.py first.' assemble-annotations.py and node assemble-annotations.js both print 'Total: 0 passages converted' and 'Written to .../reader.html'.
site.repro: In a copy: python3 aurelius-meditations/data/collect_texts.py (needs raw.githubusercontent.com), then git diff --stat aurelius-meditations/aurelius-meditations.json. Then python3 aurelius-meditations/data/align_casaubon_long.py.
site.fix: Commit the Casaubon source (for example data/texts/casaubon.json), read it from the repo, and fail hard rather than warn when it is missing. Pin the Perseus and Standard Ebooks URLs to a commit SHA. Point align_casaubon_long.py at aurelius-meditations.json. Delete assemble-annotations.py/.js, or mark them historical in CLAUDE.md.
verifier_corrections: The Casaubon loss affects only aurelius-meditations.json and data/texts/meditations-complete.md; no reader output loses Casaubon, because reader-casaubon.html is standalone and the builders ignore the casaubon field. The Greek change is typographic, a combining comma above replaced by a modifier apostrophe in elisions; the problem is unpinned sources, not corrupted text. assemble-annotations.py/.js currently rewrite reader.html byte-identically (a no-op), so it is docs drift, not a live breach of the never-edit rule. The line references are correct: 413-417 is the warning, 234 is load_greek_cached reading /tmp/greek_meditations.json, and 32-39 are the master URLs.

Scope: the Casaubon loss affects only aurelius-meditations.json and data/texts/meditations-complete.md, not any reader. reader-casaubon.html is hand-maintained and still holds all 412 passages, so the source text is in the repo but unextracted. The Greek drift is an upstream Unicode correction, not damage. assemble-annotations.py/.js are effectively no-ops that are documented as live, which is docs drift, not an active rule violation. Add the root cause of the align breakage: commit 47e9a86 renamed the JSON without updating align_casaubon_long.py:24. Severity should be low.

site.title: Vedas: rerunning merge_bengali.py rewrites Bengali source labels and drops the 'llm' marking; the LLM step is not in the repo
site.detail: CLAUDE.md documents the merge priority as 'curated > ebanglalibrary > rkm > archive_ocr > llm'. merge_bengali.py actually uses curated > existing > ebanglalibrary > rkm > archive_ocr, and has no llm source at all. 'existing' is read back from seeds/rigveda-complete.json, which build_rigveda.py generates from this script's own previous output, so the pipeline is circular and not idempotent. The committed merged file records 9,906 ebanglalibrary, 144 llm, 49 curated and 44 archive_ocr sources. A rerun keeps the meaning_bn text but relabels 10,094 mantras as 'existing' and wipes the only record of which 144 Bengali meanings are LLM-generated. Nothing reads or writes llm_bengali_all.json, missing_bengali.json or missing_batch_1..3.json. The run also prints a false note, "'ebanglalibrary' contributed 0 mantras (file may not exist yet)", although the file exists. Related: rigveda.html's mandala data carries no source field, so readers are never told those 144 meanings are machine-generated, unlike the Rubáiyát, which labels its AI renderings.
site.evidence: Offline run in the copy: 'Source contribution: curated: 49 ... existing: 10094'. Field diff against HEAD: meaning_bn 0 changes, meaning_bn_source 10,094 changes, meaning_bn_alt 9,950 changes, merge_date changed (non-deterministic output). Counter over the committed file: {'ebanglalibrary': 9906, 'llm': 144, 'curated': 49, 'archive_ocr': 44}. `grep -rn llm_bengali` over *.py/*.md finds no references.
site.repro: In a copy: cd vedas/scripts && python3 merge_bengali.py; then compare meaning_bn_source counts in output/rigveda_bengali_merged.json with git HEAD.
site.fix: Drop the 'existing' tier, or read it from the committed merged file so labels are kept. Add the llm source (llm_bengali_all.json) at lowest priority. Fix the 0-contribution note. Make CLAUDE.md match the code. Carry a per-mantra source flag into the mandala data so rigveda.html can mark machine-generated Bengali.
verifier_corrections: The 'readers are never told' part is overstated. vedas/index.html:889-893 does disclose 'machine-generated fill-in for the remaining 1.4%' in aggregate. What is missing is per-mantra marking in rigveda.html and its mandala data, and any disclosure inside rigveda.html itself.

That note does exist in CLAUDE.md itself, at :109 'Extraction gotcha (Greek XML parsing)'. So the reference is a wrong filename pointer, not missing documentation. site.title: Vedas: the curated hymn data is kept in three hand-maintained copies, though the docs say it is not duplicated
site.detail: CLAUDE.md and payload.py say mobile, theater and pdf-reader parse VEDAS_DATA from reader.html, 'hand-written and canonical, so the data is not duplicated'. In fact fullbleed.html embeds a second full copy (`const vedas = {...}`, commented 'same as reader.html'), and seeds/hymns.json, samaveda.json, yajurveda.json and atharvaveda.json are a third copy. build_rigveda.py reads the curated Bengali overlay from seeds/hymns.json, not from reader.html. The copies agree today, but a maintainer who edits the 'canonical' reader.html as told updates 4 pages and leaves fullbleed.html and rigveda.html (after its next rebuild) on the old text.
site.evidence: Python compare: the fullbleed.html vedas object == reader.html VEDAS_DATA (True), and all 95 mantras x 5 fields (sa_devanagari, sa_bengali, transliteration, meaning_en, meaning_bn) are identical to seeds/*.json (0 diffs).
site.repro: grep -n 'const vedas = ' vedas/fullbleed.html; grep -n 'hymns.json' vedas/build_rigveda.py
site.fix: Pick one source, e.g. seeds/*.json. Generate VEDAS_DATA into reader.html and fullbleed.html from it (payload.py already has the flattening), or at least document all three copies and add a consistency check to the build scripts.
verifier_corrections: The fullbleed copy is partly acknowledged. payload.py:3-4 itself says '`reader.html` and `fullbleed.html` embed VEDAS_DATA'. vedas/CLAUDE.md:27 says fullbleed has the 'Same 4-Veda content as reader.html'. The root .project/todo.md:59 says 'Add more curated suktas to reader.html/fullbleed.html'. What nobody documents is the need to keep them in sync, plus the seeds copy. The build-side risk is also narrower than stated. build_rigveda.py and merge_bengali.py take only meaning_bn, and only from hymns.json (the 49 Rigveda mantras). rigveda.html would therefore diverge only on those Bengali meanings. samaveda.json, yajurveda.json and atharvaveda.json are read by no script at all, so they are unused duplicate data rather than a build input.

site.title: build_rigveda.py's built-in fallback template produces a broken page
site.detail: If data/rigveda-template.html is missing or renamed, main() falls back to the ~440-line inline HTML_TEMPLATE, an older UI. That template contains `const RV=__DATA_JSON__;`, but main() only replaces `__META_JSON__`, and build_compact_json(), which would fill __DATA_JSON__, is never called. The fallback therefore writes a rigveda.html that throws a ReferenceError, and the build reports success ('Using inline template (external not found)'). The fetch stage needs rigveda-online.github.io (unreachable in this sandbox). The offline stage reproduced every committed output exactly.
site.evidence: The inline template (lines 375-812) contains one placeholder, __DATA_JSON__ (line 570); main() at line 844 does html_template.replace('__META_JSON__', meta_json). Rebuilding the offline stage from the committed data/mandala-*.json left rigveda.html, all 20 mandala files, seeds/rigveda-complete.json and rigveda-samhita.md unchanged per git status.
site.repro: Read build_rigveda.py lines 836-846 alongside line 570; or rename data/rigveda-template.html in a copy and run the offline stage.
site.fix: Delete HTML_TEMPLATE and build_compact_json, and exit with an error when data/rigveda-template.html is missing.
verifier_corrections: The line references are accurate (inline template 375-812, placeholder at 570, main at 836-846, build_compact_json at 282-284). One small addition: the build exits 0 and prints 'Done! Open ... in a browser', so nothing tells the maintainer the output is broken.

site.title: #p-N means a printed page in some fullbleed readers and a spread number in Vedas, whose counter disagrees with its own page numbers
site.detail: The Alice, Prophet and Meditations fullbleeds treat N as a printed page number: #p-40 becomes #p-41, the right-hand page of the 40|41 spread. Vedas treats N as the spread index: #p-30 opens printed pages 59–60 while the footer counter reads '30 / 95'. Khayyam uses the quatrain number, which its docs state. AGENT_README:137 says 'content page/spread number', which allows both meanings. A reader who shares or types the page number printed on a Vedas page lands on a spread about twice as far in.
site.evidence: fbspread.js: vedas/fullbleed.html#p-30 → left page 59, right page 60, counter 30; alice-in-wonderland/fullbleed.html#p-40 → pages 40|41 with the hash normalised to #p-41.
site.repro: Open vedas/fullbleed.html#p-30: the pages shown are numbered 59 and 60.
site.fix: Choose one meaning (the printed page, since that is what readers see) and state it in AGENT_README. Then either make Vedas write and parse the printed page number, or have it show spread numbers instead of page numbers.
verifier_corrections:
The Vedas inconsistency is broader than the finding says:
- At phone width (<768px), vedas/fullbleed.html:644 prints the spread index (pageIdx+1) as the page number. The same passage is page 59 on desktop and page 30 on a phone.
- The Vedas TOC page column (line 601, suktaStartPages+1) also uses spread indices. For example, a TOC entry labelled 46 sits near printed pages 93|94.

In short, Vedas mixes the two meanings inside a single page, not just against the other books.

gap.title: Casaubon reader: 156 of 412 passages (Books 6–12) show the modern English and notes of a different passage
gap.detail:
This is a separate problem from the reported Leopold Books 4–12 misalignment in aurelius-meditations.json. Here the Casaubon text is correct, but the 'Modern English' and 'Notes' panels attached to it belong to a same-numbered passage from an earlier book (Book N−1 to N−3). Affected passages per book: 6: 5, 7: 2, 8: 30, 9: 32, 10: 31, 11: 30, 12: 26, for 156 in total (38% of the reader). Examples: XI.III, the famous 'not from obstinacy, as Christians are wont' passage, shows IX.III's paraphrase about teething, beards and 'Hurry, O Death'. IX.I 'He that is unjust, is also impious' shows VI.I's 'The matter that makes up the universe is pliable'. VIII.XXIV, the Lucilla/Verus passage, shows an Antisthenes paraphrase, and its own Lucilla annotation appears on IX.XXIV. The source files are correct: data/annotations/book-09.json 'I' does paraphrase 'He that is unjust…'. The fault is in injection. assemble-annotations.py builds `

{num}.…` and runs `pattern.search(html)` over the entire document, not the book's `

`. When Book N's numeral was already converted, the first plain match is in a later book.
gap.evidence: Parsed all 412 .med-passage blocks and compared each rendered Modern English with data/annotations/book-NN.json by (book, num), plus a reverse lookup of which JSON entry the rendered text actually is: 156 rendered annotations are verbatim another (book, num), e.g. (11,'III')←(9,'III'), (9,'I')←(6,'I'), (12,'I')←(9,'I'). gap.title: Forced colours (Windows High Contrast): theme swatches, every 'selected' state and all progress fills disappear
gap.detail: No page or data/*-template.html has an @media (forced-colors) rule or any forced-color-adjust. In forced colours the browser replaces every background with Canvas and drops box-shadow, and the site uses exactly those two for state. (a) Theme swatches: most are `border:none` with a background colour (e.g. alice reader .theme-dot:393, the canonical khayyam index:148), so on 36 of 51 pages the five dots render as nothing: an empty gap with invisible tab stops. On 6 pages (Meditations index, the Meditations, Khayyam and Vedas mobile sheets, Prophet pdf-reader, Khayyam reader) they become five identical empty rings. The active theme is marked only by box-shadow (41 pages, e.g. :412), so it is never shown. On the mobile sheets the only ring left is the focus outline on the first dot (Sepia) while Light purple is active. (b) Current state becomes invisible, and this is the real harm: which edition you are reading (Homer reader/mobile ed-switch, Khayyam reader, fullbleed and theater: colour or background only; Homer fullbleed and pdf keep only opacity 1 vs 0.8), the Text size/Font/Page width choice in all 8 reader.html plus rigveda (.opt.active background), which Vedas scripts are on (.toggle-btn.active), which sūkta is current in the rigveda strip (.s-pill.active background; mandala tab only 600 vs 500 weight). (c) Progress: the reader.html reading-progress fill, rigveda #progress-fill and theater progress fills are background-only and vanish; only the chapter tick borders remain. (d) Boundaries: the pdf-reader page card (background + shadow) merges with the viewer; the fullbleed spine and gutter vanish; mobile bottom sheets lose their scrim, so only a hairline separates a sheet from the page. Focus rings (outline) and the fullbleed scrubbers (opacity) do survive.

The 'Medium' vs 'Small' text-size buttons differ only in background rgb(0,0,0) vs transparent. Odyssey mobile chips are all border rgb(255,255,255) 1px, weight 400 (snap eval). prog.js: reader progress track variance 0.42 → 0.008; Prophet theater fill (320px wide) is invisible. Open homer-odyssey/reader.html and click Aa: nothing shows Pope as the current edition or Medium/Serif as the current settings; the theme dots next to the sun icon are invisible. The invisible dots amount to 5 unseen tab stops, and the focus outline survives on them. Add that the .opt, .toggle-btn and .s-pill buttons in alice/vedas/odyssey readers and rigveda have no aria-pressed or aria-current (0 occurrences). gap.title: Book-spread formats block text selection (user-select:none plus click zones over the text); double-clicking a word flips one or two pages
gap.detail:
Two mechanisms stop readers from selecting text.

First, user-select:none is set on #book and .page-half in alice, prophet and vedas fullbleed, and on #book in khayyam fullbleed.

Second, transparent click zones sit on top of the text:
- #click-left/#click-right (50% each, z-index 8) in alice, prophet and khayyam fullbleed, and in meditations fullbleed at its phone breakpoint
- #zone-left/#zone-right (z-index 40) in alice index and meditations index
- #hit-left/#hit-right (18%, 26% when narrow) in Homer fullbleed and #hit-left-pdf/#hit-right-pdf (20%) in Homer pdf-reader
- the illustrated hit zones on phones.

Effects:
- Readers can't select or copy a quote.
- On phones, a long-press to select, look up or translate a word lands on user-select:none or on an empty div.
- A double-click on a word, the standard way to select one, fires two flip clicks. Instead of selecting, it jumps the reader 1-2 pages.
- In vedas fullbleed there is no overlay, but #book's click handler turns the page on the mouseup that ends a drag-select.

Theater formats (all but Alice) also advance on drag or double-click. That is the click handler already reported for tap/click, but the fix should treat selection too.

Relation to earlier findings: these are the same overlays already reported as blocking links, the TOC and notes scrolling (Meditations index, Prophet/Khayyam/Vedas fullbleed). Text selection is a separate symptom, and user-select:none is a separate cause.

Where selection works (all reader.html, scroll, single, web-reader, mobile, pdf-reader), the copied text is clean. The only oddity is a stray '…' per quatrain from Khayyam's details button.

gap.title: Meditations (Leopold) notes and tooltips state wrong identities and relationships as fact: 1.4, 1.14, 8.25, 8.5/10.27, 11.3
gap.detail:
These records are aligned with their own Greek, so the errors are in the editorial content itself. They appear in the reader.html notes and tooltips and in the mobile.html and pdf-reader.html apparatus.
(1) 1.4: the note says 'Marcus's great-grandfather is Marcus Annius Verus I' (the tooltip is the same). The standard identification is his maternal great-grandfather L. Catilius Severus, after whom Marcus was first named (Historia Augusta, Marcus 1.9). George Long's own note on this line, in the edition this site uses, reads 'Perhaps his mother's grandfather, Catilius Severus'. Annius Verus I is also chronologically implausible: the reader's own 1.1 tip puts the grandfather's birth in the 60s CE, which puts the great-grandfather a century before Marcus's schooling. I judge the note wrong, not merely contested.
(2) 1.14: the note says 'Claudius Severus Arabianus was … Marcus's brother by adoption (both were adopted by Antoninus Pius)', and the tooltip says 'Marcus Aurelius's adoptive brother'. Antoninus adopted only Marcus and L. Verus. Long's notes say 'Antoninus had no brother' and that the word 'brother' may not be genuine (note 12), and 'The emperor had no brother, except L. Verus, his brother by adoption' (note 20).
(3) 8.25: the note says 'Lucilla was the mother of Lucius Verus', and the tip says 'Lucilla, mother of Lucius Verus' and links to Annia_Galeria_Faustina. Lucius Verus's mother was Avidia Plautia. The usual reading of 'Lucilla [saw] Verus [die], then Lucilla' is Marcus's mother Domitia Lucilla and his father Annius Verus, consistent with this dataset's own 1.2/1.3 tips and 1.17. The older reading (Gutenberg #2680 glossary) is Marcus's daughter Lucilla, wife of L. Verus. Under neither reading is she his mother.
(4) 8.5: the note and tip say Hadrian was 'his adoptive grandfather's predecessor', which would be Trajan; Hadrian himself was Marcus's adoptive grandfather. The 10.27 tip calls Hadrian 'Marcus Aurelius's adoptive great-uncle and predecessor', which contradicts 8.5; Hadrian was Antoninus's predecessor, not Marcus's.
(5) 11.3: the note says 'one of only two references to Christians in the Meditations'. It is the only one: Long's note 104 says 'This is the only passage in which the Emperor speaks of the Christians', and grep finds Χριστιαν/Christian only in 11.3.
gap.evidence: Browser DOM of reader.html (1440x900): 1.4 note 'Marcus's great-grandfather is Marcus Annius Verus I…'; 1.14 note '…brother by adoption (both were adopted by Antoninus Pius)'; 8.5 '…Hadrian (his adoptive grandfather's predecessor)'; 8.25 'Lucilla was the mother of Lucius Verus'; 11.3 'one of only two references to Christians'. Screenshot of the 1.14 panel: scratchpad/work/gap-annotations/leopold-1.14-detail.png. mobile.html #m-8.25 with notes on lists 'Lucilla, mother of Lucius Verus…' and 'Verus: Lucius Verus (130-169 CE)'. Long endnotes fetched from raw.githubusercontent.com/standardebooks/marcus-aurelius_meditations_george-long/master/src/epub/text/endnotes.xhtml (notes 4, 12, 20, 104). A grep of all Greek, Long and Casaubon text finds only 11.3 mentioning Christians.
gap.repro: Open /aurelius-meditations/reader.html#ch-1, open the details on 1.4 and 1.14, and hover 'Severus'. Open reader.html#ch-8 on 8.5 and 8.25, and #ch-11 on 11.3; or open mobile.html#m-8.25 and tap the 'i' button.
gap.fix: 1.4: 'Probably L. Catilius Severus, his maternal great-grandfather (HA Marcus 1.9)'. 1.14: 'Claudius Severus, a Peripatetic whose son married Marcus's daughter; "brother" is loose or corrupt (Antoninus adopted only Marcus and L. Verus)'. 8.25: Lucilla = Domitia Lucilla, Verus = M. Annius Verus (Marcus's parents), noting the older daughter/L. Verus reading. 8.5/10.27: 'Hadrian, Marcus's adoptive grandfather'. 11.3: 'the only reference to Christians'. Edit data/annotations/leopold-*.json, rerun collect_texts.py (see the build caveats), then assemble-reader.py and build_mobile/theater/pdf.py.
verifier_corrections: Wider scope than stated. The same content is also in theater.html (every phrase present). The Casaubon-era file data/annotations/book-08.json:193 carries the same 'Lucilla was the mother of Lucius Verus' error, and it renders in reader-casaubon.html (currently on IX.XXIV because of finding 0). Also fix the 1.14 Severus tip URL, which points at the son (consul 167). Soften the 10.27 sub-point: 'great-uncle' by marriage is defensible, so only 'adoptive' is wrong there. 1.4 is better described as a contested/likely-wrong identification than a false genealogical statement.

Scope: the errors also appear in theater.html, which the finding does not list. The 8.25 note also appears in reader-casaubon.html, via book-08.json XXIV, which finding 0 displaces onto IX.XXIV. The 'Lucilla, mother of Lucius Verus' tooltip and the 10.27 'adoptive great-uncle' tooltip are not in reader.html; they appear only in mobile, pdf-reader and theater. Line 8193 is a tip, not a note. For 10.27, 'great-uncle' has some genealogical basis: Hadrian may have been Marcus's great-uncle by marriage if Rupilia Faustina was Vibia Sabina's half-sister, and 'predecessor' can be read loosely. The solid defects there are 'adoptive' and the inconsistency with 8.5. That sub-item is weaker than stated. The 1.14 tooltip also links to Gnaeus_Claudius_Severus_(consul_167), the son, while naming the father, Arabianus.

gap.title: Meditations landing page: Greek epigraphs that are not in the Meditations, an invented 'At Vindobona' book title, and a wrong source credit
gap.detail:
(1) The About spread prints, in Greek and in quotation marks, “Τὰ τῶν ὅλων μεταβολή, οὐδὲν κακόν.” / “The change of all things — nothing evil in it.” The colophon prints “Δὸς ἐνεργεῖν εἰς τὸ κοινόν.” / “Give yourself to the work of the common good.” Neither sentence occurs anywhere in the Leopold text. The first loosely paraphrases 2.17 and 4.42 ('Οὐδέν ἐστι κακὸν τοῖς ἐν μεταβολῇ γινομένοις'); the phrase εἰς τὸ κοινόν does not occur in the Meditations at all. Readers are shown invented Greek as the emperor's words.
(2) 'The Twelve Books' gives Book II as 'On the Carnuntum Frontier' and Book X as 'At Vindobona'. The only place notes in the manuscripts are 'Among the Quadi at the Granua' (end of Book I) and 'At Carnuntum' (end of Book II); see Long's notes 23 and 30. No book is headed Vindobona. The readers themselves (payload.py, assemble-reader.py) title Book II 'Written Among the Quadi', so the landing page contradicts its own formats.
(3) Data sources gives 'Source: Gutenberg #2680' for the English, and the colophon says 'English text from Project Gutenberg'. Gutenberg #2680 is the Casaubon translation. Long's text came from Standard Ebooks (aurelius-meditations.json sources.long), which is never credited. CLAUDE.md:119 also lists Long as 'Gutenberg #2680'. The old audit's LOW item (index.html credits only Casaubon) was therefore only partly addressed.
gap.evidence: Decoded the \u escapes in index.html and searched the accent-stripped Greek of all 486 passages: no match for either epigraph and no occurrence of 'εις το κοινον'. The nearest are 2.17 '…οὐδὲν δὲ κακὸν κατὰ φύσιν' and 4.42 'Οὐδέν ἐστι κακὸν τοῖς ἐν μεταβολῇ γινομένοις'. The books array (index.html:664-677) and BOOK_SUBTITLES in payload.py:22-26 were read directly. aurelius-meditations.json sources.long = Standard Ebooks; the GITenberg 2680.txt fetched from raw.githubusercontent.com is Casaubon.
gap.repro: Open /aurelius-meditations/index.html and turn to the About spread (the Greek quote under the themes), then to the last spread (the Twelve Books list and the colophon epigraph).
gap.fix: Replace both epigraphs with real passages, e.g. 4.42 'Οὐδέν ἐστι κακὸν τοῖς ἐν μεταβολῇ γινομένοις' and 6.7, or drop the Greek. Remove 'At Vindobona' and give Book II the same subtitle the readers use. Credit 'George Long (1862) via Standard Ebooks (CC0); Meric Casaubon (1634) via Gutenberg #2680', and fix CLAUDE.md:119.
verifier_corrections: Status for sub-point (3) is closer to 'regression' (incomplete fix): the old audit's LOW item at index.html:596-608 was partly addressed by adding the Long row, but the Source row and colophon were never corrected. For (2), note that every subtitle on this list is editorial; the actionable defects are the unsupported 'At Vindobona' place claim and the Book II title that contradicts the readers. The finding's placement note ('end of Book I/II') is one of two manuscript conventions; the site's own readers use the start-of-book heading convention.

Point (2) is partly misframed. In this dataset's Leopold text, the Quadi subscription is at 1.17 (end of Book I) and Carnuntum at 2.17 (end of Book II). The landing page's 'On the Carnuntum Frontier' for Book II is therefore consistent with the displayed text. The readers' 'Written Among the Quadi' (II) and 'In Carnuntum' (III) follow the heading-at-start-of-next-book convention and are out of step with the text they show. The defect is the inconsistency (the landing page gives both II and III a Carnuntum title) plus the baseless 'At Vindobona'. Copying the readers' Book II subtitle is not clearly the right fix. CLAUDE.md:119 actually reads 'Public domain (Gutenberg #2680) / CC0 (Standard Ebooks)', so Standard Ebooks is named there; only the #2680 attribution for Long is wrong. .project/changelog.md:113 has the same wrong 'George Long … Project Gutenberg #2680'. The severity rests mainly on the invented Greek epigraphs; the credit and title items alone would be low.

gap.title: Curated Vedas: 'Rigveda 3.62.18' is really RV 5.82.5, 3.62.11 is conflated with 1.2.7, and the Samaveda opener's verse 2 is not RV 6.16
gap.detail:
These are not the typo-level 'small errors in the curated text' already reported: whole verses are misattributed in the site's signature hymn.
- The Gayatri sūkta (3.62) shows verse '62.18' as 'viśvāni deva savitar duritāni parā suva | yad bhadraṃ tan na ā suva'. That is RV 5.82.5, the Śyāvāśva hymn to Savitṛ. The real 3.62.18 is 'gṛṇānā jamadagninā yonāv ṛtasya sīdatam | pātaṃ somam ṛtāvṛdhā', addressed to Mitra–Varuṇa and naming Jamadagni.
- The curated 3.62.11 splices 3.62.11's first half onto 'dhiyaṃ ghṛtācīṃ sādhantā', the close of RV 1.2.7. The real second half is 'bhagasya rātim īmahe', and the English 'perfecting the thought rich as ghee' translates the wrong half.
- The header gives the whole sūkta as devatā Savitṛ and ṛṣi Viśvāmitra. In fact 3.62 is addressed in triads to Indra–Varuṇa, Bṛhaspati, Pūṣan, Savitṛ, Soma and Mitra–Varuṇa; the repo's own complete Rigveda titles it 'Indra And Others', and verses 16–18 are Jamadagni's.
- Samaveda: the note says 'These verses correspond to Rigveda 6.16.10–12', but mantra 2 ('agne vivasvad uṣaso vibhāvaso divas pṛthivyor abhi sandhim eṣām | mā no martā abhi duścarmāṇo…') matches no verse in the repo's complete Rigveda. It begins like RV 1.44.1, then diverges, and its long pādas are not the Gāyatrī stated in the header. RV 6.16.12 is missing. The note also calls 'agna ā yāhi' 'the opening hymn of the Samaveda Uttararchika'. That verse is SV 1, the opening of the Pūrvārcika; the Uttarārcika opens with the Soma triad 'upāsmai gāyatā naraḥ' (RV 9.11.1).
gap.evidence: difflib comparison (viramas normalised) of all 42 curated Rigveda verses with seeds/rigveda-complete.json. Only 3.62.11 (0.71) and 3.62.18 (0.22) differ. gap.title: 100vh-sized book boxes run under the iOS Safari toolbar and Android URL bar: Classic Book and fullbleed pages lose their bottom lines and page numbers
gap.detail: On iOS Safari and Android Chrome, 100vh is the LARGE viewport, meaning the size with the browser bars retracted. gap.title: Reload, or Back/Forward without bfcache, sends the Alice, Meditations and Khayyam readers back to the start of the chapter, overriding the browser's exact scroll restore
gap.detail:
On a reload, or a history traversal served without bfcache, Chrome restores the exact scrollY (history.scrollRestoration is 'auto'). These readers then run their hash restore unconditionally, even though the hash only names a chapter or group:
- alice restoreHash() after fonts.ready
- meditations restoreHashPosition() plus reapplyHashPosition() on load and on fonts.ready
- khayyam restoreHash()

It scrolls to the top of the #ch-N chapter or #chg- group, discarding the precise position. The loss is up to a whole chapter: an Alice chapter averages 12.6 phone screens (7.6 desktop), a Meditations Book 23.6 phone screens (max 29.8) and a Khayyam group about 3.

Why it matters: on phones, background tabs are regularly discarded and reloaded on return, and bfcache is not always used (it is evicted after a timeout or under memory pressure, and other browsers differ). Readers who switch apps come back several screens earlier.

The pages with no hash restore (alice web-reader.html, scroll.html) and vedas reader.html come back exactly. This shows the browser would keep the place if the script did not override it.

With bfcache the page is not reloaded, and nothing blocks bfcache (no unload/beforeunload handlers). That path could not be run here because Playwright's headless Chromium forces --disable-back-forward-cache.

prophet reader.html shows the same loss, but it is masked by the already-reported bug where its hash is stuck at #ch-1.
gap.evidence:
reload.js at 1440x900, scrollY after reload at 0 / 100 / 300 / 800 / 2500 ms:
- alice #ch-5: 27339 -> 27336 -> 26761 -> 24846 -> 24846 (started at 27346; the browser restored it, then the script moved to the chapter top)
- meditations #ch-4: 29755 -> ... -> 25766 (started at 29766)
- casaubon: 33211 -> 29218
- khayyam #chg-fifth-4: 7758 -> 6566
- web-reader (no restore script): 30000 throughout (control).

reloadm.js at 390x844: alice lost 3000px (41626 -> 38626, the chapter top); meditations lost 3000px (42615 -> 39615).

roundtrip.js (page -> index.html -> Back, reloaded): the same losses (alice 2500px, meditations 4000px, casaubon 4000px, khayyam 1200px). Vedas reader, web-reader and scroll.html came back exact.

chh.js gives the chapter lengths in screens.
gap.repro:
1. Open alice-in-wonderland/reader.html#ch-5 and scroll about 3 screens into the chapter.
2. Press F5, or open another site in the same tab and press Back (with DevTools 'Disable cache' / bfcache off, or after the tab was discarded).
3. The page briefly appears at the right spot, then scrolls back to the 'Advice from a Caterpillar' heading.
gap.fix: Only restore from the hash on a fresh navigation. Skip it when performance.getEntriesByType('navigation')[0].type is 'reload' or 'back_forward' and scrollY is already inside the hashed chapter. Or set history.scrollRestoration = 'manual' and store the exact offset in history.state (replaceState({y}, '', '#ch-N')), restoring state.y when present. Also make meditations' reapplyHashPosition respect a browser-restored scroll, not just user input.
verifier_corrections: All line numbers check out. Add AGENT_README.md:144-145 ('restore it in script rather than relying on the browser's native fragment scroll') to the scope: the readers follow that convention literally, so the convention text should gain a 'skip on reload/back_forward when already inside the hashed chapter' clause too. Otherwise future readers will copy the same behaviour.
The bfcache-enabled Back path was not testable (Playwright headless disables bfcache). The Back/Forward half of the claim applies only when bfcache is not used, as the finding already says.

gap.title: Alice fullbleed, Meditations fullbleed and Alice mobile do nothing until every font file settles: cover or 'Loading…' is inert, saved theme and #p-N not applied (3 new instances of the reported Prophet fullbleed root cause)
gap.detail: These three pages share the root cause of the reported gibran-prophet/fullbleed.html:1556 finding and are listed here as new instances. Each calls its whole init only after `document.fonts.ready`, with no timer fallback: alice fullbleed `document.fonts.ready.then(init)`, meditations fullbleed the same on one line, alice mobile `document.fonts.ready.then(go)`. In the two fullbleeds, every listener (click zones, keydown, prev/next, theme button, scrubber) and the saved-theme restore sit inside init() (alice 1373-1541, meditations 993-1117). When the CSS arrives but the font files hang, the reader sees a readable cover that says 'Click anywhere to open'. Clicking, tapping, arrow keys, → and the theme button all do nothing. The saved theme is not applied, and a #p-N link is not honoured until the font requests end. Alice mobile shows a 30%-opacity 'Loading…' with a live-looking I–XII chapter bar, and those buttons are dead because chStarts is still {}. fonts.ready only resolves when every pending face has loaded or failed. After init, more faces are requested (italic, 500/600 weights), so a second wait follows, but init does not re-run. Khayyam reader shows the right pattern: it races fonts.ready against a 400 ms timer (khayyam-rubaiyat/reader.html:1272-1277).
gap.evidence: Font files held, CSS served; measured time until the first spread or page renders (page-num set, or the 'Loading…' gone). With a 0 s hang: 0.4–1.0 s. With a 10 s hang: alice fullbleed 10.5/10.4 s (390/1440), meditations fullbleed 10.6/10.6 s, alice mobile 10.2/10.2 s. With a 60 s hang: alice fullbleed 60.3/60.4 s, meditations fullbleed 60.8/60.6 s, alice mobile 60.2/60.1 s. FCP in those same runs was 44–292 ms, so the page looks loaded but is inert for the whole hang. For reference, the already-reported prophet fullbleed measured 10.2–10.3 s and 60.3 s. With both hosts hanging 30 s: alice fullbleed usable at 60.3 s, meditations fullbleed at 60.5 s, alice mobile text at 60.4–60.6 s. Interaction log with a 30 s hang, saved theme dark-blue and hash #p-20: alice fullbleed at 390 and 1440 and meditations fullbleed at 390 and 1440 all showed the same thing after cover click, ArrowRight, #btn-next and #theme-btn at t=4–6.7 s. page-num stayed '', the hash stayed #p-20 and the theme stayed default (light-purple on alice, sepia on meditations). At 33.5 s the page switched to dark-blue on p-20/21. Alice mobile ignored a tap and ArrowRight while showing 'Loading…'. Screenshots: scratchpad/work/gap-fonts/shots/alice-fb.m.fontHang.t4.png, med-fb.d.fontHang.t4.png, alice-mob.m.fontHang.t4.png. Logs: g-alice-fb-d.txt, g-med-fb-m.txt, g-med-fb-d.txt, g-alice-mob-m.txt, stuck.txt, stuck-both.txt.
gap.repro: Playwright: serve fonts.googleapis.com normally (or with any css2 response) and hold every fonts.gstatic.com request for 30 s. In localStorage set alice-fullbleed-prefs={"theme":"dark-blue"}. Open /alice-in-wonderland/fullbleed.html#p-20 at 390x844 and tap the cover, press ArrowRight, tap → and tap the theme icon. Nothing happens and the theme is light-purple, for 30 s. Same with /aurelius-meditations/fullbleed.html#p-20 (key meditations-fullbleed-theme=dark-blue) and /alice-in-wonderland/mobile.html, which stays on 'Loading…'.
gap.fix: Wire up the listeners and apply the saved theme synchronously. Start after a bounded wait: `Promise.race([document.fonts.ready, new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 1500))]).then(init)`. Then repaginate once more, keeping the reader's position, when the fonts really land: `document.fonts.ready.then(() => { if (booted) repaginateKeepingPosition(); })` or a document.fonts 'loadingdone' listener, which is the approach homer-odyssey/illustrated.html:991-997 already uses. For alice mobile, fix gen_mobile.py:542-549 and regenerate. Fix the prophet fullbleed (already reported) the same way.
verifier_corrections: Alice mobile does apply the saved theme immediately (mobile.html:511-512), and its theme button works during the wait. It has no #p-N support, so only the pagination, navigation and chapter bar are inert there. The title's 'saved theme and #p-N not applied' applies only to the two fullbleeds. This shares its root cause with the already-reported gibran-prophet/fullbleed.html:1556 finding and should be merged into it as one finding with four locations, not reported separately.

Alice mobile does apply the saved theme at once (applyTheme runs before the wait, mobile.html:512-513). It also has no #p-N handling, so for that page the only effect is that content and navigation are dead. In the fix text, homer-odyssey/illustrated.html:991-997 does not use a document.fonts 'loadingdone' listener. It renders first, then calls Promise.all([fonts.load(...), fonts.load(...), fonts.ready]).then(repaginateKeepingPosition). That render-then-repaginate pattern is the right model to cite.

gap.title: Every page stays blank and runs no script while fonts.googleapis.com hangs: the Google Fonts <link> blocks rendering and scripts on all 51 pages
gap.detail: Every live page loads its fonts with `<link href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?...&display=swap" rel="stylesheet">` in <head>. The line is 9 on 30 pages, 10 on 12 Homer pages, 7 on alice index/scroll/single/theater and meditations index, 11 on the alice and prophet mobile pages, and 12 on the homer mobile pages. A stylesheet link blocks rendering, and it also blocks scripts: the parser stops at the first inline <script> until the CSS arrives or fails. `display=swap` only helps once this CSS has arrived; it does nothing while the CSS request itself hangs. When the host fails fast (offline, DNS NXDOMAIN, the sandbox) nothing is lost. When the host hangs, readers get a white screen with no text, no theme and no JS. That happens with a blackholed Google in mainland China, a captive portal, a corporate firewall that drops packets, or lie-fi. The blank lasts until the TCP connection gives up. From general OS behaviour, not measured here, that is about 21 s on Windows, about 75 s on macOS and about 127 s on Linux/Android. Other external CSS/JS: none. There are no external <script src>, no @import and no external url() in CSS. The 46 preconnect links do not block. So this one tag is the whole problem, and it comes from 21 data/*-template.html files plus alice-in-wonderland/gen_mobile.py and vedas/build_rigveda.py. The previous audit saw the symptom and wrote it off: '~15s page load times in smoke data are the sandbox's Google-Fonts timeout, not a site defect' (.project/ui-ux-audit-2026-08-20.md:192). README.md:117-118 says 'a reader works offline'. That holds only when the font host fails fast.
gap.evidence: Playwright page.route held the fonts.googleapis.com request for 30 s and then aborted it. First-contentful-paint came at 30.03–30.45 s on all 51 pages at 390x844 and 30.04–30.41 s at 1440x900 (median 30.08 s / 30.09 s). Readable text appeared at 30.1–31.7 s. Baseline with both hosts failing fast: FCP 32–484 ms, text by 0.5–0.9 s. In every sample taken before 29 s, across all 102 runs, document.readyState was 'loading' and no paint entry existed: the parser was stuck at the first inline script. Examples: index.html has scripts=1 and gibran-prophet/reader.html has body innerText length 0 at t=5 s. A CDP Page.captureScreenshot at t=5 s timed out, meaning no frame was produced, for index.html, gibran-prophet/reader.html and homer-iliad/reader.html. With both hosts hanging (CSS held 30 s then served, font files held 30 s), FCP was again 30.0–30.5 s on every page. Raw data: scratchpad/work/gap-fonts/res-base.jsonl, res-cssHang.jsonl and res-bothHang.jsonl; summ.py prints them per page.
gap.repro: 1) In Chrome DevTools, block nothing but add a network rule that never answers fonts.googleapis.com; or use Playwright: ctx.route(/fonts\.googleapis\.com/, r => setTimeout(() => r.abort(), 30000)). 2) Open any page, e.g. http://localhost:8111/ or /gibran-prophet/reader.html at 390x844. 3) The screen stays blank for the full 30 s, and performance.getEntriesByName('first-contentful-paint') stays empty. It paints about 30.1 s after navigation.
gap.fix: Preferred: self-host the fonts. Put woff2 subsets (latin/latin-ext, plus greek for EB Garamond, arabic for Vazirmatn and Noto Naskh Arabic, bengali/devanagari for the Noto Serif and Tiro families) in /fonts/, declared with @font-face { font-display: swap } in a same-origin stylesheet or inline <style>. That removes the third-party failure mode and the privacy exposure, and makes the README's 'works offline' claim true. If the pages stay on Google, make the CSS non-blocking in every template and generator: `<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?...&display=swap" media="print" onload="this.media='all'"><noscript><link rel="stylesheet" href="..."></noscript>`. Either way, pages that paginate by measuring text must repaginate when fonts arrive, via document.fonts 'loadingdone' or a later fonts.ready. With async CSS, fonts.ready can resolve before any font request has started, which is the trap documented at homer-odyssey/data/illustrated-template.html:982-990. Write the pattern into AGENT_README.md 'Fonts' (lines 105-110) so new books do not reintroduce the blocking tag, and correct the method note in the old audit.
verifier_corrections: Template count is wrong. 24 data/*-template.html files carry the tag, not 21. The tag is not only template-sourced either: many live pages are hand-maintained single files that contain it directly (root index.html, most of the Alice and Prophet pages, Meditations index/reader/reader-casaubon/fullbleed, Vedas index/reader/fullbleed, Khayyam index and others). A fix has to touch those files as well as the 24 templates plus gen_mobile.py and build_rigveda.py. Severity should be medium, not high.

The blocking link is in 24 data templates, not 21: aurelius-meditations x3, homer-iliad x5, homer-odyssey x7, khayyam-rubaiyat x5 and vedas x4 (mobile, pdf, rigveda and theater templates). It is also in alice-in-wonderland/gen_mobile.py and vedas/build_rigveda.py. Several live pages have no template and would need direct edits: all of alice except mobile, all of prophet, meditations fullbleed/reader/reader-casaubon/index, and the root index. Severity is medium, not high: the effect is severe but depends on the network.

gap.title: Meditations (Leopold): contested or loose identifications stated as fact, and a swapped 10.31 paraphrase
gap.detail:
These are stated as fact but are contested or loose.
- 1.14 'Dion' is identified as Dio Chrysostom. The anti-tyrant list (Thrasea, Helvidius, Cato, Dion, Brutus) is usually read as Dion of Syracuse. Long's note 13 points to Plutarch's paired Lives of Dion and Brutus, and the site's own Casaubon reader and the Gutenberg glossary say Syracuse.
- 1.9: Sextus is called 'nephew of Plutarch' as fact. HA Marcus 3.1 has 'Plutarchi nepotem', and Long's note 8 says 'more probably a grandson'.
- 1.14: Brutus is called a 'Stoic'. Plutarch (Brutus 2) makes him a follower of the Old Academy (Antiochus).
- 1.12: Alexander the Platonist, 'Little is known about him beyond this reference'. He is generally identified as Alexander of Seleucia 'Peloplaton', Marcus's Greek secretary (Philostratus, Lives of the Sophists 2.5).
- 1.6: philosophic dress adopted 'as a teenager'. HA Marcus 2.6 says in his twelfth year.
- 11.25: the note and tip present Perdiccas II inviting Socrates. Other sources name Archelaus (Aristotle, Rhetoric 2.23; Long's note 111: 'Perhaps the emperor made a mistake').
- 10.31: the modern_english says 'When you see Xenophon, think of Crito or Severus', but its own Leopold Greek reads Σευῆρον ἰδὼν Κρίτωνα ἢ Ξενοφῶντα φαντάζου ('seeing Severus, think of Crito or Xenophon'). gap.title: Rubáiyát edition facts: fifth edition 'months after' FitzGerald's death, Heron-Allen dated 1898, 'anonymous debut', and the Foroughi-Ghani date and calendar
gap.detail:
(1) 'The canonical text, published months after FitzGerald's death' (index.html:456; the fifth edition's note in build_reader.py:436, shown on the fullbleed colophon). FitzGerald died on 14 June 1883, and the fifth edition appeared in 1889 in Letters and Literary Remains (ed. W. Aldis Wright): six years, not months. The site itself prints 'FitzGerald (1809–1883)' and 'Fifth (1889)'.
(2) 'Heron-Allen's 1898 scholarly Persian-source analysis' (index.html:397 and :457, CLAUDE.md, and the 'Heron-Allen analysis 1898 · scholarly' label in every FG5 detail panel). Edward FitzGerald's Rubâ'iyât … with their original Persian sources was published by Quaritch in 1899. Its preface, in the repo's own source #38511, calls his Ouseley facsimile '(London, 1898)' 'my recently published translation' and says 'forty years have elapsed' since 1859.
(3) 'FitzGerald's anonymous debut' (index.html:449, build_reader.py:423). The 1859 Rubáiyát was anonymous but was not his debut: Euphranor (1851), Polonius (1852), Six Dramas of Calderon (1853) and Salámán and Absál (1856) came first.
(4) 'Foroughi & Ghani, 1960' (index.html:395 and :508, seeds, CLAUDE.md). The Foroughi–Ghani edition was published in Tehran in 1321 SH (1942), the year Foroughi died; 1339 SH (1960) is a later printing. The reader's caption shows 'Persian — Foroughi & Ghani · 1339 · 178' (reader-template.html:1026) in the slot where the other editions show CE years (1859, 1889, 1883, 1903), so it reads as a 14th-century date. Other formats say 1960.
gap.evidence: Browser text: the index.html section notes (quoted above); mobile and pdf detail panels show 'HERON-ALLEN ANALYSIS 1898 · SCHOLARLY'; the reader's #edition-caption after clicking the Persian tab reads 'PERSIAN — FOROUGHI & GHANI · 1339 · 178 رباعیات · ANNOTATED'. Gutenberg #38511 (GITenberg mirror): lines 1848-1856 (preface), 2019-2022 ('O.— Ouseley MS … (London, 1898)') and 15724-15725 ('Letters and Literary Remains … London, 1889'). fetch_persian.py:4 itself says 'Foroughi-Ghani 1339/1960'.
gap.repro: Open /khayyam-rubaiyat/index.html and read the FG1/FG5 cards and the About panel. Open reader.html, click the فا tab and read the caption. Open fullbleed.html in the FG5 edition and turn to the colophon.
gap.fix: FG5: 'published posthumously in 1889, six years after FitzGerald's death'. Heron-Allen: 1899. FG1: 'published anonymously'. Persian: 'Foroughi & Ghani (1942; text from the 1960 / 1339 SH printing)', and label the year with SH or give the CE year in the reader caption. Update build_reader.py, the reader template and CLAUDE.md, then rebuild.
verifier_corrections: Scope: the 'months after' note is also in mobile.html, pdf-reader.html and theater.html, not only index.html and fullbleed. Drop or soften sub-point (3): 'debut' is ambiguous and may just mean the first edition. For (4), the actionable defect is the unlabeled 1339 in the reader caption and the inconsistent 1339/1960; citing the 1960 printing is acceptable if it is labeled as a printing of the 1942 edition. Severity low: metadata and blurb dates, not reading content.

Item (3), 'anonymous debut', is weak. In a card describing the first edition it reads naturally as the poem's anonymous debut, not FitzGerald's first book, so it is at most a wording nit. Item (4): '1960' is the printing the site actually used (fetch_persian.py:4 says 1339/1960). Citing it is misleading as an edition date rather than false. The concrete UI defect is the unlabelled '1339' in the CE-year slot of the reader caption (reader-template.html:1026), which also disagrees with the '1960' shown in the other formats. Additional locations: CLAUDE.md:22, 28, 47, 175, build_fullbleed.py:15, build_reader.py:17/168/472, reader-template.html:792 (tab title).

gap.title: Rubáiyát Persian notes: one wrong FitzGerald match and a misattributed quotation
gap.detail:
The Persian notes' FitzGerald cross-references are almost all right: the cited stanza contains the quoted words in every case but these two.
- #136: the note says 'the closer match is FG 1st XXXVII / 5th 37 ("Unborn TOMORROW and dead YESTERDAY")', and fg_5th is {num: 37}. FG5 XXXVII is the Potter stanza ('For I remember stopping by the way / To watch a Potter thumping his wet Clay'); the 'Unborn To-morrow and dead Yesterday' line in the fifth edition is LVII (the note on #18 already cites it correctly). The FG5 Potter quatrain is therefore paired with the wrong Persian source in the apparatus.
- #52: the note says "FitzGerald's 'Whose Throne of Saturn' and 'Throne of Kobad' (1st IX, 5th X)". Neither phrase is in FG1 IX or FG5 X: 'Throne of Saturn' is FG1/5 XXXI, and 'Throne of Kobad' is Whinfield's wording (as the #96 note says).
These notes are disclosed as machine-generated, but they are presented as matches.
gap.evidence: A script checked every FG stanza number cited in the 178 notes against seeds/fitzgerald.json (share of quoted words present in the cited stanza) and every FG1/FG5 pair for mutual similarity. Only #136 (0 of 4 words; FG1 37 and FG5 37 are unrelated stanzas) and #52 (0 of 3) failed.
