gap.fix: Set #136 fg_5th to {num: 57} and fix the note; correct the #52 note to cite XXXI and Whinfield 64.
verifier_corrections: Change the repro and impact: FG5 XXXVII shows the correct source (#107). The wrong pairing appears in the Persian edition at quatrain ۱۳۶, where the 'Other historical translations' panel lists FG 5th 37 (the Potter stanza), and in the #136 note (persian.json:4180). The proposed fg_5th {num:57} is also debatable. LVII only reuses the 'Unborn To-morrow' line in a different poem, so removing fg_5th or marking it weak is safer. #18 already maps to 57 as a strong match.

gap.title: Vedas metadata and counts: wrong metre for 10.191, and two contradictory Rigveda totals
gap.detail:
(1) 10.191 (Samjñāna): the chandas is given as 'Anushtubh and Gayatri'. Verse 3 ('samāno mantraḥ samitiḥ samānī…') is Triṣṭubh (11-syllable pādas) and the others are Anuṣṭubh; no verse is Gāyatrī. The devatā is given only as Saṃjñāna, but verse 1 ('saṃ-sam id yuvase vṛṣann agne') is to Agni; the repo's complete Rigveda titles the hymn 'Agni'.
(2) The landing page advertises the complete Rigveda as 'the whole Rigveda, not a selection — all 1,028 sūktas and 10,143 mantras'. The curated reader and fullbleed intro (hymns.json:7) say the Rigveda has 10,552 verses, which is the standard count. The landing's per-mandala table (I 1,979, II 430, III 619, IV 588, V 725, VI 766, VII 843, VIII 1,331, IX 1,108, X 1,754) differs from the standard (2,006 / 429 / 617 / 589 / 727 / 765 / 841 / 1,716 / 1,108 / 1,754) in eight mandalas and is 409 verses short in total. That is 385 in Mandala 8 (the empty sūktas already reported) and 27 in Mandala 1, which is not covered by that report. The completeness claim should not stand alongside the site's own 10,552.
gap.evidence: hymns.json lines above; the 10.191 verse text is in the same seed. Counted mantras per mandala in seeds/rigveda-complete.json (10,143 total, matching the index table); the standard per-mandala totals sum to 10,552. Spot-checked 39 well-known sūkta lengths: only 1.139 differs (12 vs 11).
gap.repro: Open /vedas/index.html and read the complete-Rigveda card and the mandala grid; then open /vedas/reader.html and read the intro (10,552) and the Samjnana header.
gap.fix: Set 10.191 to 'Anuṣṭubh; v.3 Triṣṭubh' and 'Agni (v.1), Saṃjñāna (2–4)'. On the landing page, say '10,143 of the 10,552 mantras', or fix the source gaps before claiming completeness.

gap.title: Six formats ignore same-document hash navigation (pasting a shared link into an open tab, or Back/Forward between such entries); the address bar then names a place that isn't shown
gap.detail:
These pages read the hash only once at load and have no hashchange or popstate listener:
- alice fullbleed (#p-N)
- meditations fullbleed (#p-N)
- prophet fullbleed (#p-N), pdf-reader (#p-N), mobile (#ch-N) and theater (#ch-N)

When only the fragment differs, the browser does a same-document navigation and the page does not move. This happens when a reader opens a bookmark or shared link to the same page in a tab where it is already open, or uses Back/Forward across such entries. The URL then names a different page from the one shown, so bookmarking or sharing at that moment saves the wrong place, until the next page turn overwrites the hash. Their sibling formats in the same books (alice theater, khayyam fullbleed/mobile/pdf/theater, meditations mobile/pdf/theater) react correctly.

Separately, every reader.html sidebar/TOC link calls preventDefault + replaceState, following AGENT_README's 'replaceState without adding history entries'. So a TOC jump adds no history entry, and Back after a mistaken jump leaves the book entirely instead of returning to where the reader was.
gap.evidence:
hash.js: set location.hash, then compared with a fresh load of the same URL:
- alice fullbleed #p-5 -> #p-40: counter stays '5' (a fresh load shows 41)
- meditations fullbleed #p-5 -> #p-60: stays 5 (fresh 61)
- prophet fullbleed: stays 5 (fresh 41)
- prophet pdf-reader #p-5 -> #p-60: text unchanged ('Fain would I take with') vs fresh 'Would that I could be'
- prophet mobile #ch-2 -> #ch-20: still 'When love beckons…'
- prophet theater: still 'ON LOVE | 2 / 28' vs fresh 'ON TALKING | 20 / 28'
- controls: alice theater, khayyam fullbleed/mobile/theater/pdf and meditations mobile/theater/pdf follow the new hash.

back.js: after two sidebar clicks in alice, meditations, casaubon, prophet, khayyam and vedas reader.html, history.length stayed 3, and goBack went to index.html.
gap.repro:
1. Open gibran-prophet/theater.html#ch-2.
2. In the same tab, edit the address to #ch-20 (or open a shared #ch-20 link there) and press Enter. The chapter stays 'On Love' while the URL says ch-20.
3. Press Back: the URL changes, the content doesn't.
gap.fix: Add window.addEventListener('hashchange', () => restoreFromHash()), reusing each page's load-time parser (the lines listed), to the six pages, as the sibling formats already do. For explicit TOC jumps, consider history.pushState instead of replaceState so Back undoes a jump. Keep replaceState for scroll-driven position updates, and note the distinction in AGENT_README.md:143.
verifier_corrections: The scope is wider than 'six formats'. The same defect, with no hashchange listener and verified STAY in the browser, also affects vedas/fullbleed.html:698 (spreadFromHash), vedas/reader.html:953, vedas/rigveda.html:523 (parseHash), homer-iliad/{fullbleed.html:272, mobile.html:294, pdf-reader.html:257, theater.html:292} and homer-odyssey/{fullbleed.html:275, mobile.html:298, pdf-reader.html:260, theater.html:295, study.html:428}. That makes 17 pages, not 6. The claim that Vedas' siblings react correctly holds only for mobile/pdf/theater, not for fullbleed/reader/rigveda. Repro step 3 is slightly off: after Back, the URL returns to #ch-2, which matches the unchanged content again; the mismatch returns on Forward. The TOC/replaceState part follows the documented AGENT_README convention and should be framed as a proposed convention change, not a bug. Aside, not assessed and possibly a sandbox artifact of document.fonts.ready waiting on blocked Google Fonts: a fresh load of gibran-prophet/reader.html#ch-20 stayed on ch-1 (scrollY 308) even after 5.5s.

gap.title: Alice reader: while fonts are slow, the #ch-N restore freezes the URL position, then jumps the reader back to the linked chapter once fonts settle
gap.detail: restoreHash() (added by the previous audit's fix for the ch-1 race) captures the target and sets restoringHash=true (line 1862). That stops the chapter observer from writing the hash (line 1965). The actual scroll is deferred to `document.fonts.ready.then(() => setTimeout(go, 50))` (line 2006), with no timeout and no check that the reader has moved. When fonts are slow, the browser's own fragment jump already puts the reader on chapter N, and they start reading. Meanwhile the URL stays #ch-N, so reloading or sharing loses their progress. When fonts finally settle, go() scrolls back to the top of chapter N, discarding everything they read since. The fix pattern already exists in this repo. Meditations reader aborts the late re-apply once the user has moved (hashUserMoved, aurelius-meditations/reader.html:7890-7909). Khayyam reader races a 400 ms timer. Both were verified: no jump. gibran-prophet/reader.html:2012-2024 has the same unbounded fonts.ready deferral. Its restore problem is already reported ('lands on chapter 1'), but with a late fonts.ready it also snaps the reader to the top of whatever chapter is in view. Any fix for that finding should bring the guard and timeout too, not copy Alice's version.
gap.evidence: 1440x900, /alice-in-wonderland/reader.html#ch-5, font files held 30 s. At t=4 s: scrollY 24902, chapter 5, hash #ch-5. The reader wheels on to chapter 7 (scrollY 45902, t=12.5 s) and the hash stays #ch-5. At t=33.5 s: scrollY 24846, chapter 5, a jump back of about 21,000 px. At 390x844 with only 6 wheel steps: 42882 back to 38626. With a font that merely arrives after 4 s (real TTF served, slow-3G-like), the jump still happens: at 390x844, 44682 back to 37608 (7,074 px); at 1440, 30902 back to 24178. Prophet reader, #ch-10 at 1440 with a 30 s hang: scrollY 42125 in chapter 23 goes to 41995; at 390 with a 4 s font delay, 32208 goes to 28817 (top of chapter 12). The Meditations reader under the same test stayed at 67088 (no jump). Khayyam's hash kept tracking (#chg-fifth-7) with no jump. Logs: scratchpad/work/gap-fonts/g-alice-rd-d-far.txt, g-alice-rd-m.txt, g-prophet-rd-d-far.txt, g-med-rd-m.txt, g-kh-rd-m.txt; slowyank.js output above.
gap.repro: Hold fonts.gstatic.com requests for 30 s (or 4 s). Open /alice-in-wonderland/reader.html#ch-5 and scroll down a few screens, into chapter 6 or 7. The address bar keeps #ch-5. When the font requests end, the page jumps back to the start of chapter 5.
gap.fix: In restoreHash(): record user movement (`['wheel','touchstart','keydown','mousedown'].forEach(ev => addEventListener(ev, () => moved = true, {once:true, passive:true}))`). Bound the wait: `Promise.race([document.fonts.ready, new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 1000))]).then(() => setTimeout(go, 50))`. In go(), `if (moved) { restoringHash = false; return; }`. Clear restoringHash on the timeout path as well, so the URL starts tracking again. Apply the same guard and timeout in the prophet reader's restoreHash.
verifier_corrections: Line range is fine: restoreHash spans 1992-2011, and it is called at 2118. The Prophet effect is a snap to the top of the chapter currently in view, usually a few hundred px, not a return to the linked chapter. Severity low rather than medium, given the narrow trigger.

The Prophet part is only a snap to the top of the current chapter, not a lost URL position. Its hash keeps updating during the deferral. It deserves a line inside the Prophet restore finding, not equal weight here.

gap.title: OS dark mode is ignored by every book page; nine pages also save the light default on first load
gap.detail: Only the root catalog reads prefers-color-scheme (index.html:235-241, added by the previous audit's P1). Every book page hard-codes `<html data-theme="light-purple">` (or sepia) and uses it whenever there are no saved prefs. A dark-mode visitor leaves a dark catalog and lands on bright cream book pages: every landing page, all 8 reader.html, 5 of 7 mobile.html, the pdf-reader page cards and the non-Homer fullbleeds. Because prefs are per {book}-{format}, getting dark reading everywhere means picking a dark theme separately in up to ~45 formats. Neither AGENT_README (Theme System names light-purple as the fixed default) nor any CLAUDE.md sets an expectation either way. Adoption is simple on most pages: they save prefs only after a user action, so `theme = prefs.theme || (matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)').matches ? 'dark-violet' : 'light-purple')` keeps the saved choice first. Nine pages write the default theme to localStorage on first load with no user action (prophet-mobile-prefs; iliad-fullbleed, iliad-mobile and iliad-pdf-prefs; odyssey-fullbleed, odyssey-mobile, odyssey-pdf and odyssey-illustrated-prefs; vedas-rigveda-prefs). Anyone who ever opened them now has 'light-purple' saved as if they had chosen it, so those pages must stop persisting defaults before they can honour the OS setting.
gap.evidence: dark.js, 1440x900, empty storage, colorScheme dark vs light: 50/51 pages produce identical screenshots. Mode luminance under OS dark: catalog 9. Book landing pages, reader.html and mobile.html 225–248. pdf-reader viewers 81–193 with white cards. Only the 7 theaters and 2 Homer fullbleeds are dark (9–24), by design. lsdump.js: after load with no interaction, prophet-mobile-prefs={"theme":"light-purple"}, iliad-fullbleed-prefs={"book":0,"edition":"pope","theme":"light-purple"}, vedas-rigveda-prefs={"theme":"light-purple",…}, etc.
gap.repro: Set the OS to dark mode and clear site data. Open https://lib.sadh.app/ (dark), then open any book (e.g. aurelius-meditations/index.html, then reader.html): both are light-purple. Check localStorage after only opening vedas/rigveda.html: vedas-rigveda-prefs already contains theme light-purple.
gap.fix: In each template's early head script, when no saved theme exists, pick dark-violet under prefers-color-scheme: dark (and light-purple otherwise) before first paint. Only call savePrefs() from user actions (gibran-prophet/mobile.html:409, vedas/rigveda.html:317, the Homer build templates' save-on-render at homer-iliad/fullbleed.html:177 etc.). Document the rule under AGENT_README 'Theme System': a saved pref wins, otherwise follow the OS.
verifier_corrections: All 7 mobile.html pages default to light, not '5 of 7'. Severity should be low: this is design consistency with the catalog, AGENT_README documents light-purple as the default, and the old audit deliberately scoped the OS-following fix to the catalog. Seen in passing, separate from this finding: the Homer prefs written on load carry reading position ('book':0, and 'page':0 for odyssey-illustrated). That breaks the AGENT_README rule that a prefs object never carries a chapter/page. Homer is still under active development.

Severity should be low, not medium. There is no documented convention to follow the OS on book pages, and the prior audit deliberately limited this to the catalog. The saved-default half is latent (no current visible effect). The Homer theaters also write iliad/odyssey-theater-book and -edition keys on load, which is outside this finding.
